title: Force garbage collection at end of each slot
idea: Trigger an explicit garbage collection or memory release at the end of each slot, when the node is idle, to bound memory growth between slots. Check whether Lighthouse runs any per-slot memory release (for example malloc_trim or a jemalloc purge) from its slot timer.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:36-38 Linux builds enable tikv-jemallocator feature background_threads

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/build.rs:221-228 and :457 that feature compiles background_thread:true into malloc_conf

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/include/jemalloc/internal/arena_types.h:7-8 dirty_decay_ms 10s, muzzy_decay_ms 0
common/malloc_utils/src/glibc.rs:14-20 fixed 128KB mmap threshold to keep glibc heap small
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7471 per_slot_task has no explicit release
gap: No explicit slot-aligned release. Jemalloc background threads already purge dirty pages on a ~10s decay (about one slot), so memory is returned between slots asynchronously. Only an explicit arena purge (arena.<MALLCTL_ARENAS_ALL>.purge) or malloc_trim(0) for sysmalloc builds from per_slot_task is missing.
impact: Small for default jemalloc builds, because the background purge already does time-based release; could help sysmalloc/glibc builds and reproducible builds that link Debian libjemalloc without the compiled conf.
refute_note: The earlier review missed that Linux builds turn on jemalloc background purge threads via the tikv-jemallocator background_threads feature, which is a time-based equivalent of per-slot release. I confirmed no malloc_trim, mallctl purge or prof call anywhere in the workspace sources.

title: Use SHA-NI accelerated sha256 implementation
idea: Use a sha256 implementation that dispatches to CPU SHA extensions (SHA-NI/ARMv8 crypto) for tree hashing and pool its buffers. Check that the sha256 crate used by Lighthouse's tree hashing detects and uses SHA instructions at runtime.
measured_best: gave a nice boost on Celeron, not benchmarked (pr:caplin#7060)
evidence: ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:111-137 cpufeatures runtime detection of x86 SHA extensions, selects sha2 asm path
ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/Cargo.toml:31 default features include ring (ARMv8 crypto path); Cargo.toml:153 uses default features

title: Benchmark mimalloc or tcmalloc as global allocator
idea: Allow selecting an alternative global allocator (mimalloc, tcmalloc) and benchmark it against jemalloc on state transition runtime and RSS. Check whether Lighthouse has a build feature for mimalloc and what the benchmarks showed.
measured_best: mimalloc 13,120 ms vs jemalloc 22,559 ms vs glibc 17,471 ms, but RSS 45.4 MiB vs 23.0 MiB (pr:lighthouse#10046)
evidence: common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:14-26 only jemalloc and sysmalloc features
Cargo.lock has no mimalloc crate; grep for mimalloc/tcmalloc across the tree finds nothing
lighthouse/Cargo.toml:80 malloc_utils with jemalloc
gap: Add a mimalloc feature to malloc_utils (GlobalAlloc in lib.rs) and benchmark. The measured result (state transition 13.1 s vs 22.6 s jemalloc) is attractive but RSS doubles (45 vs 23 MiB), and the PRs were not adopted.
impact: Possibly ~40% faster state-transition-heavy workloads but about 2x RSS; unclear net win on a mainnet node, and jemalloc stats/profiling metrics would be lost.

title: Low-allocation hex encoding of roots and pubkeys
idea: Convert 32-byte roots and 48-byte pubkeys to hex with a specialised helper that writes into a reusable buffer or lookup table instead of string concatenation or per-call allocation, and use it everywhere roots are stringified (gossip, fork choice, cache keys). Check whether Lighthouse formats roots to hex strings on hot paths, for example as map keys or in logs that are always evaluated.
measured_best: toRootHex 156 ns to 105 ns; GC time ~2.9% to <2.3% (pr:lodestar#7060, pr:lodestar#7036)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/topics.rs:374 hex::encode only for fork digest topic names
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1313 hex only in a log path
Hot-path maps key on Hash256 (fixed bytes), not strings
gap: Lighthouse keys caches and fork choice on Hash256/PublicKeyBytes byte arrays and formats hex only at logging/API edges (tracing fields are lazy), so there is no hot-path stringification to optimise.
impact: Little to gain; hex formatting is off the hot path.

title: Serialize arena-backed proving on one thread
idea: When a prover uses a per-thread arena whose slabs are never released, run all proofs on one long-lived thread or behind a one-at-a-time permit, so only one proof-peak slab is pinned. Check whether Lighthouse runs any arena-allocating crypto job on arbitrary pool threads.
measured_best: OOM about every 40 min (~29 GB RSS) fixed; slab count stays 10 vs 10 to 14 before (pr:ethlambda#641)
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/rust_eth_kzg-0.9.1: no thread_local arena or bump allocator in the source
Cargo.lock kzg stack: c-kzg, rust_eth_kzg, blst; no proving arena is used
gap: Lighthouse does not run a prover with a per-thread arena that never releases slabs; KZG/blob verification and cell recovery allocate through the global jemalloc.
impact: None.

title: Jemalloc heap profiling over HTTP endpoint
idea: Expose jemalloc heap profiling through an HTTP debug endpoint so memory growth can be diagnosed on running nodes. Check whether Lighthouse can dump jemalloc heap profiles at runtime.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:20 jemalloc-profiling = tikv-jemallocator/profiling
lighthouse/Cargo.toml:40-41 forwards the feature

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/src/ctl.c:140-145,194 prof options exist in the bundled jemalloc
gap: Profiling needs a custom build plus a restart with _RJEM_MALLOC_CONF, and dumps go only to files. There is no HTTP route (http_api or http_metrics) that toggles prof.active or calls prof.dump and returns the profile.
impact: Diagnostic only: lets operators debug memory growth on a running node without a restart; no direct resource saving.
refute_note: I searched the whole workspace for mallctl, prof.dump, prof.active, pprof and tikv_jemalloc_ctl. The only user is the stats scrape in jemalloc.rs, and http_api has no allocator route. The env-var interval dump is the only runtime path.

title: Tune jemalloc decay and background purging
idea: Configure jemalloc with background purge threads and shorter dirty/muzzy decay times so freed pages return to the OS and RSS stays lower. Check Lighthouse's jemalloc config string for background_thread and decay settings.

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/include/jemalloc/internal/arena_types.h:7-8 defaults dirty_decay_ms 10000, muzzy_decay_ms 0

gap: Background purge threads are already on in the normal Linux and Docker builds, and muzzy decay is already 0. What is missing: an explicit dirty_decay_ms setting (left at the 10s default), and the reproducible JEMALLOC_OVERRIDE builds, which link Debian's libjemalloc and lose both background_thread and narenas:16.

refute_note: The earlier review misread build.rs: always_enabled comes from CARGO_FEATURE_BACKGROUND_THREADS, which malloc_utils turns on for Linux, so background_thread:true is compiled in. I also checked the jemalloc 5.3 decay defaults and the reproducible override path.

idea: Hash with one-shot functions on stack buffers or a pooled reusable hasher instead of allocating a hasher object per call in tree hashing. Check whether Lighthouse's hash32_concat and tree-hash paths allocate a Vec or hasher per hash.

DynamicImpl::best() picks sha2 (SHA-NI) or ring at runtime

idea: Benchmark runtime or toolchain upgrades before rollout and pin the version when a new release regresses performance. Check whether Lighthouse pins its Rust toolchain and benchmarks compiler upgrades.

idea: Reuse snappy stream reader/writer objects (each with ~142 KB scratch buffers) from a pool instead of creating one per response chunk or message. Check whether Lighthouse rpc codec creates a new snappy FrameEncoder/Decoder per chunk.

title: Remove needless iterator-to-vector collections
idea: Do not convert iterators or views into owned vectors in hot paths and REST/sync code when they are only iterated. Check Lighthouse for collect::<Vec<_>>() followed by a single iteration.

title: Use cached committees for attesting indices
idea: Resolve attesting indices in gossip verification, the op pool, fork choice vote updates and duties from a per-epoch committee/shuffling cache instead of recomputing the shuffling from a BeaconState per attestation. The shuffling is fixed for the epoch, so one computation serves every attestation.
measured_best: 95% reduction in attestation processing time (best case) (pr:lighthouse#841)

title: Shuffling cache keyed by epoch and dependent root
idea: Key the committee/shuffling cache (and per-committee aggregate pubkeys) by (target epoch, shuffling decision/dependent root) so entries are correct across forks and shared by attestation verification, block production and API. Compute each shuffling once (at epoch transition or slot tick, deduplicating concurrent computations) so attestation committees come from the cache without recomputing the shuffling or needing a full state.
measured_best: single verify ~+100ns of ~70us; batch same or cheaper (pr:silver#329)

title: Compute committee length without building committee
idea: When only a committee's size is needed (attestation validation, attesting info), compute it arithmetically from the cached active validator count instead of shuffling and materialising the committee. Avoids the shuffle and the allocation.

title: Same-message signature check for equal-data attestations
idea: Group unaggregated gossip attestations by (slot, attestation data root), aggregate the pubkeys and signatures of each group and do one signature check per group, falling back to per-attestation verification on failure. Verification cost scales with distinct data, not message count.
measured_best: 128 sigs: 130.5 ms vs 8.97 ms; CPU 140-160% vs >=300% (pr:lodestar#5729)
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36 verify_signature_sets builds one (msg, agg_pk, sig, rand) tuple per set, no grouping by message
blst-0.3.17/src/lib.rs:1335 verify_multiple_aggregate_signatures has '// TODO - check msg uniqueness?' and runs mul_n_aggregate (hash-to-curve + Miller loop) per element
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification/batch.rs:170 one signature set per unaggregated attestation
gap: Group the partially verified unaggregated attestations in batch_verify_unaggregated_attestations by signing root, aggregate pubkeys and signatures per group into one SignatureSet (or merge equal messages inside verify_signature_sets), keep the existing per-attestation fallback via from_indexed with CheckAttestationSignature::Yes.
impact: Pairing work for gossip unaggregated batches (up to 64) drops from one hash-to-curve + Miller loop per attestation to one per distinct data; several-fold less BLS CPU on subscribed subnets.
refute_note: Checked the blst 0.3.17 crate itself for message dedup in the multi-verify path: none, only a TODO. No grouping in batch.rs or the beacon processor.

title: Validate same-data attestations as one group
idea: When draining queued or API-submitted attestations, group by attestation data, run the shared data checks, target state lookup and signing root once per group, and batch-verify the signatures, verifying individually only if the batch fails.
measured_best: processing 100 attestations could take up to 10s; per-attestation 50-100ms before (pr:prysm#15801)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification/batch.rs:133 gossip unaggregated attestations are batch BLS verified with per-attestation fallback when the batch fails

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1617 map_attestation_committees takes committees from shuffling_cache via with_committee_cache, so the target-state/committee lookup happens once per shuffling, not per attestation
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:106 CacheItem::Promise coalesces concurrent misses so only one state load runs for many attestations of the same target
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification/batch.rs:146 IndexedUnaggregatedAttestation::verify still runs per attestation (head block, slot range, signing root)
gap: The expensive parts of the idea (target state lookup once, batch signature verify with individual fallback) exist for gossip. Missing: bucketing by AttestationData so the head-block/target checks and signing-root hashing run once per bucket, and using the batch path for API submissions (see 009).
impact: Small: remaining per-attestation work is a fork choice read lock, a committee cache hit and one signing-root hash (microseconds); the 50-100ms per-attestation cost the source PR fixed is state lookup, which the shuffling cache already avoids.
refute_note: Earlier review missed that the shuffling cache (with promise-based miss coalescing) already gives the once-per-target state/committee lookup, and that gossip already batch-verifies with fallback.

title: Aggregate attestations in pool before fork choice
idea: Save gossip and API attestations straight into the fork-choice pool and aggregate equal-data ones there before applying them to fork choice, instead of a periodic batching step with many separate on-attestation calls.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2573 apply_attestation_to_fork_choice takes the fork choice write lock and calls on_attestation per verified attestation
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_attestations.rs:100 API path applies each attestation to fork choice, then to the naive aggregation pool
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2596 naive aggregation pool is separate and feeds aggregate production, not fork choice
gap: No aggregation of equal-data attestations before fork choice. Lighthouse has no periodic batching step to replace (it applies immediately), and on_attestation is a per-validator latest-message update, so aggregating first would only save write-lock acquisitions.
impact: Negligible: per-validator vote work is the same with or without pre-aggregation; only lock acquisitions are saved.
refute_note: Looked for any queue that aggregates before on_attestation (fork choice queued_attestations, naive aggregation pool); neither feeds aggregated votes into fork choice.

title: Batch-verify API-submitted attestations
idea: Hand attestations submitted through the validator HTTP API to the verifier as one batch so their signatures are batch verified rather than one by one.

beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_attestations.rs:76 verify_and_publish_attestation calls verify_unaggregated_attestation_for_gossip (single signature check)

gap: In publish_attestations, call chain.batch_verify_unaggregated_attestations_for_gossip over the request's SingleAttestations, then publish/apply each verified result; keep the UnknownHeadBlock reprocess path for individual failures.
impact: Only for nodes serving many local validators: roughly halves BLS cost of their POSTed attestations (more with 006); nothing for ordinary nodes.

title: Batch-verify reprocessed pending attestations
idea: When releasing queued attestations (e.g. after their block is imported), verify their signatures as one batch instead of one by one, and requeue future-slot or missing-target ones directly rather than reprocessing them.
measured_best: attestation processing was 23% of profile (pr:lodestar#2754)

title: Compute block attestations' target state once
idea: Process a block's attestations in order (sorted by slot, sequentially) so the first one loads or computes the needed target checkpoint state and blocks, and the rest reuse it. This avoids concurrent or per-attestation reads and regenerations of the same state.
measured_best: "reduce time in processing a block" (no numbers) (pr:prysm#2370)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/consensus_context.rs:161 get_indexed_attestation uses the one block pre-state and its committee caches, memoised by attestation root
gossip_methods.rs:2827 area: gossip attestations use shared shuffling/committee cache via chain.with_committee_cache (attestation_verification.rs:1076)

title: Process attestations and update head once per slot
idea: Apply pending attestations to fork choice and recompute head once per slot instead of both on tick and on proposal.
evidence: consensus/fork_choice/src/fork_choice.rs:1386 attestations of current slot queued; fork_choice.rs:1580 process_attestation_queue dequeues in bulk on update_time

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:207 recompute on block import
gap: Attestation application is batched per slot via the queue, but head is recomputed at the pre-slot timer, at slot start and on each block import, i.e. not once per slot. Could drop the per_slot_task recompute when state_advance_timer already ran for that slot.
impact: Saves one get_head (proto-array apply_score_changes over all votes) per slot, likely a few ms of the fork choice write lock; small.

title: Verify aggregates before unaggregated attestations
idea: In the attestation verification queue, prioritise aggregate-and-proof messages over unaggregated attestations so limited verification CPU goes to the more valuable, time-critical messages first.

title: Keep gossip aggregates out of fork choice
idea: Store gossip aggregate-and-proof attestations only in the op pool for block inclusion and do not apply them to fork choice, since their votes arrive anyway via unaggregated attestations and blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:631 process_gossip_aggregate_result calls chain.apply_attestation_to_fork_choice(&verified_aggregate)

Would skip the apply_attestation_to_fork_choice call in process_gossip_aggregate_result (keep op pool insert), accepting reliance on unaggregates and blocks.
impact: Removes a write-lock acquisition plus ~hundreds of vote updates per aggregate (about 100 aggregates/slot after dedup), so less fork choice lock contention; modest CPU saving. Risk: slightly later vote visibility for validators on few subnets.

title: Field-wise attestation data equality
idea: Compare AttestationData with a direct field-by-field equality instead of serialising or hash-tree-rooting both sides, removing allocations on the duplicate-detection hot path.

title: Allocation-free attesting indices computation
idea: Compute attesting indices/participants without intermediate vectors or sequences (preallocate, write directly) so per-attestation work in block and epoch processing does not allocate.
measured_best: 15% to 1% of block_sim at 100k validators (pr:nimbus#1351)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attesting_indices.rs:30 base version preallocates Vec::with_capacity(num_set_bits)

Rewrite attesting_indices_electra::get_attesting_indices to size the output from aggregation_bits.num_set_bits(), push directly, iterate committee_bits without collecting, and drop the HashSet.

title: Iterate only set bits of aggregation bitfield
idea: Derive attesting indices by iterating the set bits of the aggregation bitfield directly (word-level scan) rather than testing every bit position.

impact: Cuts per-attestation index derivation, used in block processing and fork choice; sparse aggregates benefit most. Small overall.

title: Avoid sorting attesting indices
idea: Build attesting indices by walking the committee in aggregation-bit order and skip or minimise the generic sort, and skip sorting entirely where the spec does not need ordering. This removes the sort cost and allocation per attestation.
measured_best: 8% faster overall on ncli_db bench first 100k slots; ~12% on apply block (1.67ms to 1.47ms) (pr:nimbus#2274)
evidence: get_attesting_indices.rs:41 and :149 still call sort_unstable after collecting (electra path also via HashSet)
committees are walked in order so output is already ascending in a single committee only if the committee is sorted, which it is not (shuffled)
gap: Output ordering needed by IndexedAttestation requires sorted indices, and committee order is shuffled order, so the sort cannot be dropped in the indexed path; only callers needing just counts or a set (e.g. fork choice, rewards) could skip it. Add an unsorted variant and use it there.
impact: Minor: saves a sort of up to a few hundred u64 per attestation on non-indexed callers.

title: Verify single attestations in native form
idea: Receive and verify unaggregated SingleAttestation gossip messages in their native form and convert to a full attestation only after verification, removing a separate conversion work event.

title: Fetch target checkpoint state asynchronously
idea: Retrieve the attestation target checkpoint state asynchronously (cache hit or regeneration off the processing thread) instead of a blocking store lookup, so attestation processing threads are not blocked by state loading.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5211 import_block_update_shuffling_cache_fallible primes current and next epoch shufflings at block import

title: Cache checkpoint states by target checkpoint
idea: Keep an in-memory checkpoint-state cache keyed by target checkpoint, fill it with the state regenerated on a miss, and use it for attestation verification. Many attestations to the same target then share one state regeneration instead of a database load or regen each.

idea: When the attestation's target epoch committees are already determined in the head (or another in-memory) state, i.e. the shuffling dependent root matches, verify it against that state and its committee cache, also for previous- and next-epoch targets. This avoids loading, regenerating or advancing the exact target checkpoint state.

idea: On a shuffling cache miss, load the attestation's target (epoch-boundary) state to compute committees instead of the block-root state, avoiding replay of blocks and skip slots to a mid-epoch state.

title: Reject finalized or old-target attestations before state load
idea: Before loading or regenerating any state or verifying signatures, cheaply reject attestations whose target or slot is at or before finalization (or not descended from finalized), so stale attestations never trigger multi-epoch block replays.

title: Reject far-future target epochs by clock

title: Check target block in fork choice before work
idea: Before processing a queued attestation, check that its target/beacon block is known to fork choice and skip work that is certain to fail.

impact: Already drops duplicate/subset aggregates before verification and rebroadcast.

title: Park unknown-root attestations from raw bytes
idea: Extract slot and block root from the serialized attestation bytes first and park unknown-root attestations in a bounded map for reprocessing on block arrival, instead of fully deserialising and validating them first.
measured_best: up to 16,000 attestations reprocessed at once previously (pr:lodestar#5327)

idea: Cache the block, attestation data and checkpoints for a block about to become head so attestations can be produced (and blocks served) before DB import or the head state update completes.

idea: When producing attestations for many validators, compute the committee/attestation schedule once per epoch and slot and reuse it instead of recomputing per validator.

idea: Gate attestation pre-state regeneration behind a semaphore (limit one) so attestations for different old targets do not each regenerate a state in parallel, and abort early when the request context is cancelled.

title: Avoid coarse locks around attestation state work

title: Lightweight non-SSZ indexed attestation on hot paths

measured_best: Allocations in 50s window 15.56 GB to 12.97 GB (-16.6%); getIndexedAttestation 472 MB to 17 MB (-96.4%); ~52 MB/s less garbage (pr:teku#10599)

title: Serve duty queries from epoch caches, not loaded states

Use compressed pubkey bytes in duty responses so cloning and hashing are cheap.
measured_best: Pyrmont: proposer duties 450ms peaks to <1ms; attester duties >1s to 20-30ms (pr:lighthouse#2243)

title: Compute duties for all validators in one committee pass
idea: When a duties request names many validators, iterate the target epoch's committees once while looking up members in a validator-index set or map, instead of searching the committees separately for each validator. This turns O(validators x committees) work into a single pass.
measured_best: 3.35s to 1.29-1.65s per batch (about 2-2.6x) (pr:lodestar#2717)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:61-69 cached path calls chain.validator_attestation_duties for the whole index batch

title: Query EL first, request only remaining blobs from peers
idea: When blobs or columns for a block are missing, query the local EL first and send RPC requests to peers only for the ones still missing. Share one received-sidecar set between the EL and the p2p fetch paths so no sidecar is fetched twice.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:970-991 custody_lookup_request filters sampling columns by cached_data_column_indexes (gossip and EL-imported columns are skipped)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:209-222 lookup block with MissingComponents triggers fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full

gap: The subtraction the earlier review asked for already exists: lookups skip columns already in the DA cache, and RPC lookup blocks trigger getBlobs. What is missing is ordering and in-flight sharing: the lookup custody request starts on block download, in parallel with (and before) the EL fetch that runs only after block processing, and ActiveCustodyRequest does not re-check the DA cache to drop columns the EL fills while requests are in flight. impact: Fewer redundant column RPC bytes and KZG verifications during unknown-block lookups when the EL holds the blobs; small on mainnet where gossip usually wins.

refute_note: Re-read import_block end to end, the post-DB-write tail, and every recompute_head_at_* caller in beacon_chain, network and http_api; no caller sets cached_head inside import_block or before the DB write, so the earlier partial verdict stands.

title: Import block once half of columns are available
idea: Treat a PeerDAS block as available, and import it, as soon as about 50% of data columns are accepted, since the rest can be reconstructed; complete the remaining columns in the background instead of waiting for all custody columns. This cuts import latency on supernodes.

refute_note: Read make_available and check_and_set_reconstruction_started directly; there is no availability shortcut under another name. The only early step is that reconstruction is triggered at half.
