idea: In gossip verification compute the block root from the signed block header built with the body root, instead of hashing the full block again.
measured_best: ~10ms average block root on mainnet; header should take microseconds (pr:lighthouse#5003)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:890 get_block_header_root(&header) used in gossip verification
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1975 get_block_header_root
impact: Nothing; already done (PR 5003 still in place).

title: Skip indexed attestation build for trusted signatures
idea: When replaying blocks with already-verified signatures, skip building indexed attestations and copying pubkeys used only for signature verification.
measured_best: removes is_valid_indexed_attestation from performance benchmarks when replaying blocks (commit:nimbus@5ca10d3de263)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/is_valid_indexed_attestation.rs:50 signature set and pubkey lookup only when verify_signatures is true

consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_attestation.rs:92 indexed attestation built once, cached in ConsensusContext, and needed anyway for participation updates (process_operations.rs:250)
gap: Only a small leftover: is_valid_indexed_attestation still allocates attesting_indices_to_vec and does the sort check when signatures are already verified.
impact: Pubkey work is already skipped; leftover is a tiny Vec alloc per attestation, negligible on a mainnet node.

title: Do not re-verify already verified block signature
idea: Skip re-verifying the proposer or builder signature in block/envelope processing when gossip validation already verified it, avoiding an extra BLS check and full block hash.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/execution_pending_envelope.rs:83 envelope processed with VerifySignatures::False, comment says gossip already verified
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1285 include_all_signatures_except_proposal skips the proposal signature
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:12 module docs: do not re-verify proposal signature or re-hash
impact: Already avoids the second proposer/builder BLS check and block re-hash on gossip path. Range-sync envelopes still verify (import.rs:436), which is needed since they were not gossip-verified.

title: Skip state rewind when parent state is current
idea: When the block's parent state is already the in-memory state, apply the block directly without rewinding and replaying, saving state hash_tree_root calls.
measured_best: saves 4 hash_tree_roots per state; hash_tree_root was ~45-50% of node time (pr:nimbus#919)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2057-2090 load_parent takes a cloned state advanced to block slot via get_advanced_hot_state
no rewind/replay machinery in the import path
impact: Lighthouse never rewinds a head state to the parent; it loads the parent's (pre-advanced) state from the state cache, so there is nothing to skip.

title: Wait for gossip sidecars only for recent slots
idea: Block on gossip sidecar arrival only for current or next-slot blocks; for older blocks read sidecars from storage or fetch by root immediately instead of waiting a slot.
measured_best: 12s per queued slot wait removed; fetch took ~0.9s (pr:prysm#17429)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:139 MissingComponents returns instead of blocking
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:64,794 envelope queue delay is a timer-based reprocess entry, not a blocking wait
impact: Lighthouse has no blocking wait on sidecar notifier: blocks/envelopes park in the availability cache and complete when columns arrive; missing columns trigger sync lookups. The Prysm 12s stall does not exist by design.

title: Bound reprocess queue capacity
idea: Cap the reprocessing queue and its channel below the main work channel capacity so late blocks and attestations cannot build unbounded work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:91 DEFAULT_MAX_SCHEDULED_WORK_QUEUE_LEN = 3/4 of main queue len
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:770-773 both reprocess channels use max_scheduled_work_queue_len
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:78-90 per-kind caps (16 blocks, 16384 attestations)
impact: Reprocess channels bounded at 75% of the work channel, plus per-type caps, as in lighthouse#3239.

title: Validate block outside the fork choice lock
idea: Run state transition, payload execution and signature checks before taking the fork-choice write lock, and hold the lock only to insert the block, so the lock is held briefly and forks process in parallel.
measured_best: replay 0.25-0.35 s on Hoodi under the lock (avoided) (pr:caplin#25332)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1498 state transition, newPayload and signature checks run under only a fork choice read lock
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4510-4516 import_block upgrades to the write lock for on_block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4752-4767 write lock is held across the DB write and dropped after it (comment: 'at the expense of concurrency')
gap: Verification is already outside the write lock. What is missing is to release the write lock after on_block and before the block/state DB write; this needs another way to keep fork choice and the DB consistent (see handle_import_block_db_write_error).
impact: Fork choice readers (attestation and gossip verification, head queries) stop blocking during the block and state DB write, a few to tens of ms per block, more for epoch-boundary states.
refute_note: Confirmed in the source that the write-lock guard is dropped only after do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache, and that the code comment says this is deliberate; the write is synchronous, not deferred.

title: Checkpoint sync from unfinalized state
idea: Allow checkpoint sync from a recent unfinalized state by treating it as the fork choice anchor, so a node can start and attest during long non-finality.
measured_best: node catches up and attests immediately from a 6-epoch-old unfinalized checkpoint (pr:prysm#17559)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:169-174 anchor epoch/root used as both justified and finalized regardless of the state's real finality
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:406-435 weak_subjectivity_state accepts any state and advances it to an epoch boundary, no finality check
beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:437-441 checkpoint-sync-url hardcodes StateId::Finalized
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1241-1258 --checkpoint-state/--checkpoint-block accept a manual state (the only route to an unfinalized anchor)

consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:2165-2167 viability filter needs voting_source.epoch == store justified (= anchor) or within 2 epochs of current; no clamp of descendant checkpoints to the anchor
gap: The fake-finalized anchor exists (manual --checkpoint-state), but under long non-finality descendants of the anchor carry a real justified checkpoint older than the anchor epoch, so node_is_viable_for_head rejects them and the head sticks at the anchor until the chain justifies again. Prysm's PR clamps descendant justified/finalized checkpoints to the anchor; Lighthouse has no clamp. Also missing: a non-finalized StateId option on checkpoint-sync-url, status/range-sync handling when our fake finalized epoch is ahead of peers, and custody/backfill origin handling.
impact: Lets a node resync and attest within minutes during long non-finality instead of failing to find a finalized checkpoint; no gain in normal mainnet operation.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, checked the fork choice store init (anchor forced as justified+finalized), the proto_array viability filter, and searched fork_choice/proto_array for any checkpoint clamp (none). The viability check means the manual-file path likely does not work under real non-finality, which strengthens the gap; the store-test WSS tests only cover anchors near finality.

title: Backpressure on async block DB write queue
idea: During sync, wait for free capacity in the async block/column write queue before enqueuing more, so queued data cannot grow without bound.
measured_best: Supernode external memory spiked ~4.5GB to ~10GB causing OOM before fix (pr:lodestar#8885)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4752 block and columns written synchronously via store.do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache inside spawn_blocking
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4410 import_available_block awaits import, no unbounded write queue

title: Bounded builder header timeout with local fallback
idea: Put a hard, short (configurable) timeout on the builder getHeader request during block production and fall back to the locally built payload when it expires, so a slow relay cannot delay the proposal.
evidence: beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:35 default get_header timeout 1000ms
beacon_node/cli.rs:963 --builder-header-timeout capped 3000ms
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1056 fetch_builder_and_local_payloads joins builder and local; falls back to local on error
impact: none; already bounded and falls back to local payload.

title: Compute block root after broadcasting proposal
idea: Defer hash_tree_root of the proposed block until after it is broadcast, using only the slot for pre-broadcast logging, to take the HTR off the proposal critical path.
measured_best: HTR ~10-20ms on M1 Max (pr:prysm#12504)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:167 block_root = block_root.unwrap_or_else(|| block.canonical_root()) before any publish (all full-block callers pass None: http_api/src/lib.rs:880,919,963,1005)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:878-893 GossipVerifiedBlock::new recomputes the root via signed_block_header()+get_block_header_root before publish
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:249-268 publish_block_p2p runs only after into_gossip_verified_block succeeds
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:664-669 blinded path hashes the cheaper blinded block and passes Some(root), but still before broadcast
gap: The full-block root is hashed twice before broadcast (publish_blocks.rs:167 and inside GossipVerifiedBlock::new). Pass the root computed once into gossip verification, or take it from GossipVerifiedBlock, to remove the duplicate. Gossip verification needs the root (seen-cache, proposer checks), so the root cannot move fully after broadcast the way Prysm does it.
impact: Removes one redundant block-body HTR (~several ms for large payloads) from the proposal critical path; small.
refute_note: Checked every publish_block caller, the blinded-block path, and GossipVerifiedBlock::new. No deferral exists. The search also found that the root is computed twice before publish, which is a cheaper and more realistic fix than full deferral.

title: SSZ encoding for VC block production requests
idea: Have the validator client request and receive produced blocks as SSZ instead of JSON by default, avoiding JSON encode/decode cost and payload size for large blocks with blobs.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/block_service.rs:707 post_validator_blocks_v4_ssz
validator_client/validator_services/src/block_service.rs:794 get_validator_blocks_v3_ssz
impact: none; VC uses SSZ with fallback.

title: Build proposals on state pre-advanced to proposal slot
idea: Advance the head state to the proposal slot (slot and epoch processing, including any epoch transition) before the slot starts, cache it, and have block production clone that state and run only process_block on it, passing the known state root. This removes process_slots/epoch processing from the proposal critical path.
measured_best: Pyrmont block production ~550ms -> ~150ms (pr:lighthouse#2241)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:109 advances head state at 3/4 of slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:87 get_advanced_hot_state used for production
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5870 complete_state_advance is a no-op when state is already at slot
impact: none.

title: Aggregate unaggregated attestations with aggregates when packing
idea: When packing a block, pack aggregated and unaggregated pool attestations from one combined list, aggregating singles (e.g. previous slot) into matching aggregates before selection. The block carries fewer, denser attestations and more duplicates are removed.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5944-5960 naive aggregation pool attestations are inserted into op pool before packing
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:457 AttestationMap::insert greedily aggregates into existing aggregates
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:383 aggregate_across_committees for electra+
impact: None; singles are merged into aggregates in the op pool and max cover selects from that one list.

title: Attester cache keyed by epoch and head root
idea: Keep a cache of attestation-data inputs (justified checkpoint, target root, committee lengths) keyed by epoch and head/target root, so attestation data for any slot can be served without loading and advancing a state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2025 early_attester_cache.try_attest
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2124 same-epoch path reads justified checkpoint and committee len from head state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2152 cross-epoch path get_advanced_hot_state + partial_state_advance + build_committee_cache
gap: No (epoch, root)-keyed attester cache exists (no attester_cache.rs; only early_attester_cache, shuffling_cache, beacon_proposer_cache). Cross-epoch requests still load an advanced hot state and may partial-advance it; a small cache of justified checkpoint + committee lengths keyed by (epoch, decision root) would remove that.
impact: Only epoch-boundary attestation production when head state lags request epoch; state advance timer usually pre-advances, so saving is small.
refute_note: Listed beacon_chain/src for any attester/committee-length cache and grepped AttesterCache across beacon_node; only an error variant name survives in shuffling_cache.rs:83, no cache.

title: Read next-slot proposer from head state lookahead
idea: Post-Fulu, read the next-slot proposer index from the head state's proposer lookahead instead of advancing a state through the epoch transition just to learn it, and build the prepared next-slot state only once.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1655 get_beacon_proposer_index reads proposer_lookahead post-Fulu
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1681 get_beacon_proposer_indices slices lookahead
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:227 proposer cache fills from that
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5286 get_pre_payload_attributes uses with_proposer_cache with head state
impact: Already cheap: next-slot proposer comes from the lookahead vector via the proposer cache, no epoch transition needed.

title: Allocation-free scoring in greedy proof selection
idea: In greedy aggregate/proof selection, count newly covered validators without allocating per candidate and materialize the covered set only for the winning pick.
measured_best: Removes N-1 allocations per iteration (no timings) (pr:ethlambda#254)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:61-100 greedy loop updates candidate sets in place
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:165 update_covering_set uses retain, no new set per candidate
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:176 score sums values without allocating
gap: Minor: each candidate still owns a HashMap built up front in AttMaxCover::new_for_altair_or_later, and the winner is cloned (max_cover.rs:84).
impact: Per-iteration allocation is already one clone of the winner; remaining cost is the up-front per-candidate HashMap, negligible against block production time.

title: Payload attributes withdrawals without cloning head state
idea: Compute withdrawals, randao mix and proposer index for next-slot payload attributes from the shared head/snapshot state without cloning it or doing extra state advances, and reuse cached payload attributes.
measured_best: reduced memory usage (pr:caplin#11997)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5396 compute_withdrawals_for_payload_attributes borrows head state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5432 Empty-parent path returns payload_expected_withdrawals without advance
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5440 TODO(gloas) restore pre-Gloas no-advance-past-epoch optimisation
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5452 into_owned + partial_state_advance to proposal_slot
gap: Proposer index/randao come from caches and the Empty-parent Gloas case skips advance, but the normal path still clones (CoW) and partial-advances the head state to proposal_slot, including epoch processing across a boundary. Restoring the pre-Gloas cap (advance at most to the epoch boundary, or compute withdrawals from the unadvanced state) closes it.
impact: Small: one partial advance per proposer-prep call; larger only at epoch boundaries.
refute_note: Re-read the full function: found the additional Empty-parent short-circuit (no advance) not cited earlier, and the explicit TODO confirming the advance is still done otherwise.

title: Publish proposed or gossip-valid block before full import
idea: Broadcast a block (and its blobs) as soon as gossip/consensus validation passes, in parallel with or before full import (DB write, fork choice), instead of only after import completes, so propagation starts earlier.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:249 BroadcastValidation::Gossip publishes right after gossip verification, before process_block
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1661 Accept propagated before import
gap: Consensus/ConsensusAndEquivocation levels publish only after validation by design; VC default uses Gossip level.
impact: none for default path.

title: Publish block first, blob/column sidecars afterwards
idea: On proposal, publish the block to the network immediately without waiting on sidecars, then compute/broadcast the blob or data column sidecars (KZG cell proofs) concurrently afterwards. The block leaves sooner and low-upload nodes do not delay it behind sidecar uploads.
measured_best: avg wait 18.04 ms vs 23.48 ms over 2000 holesky blocks (pr:teku#8868)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:242 sidecar build spawned as blocking task concurrently
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:249-266 block published p2p right after gossip verification (Gossip level, the VC default)
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:295 columns awaited and published afterwards (line 313)
gap: At Consensus or ConsensusAndEquivocation broadcast validation the block is published from publish_fn inside process_block, after columns are built and gossip-verified; only the default Gossip level publishes before the sidecars.
impact: Block leaves without waiting for KZG cell proof computation on the default path.

title: Tune EL payload collection deadline within slot
idea: Choose the time to call getPayload relative to slot start and attestation deadline: give the EL a fill window instead of grabbing the first (near-empty) result, but stop early enough that the block is published in time.
measured_best: Sepolia: 3 txs/0.185% gas/53 ms -> 245 txs/33.1% gas/3.08 s build (pr:caplin#21989)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:437 get_payload called when block production runs
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:976 get_payload has no fill-window or deadline logic
gap: get_payload is called whenever the VC requests a block; the EL builds from the earlier forkchoiceUpdated with attributes, but nothing tunes call time against slot start or the attestation deadline. Would need a delay/deadline in the block production path before the get_payload call in execution_payload.rs.
impact: Could raise block value (fuller local payloads) when the EL has little build time; no CPU saving. Gain depends on how early the VC requests the block.

title: Block value from rewards cached during state transition
idea: Record consensus block rewards and payload value in a per-slot cache attached to the state while processing the produced block, so block production returns the block value without a second rewards pass or body parsing, and pass block metadata between VC and BN in headers.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6537 compute_beacon_block_reward called as separate pass before per_block_processing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_block_reward.rs:273 re-walks block attestations, copies participation lists, rebuilds committee caches
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:862 same second pass for Gloas
gap: Record rewards inside per_block_processing (process_attestations, sync aggregate, slashings) into a state/ctxt accumulator, and have produce_partial_beacon_block/produce_block_on_state read it instead of calling compute_beacon_block_reward. Needs a reward-tracking hook in consensus/state_processing.
impact: Removes one extra attestation-walk and participation-list clone per produced block (a few ms on proposal only); negligible for non-proposing nodes.

title: Credential prefix check before balance read in withdrawals
idea: In get_expected_withdrawals, test the eth1 withdrawal credential prefix with a single-byte compare first and read the validator balance only for validators that pass.
measured_best: Benchmark on mainnet-like state: ~0.023-0.029 s/op before, ~0.008-0.013 s/op after (pr:teku#6525)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/withdrawals.rs:280-283 get_validators_sweep_withdrawals reads balance via get_balance_after_withdrawals for every validator before calling is_fully/partially_withdrawable_validator
consensus/types/src/validator/validator.rs:193-275 credential check happens only inside those predicates, after the balance read
gap: In get_validators_sweep_withdrawals test validator.has_execution_withdrawal_credential(spec) first and only call get_balance_after_withdrawals for those that pass (skip validator otherwise). Note most validators are 0x01/0x02 on mainnet now, so the saving is smaller than in Teku's measurement; the balance lookup is a milhouse list get.
impact: Saves up to 16384 balance tree lookups per get_expected_withdrawals (block processing, block production, payload attributes); likely sub-millisecond to low ms per call, only helps validators with 0x00 credentials.

title: Compute payload attributes once for SSE and fcU
idea: Compute payload attributes (withdrawals, gas limit) once and reuse them for both the payload_attributes SSE event and the EL forkchoiceUpdated call.
measured_best: best case 6.2us, worst case 2.8ms per run; PR calls it a cleanup, not a perf improvement (pr:lodestar#10056)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6954 payload_attributes fetched from EL cache, computed only on miss (comment: saves recomputing withdrawals)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7033-7068 PayloadAttributes::new once then insert_proposer
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7103 same value reused for SSE event; fcU reads it from the cache
impact: Already computed once per prepare and shared by SSE and fcU.

title: Early fcU with attributes hitting cached payload ID
idea: Before the slot of a known local proposer (at a proportional point in the prior slot, and again on head change), send forkchoiceUpdated with payload attributes to the EL and cache the returned payload ID keyed by head/parent, with attributes and fork detection matching those used at getPayload time. Block production then calls getPayload with the cached ID at once instead of building a payload last-minute.
measured_best: shaved 0.5s off block production in minimal-preset testnets (pr:nimbus#7986)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:217 prepare_beacon_proposer called ahead of next slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1931 also on head change
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6719 sends fcU with payload attributes
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1342 engine.get_payload_id cache lookup before getPayload
impact: none.

title: Skip parent-weight check on early fcU
idea: For early proposer forkchoiceUpdated calls, skip the parent-weight (reorg) check until current attestations are imported, so the EL does not build a payload that is later discarded.
measured_best: avoids wasted EL payload build (pr:prysm#13683)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5576-5586 head/parent weight thresholds only enforced when fork_choice_slot == re_org_block_slot, otherwise (true,true)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5611 head-late check is the early heuristic, comment explains attestations not yet imported
impact: Early fcU (before the re-org slot) skips the parent-weight check, so the EL builds on the parent rather than a payload later discarded.

title: Delay post-import fcU until shortly before next slot
idea: Instead of sending forkchoiceUpdated right after block import, send it shortly before the next slot so the EL returns a payload id and proposer-boost reorg remains possible.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5503 overridden_forkchoice_update_params suppresses head fcU when a re-org is planned
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6719 prepare_beacon_proposer sends the payload-attributes fcU shortly before next slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:210 calls it after pre-emptive fork choice
gap: Lighthouse does not delay the post-import fcU but achieves the same effect differently: the post-import fcU is overridden to the parent when re-org conditions hold, and the payload-attribute fcU is sent late in the slot (not Gloas, which never overrides).
impact: Same re-org and payload id outcome; no extra cost to add.

title: Filter packed attestations by shuffling dependent root
idea: When packing attestations, drop those whose target shuffling/dependent root differs from the proposal state's using a cheap root comparison, before any expensive validity checks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2739 filter_op_pool_attestation
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2765 shuffling_is_compatible compares shuffling IDs from fork choice, cheap
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5983 filter passed into op_pool.get_attestations; cached per (block_root, target_epoch)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:327 filter runs before AttMaxCover::new
impact: Already done before expensive reward computation, with a per-call cache.

title: Propose with builder header without awaiting local payload
idea: If the builder header is ready, propose with it without waiting for a slow local payload; compare values only when the local payload has already finished.
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1076 comment 'Wait for the builder *and* local EL' + tokio::join!
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1157 determine_and_fetch_payload matches on both results after join
gap: fetch_builder_and_local_payloads joins both futures; no select/early return when the builder header is ready, even with builder_boost_factor favoring the builder. Switch to select with a short grace period for the local payload.
impact: Saves the local-vs-relay latency gap on builder proposals when the local getPayload is slow (usually fast since payload is prebuilt via fcU).
refute_note: Searched execution_layer/src/lib.rs for select!/timeouts and builder-preference short circuits; only builder_header_timeout on the relay side and chain-health fallback to local exist.

title: Drop newPayload for locally built payloads
idea: Do not call engine_newPayload on a locally built payload during block production; the safeguard costs more latency than it is worth.
measured_best: "a safeguard which probably costs more than is worth" (pr:nimbus#4186)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:77 precomputed status only for NotifyExecutionLayer::No with optimistic_finalized_sync
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:104 notify_new_payload otherwise calls EL
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:451 envelope import uses NotifyExecutionLayer::Yes
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1445 notify_new_payload has no payload_cache/self-built short-circuit
gap: Own blocks and self-built Gloas envelopes still go through engine_newPayload; is_locally_built_block only affects provenance/logging. Add a precomputed Valid status for payloads the EL itself produced (e.g. hit in payload_cache) in PayloadNotifier::new and the envelope PayloadNotifier.
impact: One EL round trip off local import of own block; block is already published, so small.
refute_note: Also checked the Gloas envelope path (payload_notifier.rs, import.rs) and the EL's notify_new_payload/payload_cache; self-built envelopes only get a signature-verification fast path, not a newPayload skip.

title: Read proposer index from primed proposer cache
idea: During block creation, read the proposer index from the proposer cache instead of recomputing proposer shuffling (e.g. at epoch boundaries), and have the state advance timer prime the next-epoch proposer cache (Fulu lookahead) ahead of time.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1654-1700 post-Fulu proposer index read from proposer_lookahead in state (O(1))
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:343-398 state advance primes proposer cache for current and next epoch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:409 and beacon_chain.rs:5891 get_beacon_proposer_index on advanced state
impact: Fulu lookahead makes the index a vector read; cache is primed ahead of the epoch boundary. Pre-Fulu recompute path remains but is dead on mainnet.

title: Drop subset aggregates before packing
idea: Just before packing, remove aggregates whose bits are a subset of another selected aggregate so no block space goes to attestations with no new votes.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:53 maximum_cover drops score==0 items and removes covered validators after each pick
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:165 update_covering_set removes already-covered validators so subsets reach score 0
impact: None needed; subset aggregates score zero and are never selected.

title: Build block body in parallel with payload fetch
idea: Fire the engine getPayload and builder header requests at the start of production and build the consensus/blinded body (attestations, operations, state processing) concurrently as an independent part, joining at the end. Production takes the max of the two flows instead of their sum.
measured_best: race cutoff lowered from 2.5s to 2s (pr:lodestar#7814)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5919 get_execution_payload spawned before attestation packing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5760 payload handle awaited after partial block built
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1077 tokio::join! of builder and local fetch
impact: none; production is max of the two flows.

title: Fast retry of busy payload preparation
idea: When the EL is busy and payload build preparation is skipped, retry quickly (exponential backoff from ~10 ms, or frequent retries within the preparation window) instead of a fixed long delay, so the build starts earlier.
measured_best: wait before build p50 200 ms -> 71 ms, p90 200 -> 151 ms (pr:caplin#24965)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/proposer_prep_service.rs:28-65 fixed timer prepare_payload_lookahead before slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1908-1931 prepare after each head fcU
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7137-7150 awaited fcU over JSON-RPC, no busy/skip state
impact: Caplin's embedded EL semaphore returns busy and defers; Lighthouse talks to an external EL via engine API fcU, which just blocks until the EL answers, so there is no skipped-preparation retry to tighten.

title: Recompute fork choice head right before building proposal
idea: Immediately before block production, process pending attestations and run fork choice to recompute the head, so the proposal builds on the freshest head.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:48 load_state_for_block_production first calls wait_for_fork_choice_before_block_production
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:130 waits (fork_choice_before_proposal_timeout_ms) on fork_choice_signal_rx for the slot-start fork choice run
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7496 per_slot_task runs recompute_head_at_current_slot at slot start
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7512 then notifies the waiting block production via notify_fork_choice_complete
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fork_choice_signal.rs:74 wait_for_fork_choice
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:211 extra pre-emptive recompute_head_at_slot(next_slot) before the slot
impact: Already in place: the proposal blocks until fork choice has run at the start of the proposal slot, so all attestations that may count (those from earlier slots) are applied. A second inline run would add only late votes that arrive in the few ms after slot start.
refute_note: The earlier review missed block_production/mod.rs: block production does not run fork choice itself, but it waits on the ForkChoiceSignal for the slot-start run. This gives the same freshest-head guarantee.

title: Skip payload-attribute preparation when not synced
idea: Do not compute payload attributes (state copy and slot replay) while the node is not in regular sync, and do not consider the node synced while its head is far behind peer-reported heads. This stops payload-attribute preparation from regenerating state across hundreds of epochs.
measured_best: Stated: 9 GB heap exhausted by replaying ~27-34 epoch transitions when head was 850-1100 slots behind (pr:teku#11219)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6752 skips prep if head older than sync_tolerance_epochs
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5319 SkipProposerPreparation on proposer cache miss when head far behind
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:269 MAX_ADVANCE_DISTANCE 256
gap: No peer-head based synced check, but head-vs-wallclock tolerance gives the same protection; cache miss clones head state without replay.
impact: none.

title: Greedy max-cover attestation selection
idea: Select block attestations with a greedy max-cover algorithm, scoring each candidate by not-yet-covered bits, as a cheap approximation to optimal packing.
measured_best: slower than naive sort: 512 single-bit atts about 5.1 ms vs 0.31 ms; a quality trade-off (pr:prysm#8571)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs maximum_cover greedy
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:447 merge_solutions of max-cover results
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:345 get_attestations
impact: Lighthouse already packs attestations with greedy weighted max-cover (scored by newly covered validators times reward).

title: Process slots and state root once for all attestations
idea: In block production, run process_slots and the state hash_tree_root once and reuse them for every packed attestation instead of per attestation.
measured_best: should save 50ms to 100ms on block proposals (pr:prysm#5632)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:395 complete_state_advance once per production
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:409-420 one op_pool pass on the single advanced state
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:345 get_attestations takes one state for all attestations
impact: State is advanced and rooted once, then all attestations are selected against that one state.

title: Keep pool signatures in deserialized form
idea: Store attestation pool signatures as already-decompressed curve points (lazy aggregation) so building a block does not decompress each signature.
measured_best: Proposal ~6x faster at 220k validators: 14962ms -> 2326ms non-epoch slot (pr:nimbus#2423)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:40 CompactIndexedAttestation stores bls AggregateSignature
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:249 signature.add_assign_aggregate merges points in place
impact: None needed; the pool keeps the aggregate as a blst point, so packing does not decompress per signature (assuming bls AggregateSignature holds the decompressed point, which it does in the blst backend).

title: Re-run payload preparation late in prior slot
idea: Re-send payload preparation (fcU with attributes) about one second before the slot ends so the EL builds with more mempool transactions.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/proposer_prep_service.rs:35 fires prepare_beacon_proposer slot_duration/3 before slot end
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:217 prepare_beacon_proposer again at slot_duration/24 before slot end
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7135 sends fcU with payload attributes
impact: None needed; fcU with attributes is re-sent about 0.5s before slot end (and at 4s), so the EL has mempool contents up to then.

title: Locally aggregate sync messages into block sync aggregate
idea: When packing the sync aggregate, aggregate individually seen sync committee messages along with received contributions (parallel per subnet), so the block includes a fuller aggregate.
measured_best: aggregation 3-4x faster per subnet parallelism (pr:prysm#15608)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:117 insert_sync_contribution keeps only the best contribution per subcommittee, no merging
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:163 get_sync_aggregate builds only from pool contributions
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6066 block production uses op_pool.get_sync_aggregate; naive_sync_aggregation_pool (beacon_chain.rs:428) is only used to serve contribution requests
gap: Merge non-overlapping contributions per subcommittee (aggregate bits and signatures) in insert_sync_contribution, and fold naive_sync_aggregation_pool messages for the parent root into get_sync_aggregate at production time.
impact: Slightly fuller sync aggregate (a little more proposer sync reward) at some extra aggregation CPU on the proposal path; small.

title: Request local payload and builder bid concurrently with cutoff
idea: Request the local EL payload and the external builder bid concurrently rather than sequentially, with a cutoff (~3s) after which whichever is available is used. Proposal latency becomes the max of the two, bounded by the cutoff, so a slow EL or builder does not delay the proposal.
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1077 tokio::join! of builder get_builder_header and local get_full_payload_caching
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:35 DEFAULT_GET_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MILLIS = 1000 (relay cutoff, configurable via builder_header_timeout)
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api/http.rs:52 ENGINE_GET_PAYLOAD_TIMEOUT = 2s applied to every engine_getPayload version (http.rs:988-1136)
gap: Small: no single shared cutoff. Each leg has its own timeout (builder 1s, getPayload 2s), so the join is bounded by about 2s. On a payload-id cache miss (lib.rs:1370), the local leg first sends forkchoiceUpdated, which has an 8s timeout.
impact: Already bounded: proposal latency is the max of the two requests and each has a timeout, so a slow EL or relay cannot stall it past about 2s in the normal pre-prepared-payload case.
refute_note: The earlier gap said the local EL request had no cutoff. That is wrong: engine_getPayload has a 2s HTTP timeout, and the builder header has a 1s default. Together they give the idea's bounded concurrent fetch.

title: Fall back to P2P bid in parallel with local build
idea: When a supplied builder bid fails validation, consider the best P2P bid in parallel with local payload production and return whichever is ready by the cutoff.
measured_best: Observed local build 3.483s; P2P fallback could return about 2.086s sooner (pr:lodestar#10212)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:310 tokio::join of acquire_external_bid_candidates and local build
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/gloas.rs:1117 external candidates include direct and gossip bids; failed local build falls back to external bid
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/bid_selection.rs select_payload_bid ranks all candidates
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_bid_verification/payload_bid_cache.rs:71 get_highest_bid for gossip bids
impact: Already races builder/gossip bids against the local build post-Gloas.

title: Gossip-verify blinded block in parallel with unblinding
idea: When publishing a blinded block, run the gossip validity and duplicate checks concurrently with the builder unblinding (submitBlindedBlock) request instead of after it. The checks then finish before the relay's gossip copy arrives, so the block is not delayed or treated as a duplicate.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:657 publish_blinded_block calls reconstruct_block, then returns Ok(empty) for builder blocks
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:734 el.propose_blinded_beacon_block is awaited alone and returns Ok(None); no GossipVerifiedBlock or duplicate check runs before or alongside it
gap: For builder (blinded) proposals, run gossip verification and seen-block registration of the blinded block concurrently with propose_blinded_beacon_block (for example with tokio::join!), so the full block that the relay gossips takes the fast path when it arrives.
impact: Saves the gossip-verification time (tens of ms) on import of the relay's copy of our own builder blocks.
refute_note: Read the full blinded publish path (publish_blinded_block and reconstruct_block). Only local-payload blocks go through publish_block verification. Builder blocks are only submitted to the relay, with no parallel verification.

title: Participation overlay instead of rebuilding epoch participation
idea: In the attestation packing/sorting step, do not rebuild current and previous epoch participation from the state for every proposal; keep a cached copy of on-chain participation and apply an overlay that records the mutations of candidate attestations. This removes a full participation rebuild from block production.
measured_best: Sorting init 210-221 ms -> 45-57 ms (pr:teku#9660)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/reward_cache.rs:14 RewardCache keeps a compact BitVec of on-chain participation, reused for the same (epoch, head block)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:166 update_covering_set removes covered validators from candidates (the overlay of candidate mutations); the state is never copied or mutated
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:370 reward_cache.update(state) runs on the proposal path
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/reward_cache.rs:88 the full BitVec is rebuilt whenever the head block changes
gap: The overlay half exists: max-cover covering sets work against a read-only cached BitVec. But the cache is rebuilt by a full scan of both participation lists on the first proposal after each new head, which is in practice every proposal. Build it during the state advance or update it incrementally.
impact: Removes two passes over all validators (single-digit to low tens of ms) from block production; smaller than Teku's 160 ms gain because Lighthouse already avoids state copies.
refute_note: Checked AttMaxCover: candidate mutations are already applied as an overlay, without copying participation. The only remaining cost is the per-head BitVec rebuild on the proposal path.

title: Score attestations by newly set participation flags
idea: When packing attestations, score each candidate by which participation flags (source/target/head) it would newly set in the state, i.e. by its actual reward, rather than only by the count of new attester bits. This packs higher-value attestations into the limited block space.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:88 get_attestation_participation_flag_indices computes which flags the attestation would set at this inclusion delay
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:112 per-validator reward = base_reward * sum of PARTICIPATION_FLAG_WEIGHTS for those flags
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:182 score() is the summed proposer reward, not the bit count
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/reward_cache.rs:17 documents why validators with any flag set cannot gain new flags except by slashable double voting
gap: Only the slashable-vote corner case: a validator with some flags already set is skipped instead of being scored for the missing flags.
impact: Already in place: attestations are scored by actual proposer reward from newly set flags. The remaining case needs a slashable vote, so it has almost no effect.
refute_note: The earlier gap assumed that flags could be added to a validator who already has some. That is not possible: the head flag needs delay 1 and later inclusions only lose flags, so any other route is a double vote. Lighthouse's reward-weighted scoring is therefore what the idea describes.

title: Record payload ID for late-arriving blocks
idea: When a block arrives late and triggers a forkchoiceUpdated, still store the returned payload ID in the proposer/payload-ID cache. The proposer then reuses it instead of issuing a fresh forkchoiceUpdated at proposal time.
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engines.rs:176 Engine::notify_forkchoice_updated inserts any returned payload_id into payload_id_cache keyed by head hash + attributes, regardless of caller
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1342 get_full_payload_with reads cache first, only sends fresh FCU on miss
impact: None needed; every FCU response with a payload id is cached, including those for late blocks.

title: Do not key payload cache on safe/finalized hashes
idea: When looking up a cached payload-build (payload ID) at proposal time, match on head/parent, timestamp and attributes but not on the safe and finalized block hashes. A changed finalized hash then does not cause a cache miss and an extra ~500ms getPayload delay.
measured_best: avoids consistent misses and additional 500ms delays when proposing (pr:nimbus#8268)
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engines.rs:109 PayloadIdCacheKey is only head_block_hash + payload_attributes
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engines.rs:149 get_payload_id looks up with that key (no safe/finalized hash)
impact: None needed; a changed finalized or safe hash does not cause a payload id miss.

title: Build consensus block body only once
idea: When producing a block with both builder and local EL payloads, build the consensus body (attestation packing, slashings, exits, proposal state) once and reuse it for both, or choose the payload first and then build one block, instead of building two full blocks and comparing.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5728 produce_block_on_state builds one partial block body, awaits one payload handle, completes once
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5917 get_execution_payload started concurrently with packing; builder-vs-local choice happens inside the payload fetch (Full or Blinded contents)
impact: None needed; consensus body is built once.

title: At most one state and epoch transition per proposal
idea: In block assembly, generate only the state at the block slot and run the epoch transition at most once, sharing it across body pieces, instead of also loading the previous-block state or recomputing the transition per piece.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:43 load_state_for_block_production loads one state (advanced head state from cache)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5871 complete_state_advance advances that single state once to the proposal slot; all body pieces use it
impact: None needed; no extra parent state load or repeated transition.

title: Pre-build and sign next block before slot start
idea: Build and sign the next slot's block before the slot starts against the current head, then at slot start revalidate parent and justified checkpoint and publish, falling back to a fresh build on mismatch. The heavy build work leaves the slot's critical path.
measured_best: block build ~1-2s moved off interval 0, near-100% pre-build hit rate (pr:ethlambda#445)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5237 produce_block_with_verification is driven by the VC request at slot start with randao_reveal supplied by the VC
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5960 pack_attestations is a few ms op-pool selection, not a 1-2s build
impact: Lighthouse does not sign blocks (the VC does, and the randao reveal exists only at slot start), and pre-building would miss attestations from the end of the previous slot; the build is cheap, so there is little to move.

title: Precompute attestation packing at slot start
idea: At slot start, for an expected local proposer, start attestation aggregation/packing asynchronously and return the in-flight result when the block is requested, instead of starting packing when the request arrives.
measured_best: ~580 ms async compute moved off request path (pr:teku#9122)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:456 AttestationMap::insert greedily aggregates same-committee attestations at insertion time, so that part of aggregation is already off the proposal path
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:382 aggregate_across_committees (Electra) runs on demand inside get_attestations
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:367 reward cache update and max-cover packing run on demand
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5943 naive aggregation pool imported into op pool at request time, then pack_attestations
gap: Lighthouse aggregates within a committee as attestations arrive, but the naive-pool import, cross-committee aggregation, reward cache update and max-cover packing all still start when the block is requested. Missing: a task at slot start (or at the 11.5s fork-choice/prepare_beacon_proposer point) for a known local proposer that runs these steps on the advanced head state, and a produce_partial_beacon_block path that takes the result when parent and slot match.
impact: Would take cross-committee aggregation plus max-cover (tens to low hundreds of ms on mainnet) off the proposal critical path. It helps only nodes with local proposers, and the result misses attestations that arrive after the precompute.
refute_note: The earlier review missed insertion-time greedy aggregation in attestation_storage.rs. That is an equivalent mechanism for part of Teku's precomputed aggregation. Packing itself is still on demand, and no precompute or cache of packing results exists.

title: Advance state for expected reorg parent
idea: At the last slot of an epoch, when the head is weak and a proposer reorg is expected, run next-slot state preparation (including the epoch transition) on the parent block instead of the head, so the transition is not redone at proposal time.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:277 advance_head only takes head_snapshot() and advances it; no parent or re-org-target branch

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:257 get_state_for_re_org takes the parent state from get_advanced_hot_state_from_cache(parent, slot); at an epoch boundary this is the parent advanced only to the weak head's slot (from the previous slot's timer)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5870 complete_state_advance at production time then runs the epoch transition inline
gap: In state_advance_timer, when the head is late or weak at the last slot of an epoch and get_proposer_head would pick the parent, also advance the parent's state to the next slot (including epoch processing) and cache it, so get_state_for_re_org finds it ready.
impact: Takes an epoch transition (hundreds of ms on mainnet) off the proposal path for epoch-boundary re-orgs, which have been enabled by default since v8.2.0. The event is rare, so the average gain is small.
refute_note: Checked advance_head, the 11.5s fork_choice_advance / prepare_beacon_proposer block, the FCR head-state advance in canonical_head.rs (not cached) and all complete/partial_state_advance call sites. None of them advances or caches the re-org parent's state.

title: Advance state for next slot after late blocks
idea: When a late block is imported (before the attestation deadline), still run the next-slot state advance for it, so attesters and proposers of the next slot find the advanced state ready.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4720 import_block_update_shuffling_cache runs for every imported block

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5216 primes Current and Next epoch committee caches (plus PTCs) from the block's post-state, so next-slot attesters and gossip verification have committees even across an epoch boundary
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:143 advance_head fires only once at 3/4 of the slot; a head imported after that point is not advanced
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1137 head update only reads get_advanced_hot_state, with no advance on a miss
gap: Shuffling is primed at import, but the late head's state is not advanced to the next slot. The next proposal (complete_state_advance) and the next block's import still pay the slot transition inline, plus the epoch transition at boundaries. Missing: after importing a head block that arrives after the 3/4-slot advance (or in the next slot before the attestation deadline), spawn advance_head for it.
impact: Avoids one per-slot transition, or an epoch transition at a boundary, on the next proposal and block-import path after late blocks. Attestation committees are already covered.
refute_note: The earlier review missed import-time shuffling cache priming for current and next epoch. That covers the attester and committee half of the idea. The state advance itself is still absent.

title: Produce from in-memory head state, not store
idea: Build the block on a copy of the in-memory head state rather than loading the base state from the fork choice store or disk.
measured_best: described as much faster (pr:caplin#13051)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:84 get_advanced_hot_state from the state cache, filled by the state advance timer
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5877 complete_state_advance on the loaded state
impact: Production starts from a cached, pre-advanced head state, not a disk load, in the normal case; the disk path (state_at_slot) is only for non-head parents.

title: Stop eth1 data voting work after deposit transition
idea: Once EIP-6110 deposit requests have taken over (eth1_deposit_index reached deposit_requests_start_index), skip eth1data voting in block production and prune the eth1 block cache, avoiding eth1 lookups and unbounded cache growth.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5931 eth1_data copied from state, no vote
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5933 deposits = vec![] (no eth1 deposit lookup)
impact: None needed: block production does no eth1 lookups and there is no eth1 block cache (eth1 service was removed).

title: Prune pending deposits on finalization
idea: On finalization, prune pending deposits up to the finalized checkpoint, so proposers do not read the deposit trie for old deposits.
measured_best: marked performance increase for proposing nodes (pr:prysm#12598)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5933 deposits = vec![] (no eth1 deposit tree is read in production)
impact: Lighthouse no longer keeps an eth1 deposit cache or reads deposits from a trie during block production (post-Electra deposit requests), so there is nothing to prune.

title: Publish blob sidecars before the block
idea: When publishing a locally produced block with blobs, publish the blob sidecars first, before block import and block publish, so they propagate while peers validate the block and are ready when peers ask.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:243 column build spawned before block gossip verification
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:264 default (Gossip) level: block published first
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:270 Consensus/ConsensusAndEquivocation: block publish deferred into publish_fn
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:314 columns published before block import (and before the block itself at consensus levels)
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:335 column import precedes block import at :353
common/eth2/src/types.rs:1851 default BroadcastValidation is Gossip
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:335 Gloas: envelope imported first
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:374 Gloas: columns awaited and published (:448) only after envelope import
gap: Fulu: columns already go out before block import, and before the block when broadcast_validation is consensus/consensus_and_equivocation; only the default gossip level puts the block on the wire first. Gloas (the current path for payload data): columns are published only after process_execution_payload_envelope returns, i.e. after envelope import/EL verification, so they trail the envelope by the full import time. Fix: publish columns right after column_build_future resolves (before or in parallel with envelope import), and in the Fulu gossip path publish columns before publish_block_p2p if they are ready.
impact: Gloas: columns reach peers earlier by roughly the envelope import time (EL newPayload, tens to hundreds of ms), lowering data-availability latency for the payload; Fulu: a few ms at the default level.
refute_note: Earlier review said columns always trail the block; at consensus validation levels the block is published inside process_block after columns are sent, and in all Fulu cases columns precede import. Also checked the Gloas envelope endpoint, where columns wait for envelope import, the larger remaining gap.

title: Size attestation selection buffers by new attesters
idea: In attestation packing, size per-candidate selection slices by the number of attesters with new flags, not by committee size, to avoid reserving unused memory.
measured_best: up to ~74 MB with a full pool (pr:caplin#24798)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:93 new_for_altair_or_later collects fresh_validators_rewards via filter_map over attesting indices, skipping already-attested ones
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:21 covering set is a HashMap of fresh validators only
impact: Covering sets are sized by fresh attesters, with no committee-sized buffers.

title: Skip signature verification in own block state transition
idea: When computing the post-state root of a block the node itself built (and when importing that block), run the state transition with signature verification disabled, since the contents come from verified pools and the block is verified again on import.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6529-6547 per_block_processing for state root uses VerifyRandao strategy (no attestation/op signature checks)
beacon_node/http_api/src/produce_block.rs:44 NoVerification option also exists
impact: None; signature batch verification is skipped when computing the post-state root of a self-built block.

title: Skip re-hashing transactions of unblinded builder payload
idea: When unblinding a builder payload, do not re-hash its transactions to check them against the signed header root before publishing, since a mismatch cannot be recovered anyway. This removes a full transactions tree hash from the publish path.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:734 propose_blinded_beacon_block hands blinded block to builder, which publishes it
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:715 local payload looked up by header tree_hash_root (header only, no transactions re-hash)

evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36-110 passes raw message byte slices (msgs_refs) to blst, which hashes to G2 internally per call
no hash_to/G2 cache found in crypto/ or beacon_node/beacon_chain/src
gap: Add a signing-root -> G2 point cache shared by gossip and block verification; requires lower-level blst pairing calls since verify_multiple_aggregate_signatures takes messages, not points.
impact: ~98us per repeated signing root; tens to hundreds of repeats per block. Small total CPU.
refute_note: Searched crypto/bls and beacon_chain for hash_to_curve/G2/message caches; the blst wrapper only takes byte messages, so no cache is possible at the current layer.

title: Single pass over keys and signatures in batch prep
idea: Validate and convert public keys or semi-aggregate signatures in the same loop that aggregates them, instead of iterating the list twice, and avoid boxed integers in that loop.
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:72-78 signature subgroup check and conversion in the same loop as key aggregation
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:94-103 pubkeys are collected to a Vec then aggregated
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:39 sets collected first
blst.rs:59-66 random scalar via unsafe, no boxing
gap: Signature checks and key aggregation share one loop and there is no boxing, but the pubkey refs are collected into a Vec before aggregate, and the sets are collected into a Vec first. Could aggregate straight from the iterator.
impact: A couple of percent on the batch prep step at most.

title: Skip signature checks for trusted or pre-verified blocks
idea: Pass a verify-signatures flag through block processing and skip BLS checks in the state transition for blocks already batch-verified or known valid (trusted finalized history during sync), for every fork. This removes the dominant BLS cost per block and avoids polluting the pubkey cache.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing.rs:71-77,147-164 BlockSignatureStrategy flag (NoVerification/VerifyBulk/...) threaded through per_block_processing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:671-721 signature_verify_chain_segment batch-verifies all block signatures up front
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1706-1712 per_block_processing then runs with NoVerification ('Signatures were verified earlier')
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:113-114 no_signature_verification for replay of trusted stored blocks, used at beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2566
beacon_node/store/src/reconstruct.rs:165 state reconstruction of finalized history uses NoVerification
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/historical_blocks.rs:393-415 backfill verifies only proposer signatures in one batch
gap: Only remaining difference: forward range sync of finalized history still batch-verifies all signatures (no checkpoint-trust skip), which is a trust-model choice rather than a missing mechanism.
impact: Already realized: the state transition never re-verifies BLS for batch-verified blocks, and stored/finalized blocks are replayed without BLS.
refute_note: Source PRs (nimbus#4085, lodestar flag commits) are exactly 'skip state-transition BLS for blocks already batch-verified / trusted'; Lighthouse does this via BlockSignatureStrategy::NoVerification after signature_verify_chain_segment and in BlockReplayer/reconstruction, which the earlier review missed.

title: Do not recheck proposer signature verified at gossip
idea: Build block signature sets without the proposer signature when that signature was already verified during gossip validation, so it is not verified a second time at import.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1252 from_gossip_verified_block 'Does not re-verify the proposer signature'
consensus/state_processing/.../block_signature_verifier.rs:168 include_all_signatures_except_proposal

title: No pubkey aggregation for single-signer attestations
idea: For unaggregated gossip attestations, build the signature set from the single pubkey directly instead of running a pubkey aggregation step over a one-element list.

gap: In verify_signature_sets, if signing_keys.len()==1 use the key directly and skip AggregatePublicKey::aggregate and the Vec of refs. Also avoid the vec![] in single_pubkey.
impact: Saves a point conversion and two small allocations per unaggregated attestation; well under 1% CPU.

title: Route batchable vs latency-critical BLS jobs separately
idea: Send batchable signature jobs (gossip attestations) to the batching worker threads and verify non-batchable latency-critical jobs (blocks) directly, to keep BLS job wait time under a target (100ms).

title: Subtract non-participants from full sync committee aggregate
idea: For sync-aggregate verification, start from the precomputed aggregate pubkey of the whole sync committee and subtract the keys of non-participants, since participation is over 95%, instead of summing all participants.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/signature_sets.rs:814-829 collects participant pubkeys and sums them via SignatureSet::multiple_pubkeys

idea: When blobs or columns for a block are missing, query the local EL first and send RPC requests to peers only for the ones still missing. Share one received-sidecar set between the EL and the p2p fetch paths so no sidecar is fetched twice.

title: Trigger getBlobs on first gossip column sidecar

title: Delay RPC fetch of missing sidecars
idea: Delay RPC fetches of missing blobs/columns by a slot-time-based interval (about 0.5 to 1 s, capped by the attestation deadline), so gossip can deliver them first and redundant requests are avoided.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1972 gossip block with MissingComponents starts no RPC fetch
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2874-2886 the lookup is started only by attestations for a block not in fork choice (about 1/3 slot)

beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:73 QUEUED_RECONSTRUCTION_DELAY 150ms gives gossip time before reconstruction
gap: There is no explicit slot-time-based delay. The delay comes only from the trigger: Lighthouse never fetches on block arrival, waits for attestations and 3 peers, and then requests only the columns it has not cached. The Gloas column BlockRootUnknown path (gossip_methods.rs:790) and unknown-parent lookups fetch at once, with no wait capped at the attestation deadline.
impact: Small. Most of the redundant by-root requests are already avoided. An explicit delay would only help the Gloas column and unknown-parent triggers.
refute_note: The earlier review missed that Lighthouse does not fetch at block arrival at all. Its lookup starts from attestations at about 4s and needs 3 corroborating peers, and it filters columns already received on gossip. This gives the 'let gossip deliver first' effect without a timer.

title: Pull late block when blobs arrive first
idea: If blobs arrive on gossip but the block does not arrive by a cutoff, fetch the block and remaining blobs from peers instead of waiting.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1241-1246 a Gloas gossip column for an unknown block root returns BlockRootUnknown

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1016-1023 a Fulu column with a known parent goes to the DA checker as MissingComponents and starts no block lookup
gap: Gloas already does this: a column for an unknown block root starts a block lookup at once, with no cutoff. Fulu, the live fork, does not. A Fulu column carries a signed header, so with a known parent it verifies without the block, sits as MissingComponents, and the block is fetched only when attestations arrive. Add a cutoff timer after the first Fulu column for an unseen block that sends search_unknown_block for that root.
impact: On Fulu, a block missed on gossip but whose columns arrive is recovered before the attestations come (about 4s), which improves head vote timing.
refute_note: Found the Gloas and partial-column BlockRootUnknown path, which starts a lookup from a sidecar of an unknown block. The earlier review searched only UnknownParentSidecarHeader. Fulu remains uncovered, so the verdict is partial.

title: Fetch missing columns within the slot
idea: Run the missing-column fetcher every second and request missing custody columns by root after a grace of half the time to the attestation deadline, instead of waiting a minute.
measured_best: block stayed unavailable for over a minute before (pr:caplin#24830)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2874-2886 an attestation for a block that is pending in the DA checker (not in fork choice) starts a lookup within the slot

gap: There is no periodic fetcher that scans the DA checker for blocks with missing custody columns. Recovery inside the slot depends on attestations that reference the block, from at least 3 peers. Add a 1s tick that scans pending components past a grace period and issues custody by-root requests, so recovery does not depend on attestation traffic.
impact: Low to medium. The minute-long wait that Caplin fixed does not occur in Lighthouse when attestations flow. A tick would help only when few attestations reference the block, for example a late block or a small or isolated set of peers.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the following: when a block is stuck in the DA checker, gossip attestations for it fail with UnknownHeadBlock, and that already starts an in-slot lookup that fetches only the missing custody columns. This is event-driven, not periodic.

title: Disk-backed blob quarantine

title: Evict DA entries exactly when import completes
idea: Keep a block's pending components and sampling tracker in the availability cache until fork choice import completes, then remove them at once (otherwise LRU/finality), holding the write lock only for the insert. This prevents re-downloads and keeps the cache from growing.

gap: Lighthouse keeps entries (deliberately, to avoid a re-insert race) until LRU/finality, so re-downloads are prevented and the write lock is short, but entries are not freed at import completion. Could remove in the import-complete path via a remove on overflow_lru_cache after fork choice import, if the race is handled.
impact: Only memory: a few tens of MB of columns held until finality; no CPU saving.

title: Big-endian slot-prefixed keys for ordered seeks
idea: Encode slot/epoch as a big-endian key prefix (then root, index) in prunable tables so key order equals slot order. Pruning and range queries seek directly to the cutoff slot and stream in order, instead of scanning from the table start or looking up headers per row.
measured_best: Requests tested under 2s per state regen from cold checkpoint (pr:prysm#6461)

gap: Most of the history is in big-endian slot-ordered keys with seek-based range reads (freezer roots, snapshots, diffs, LC updates). The prunable blob/column tables and the hot block/state tables are still keyed by root. Pruning them needs a block load plus up to 128 key_exists checks per block, not a seek and range delete. A slot prefix or a slot->root index needs a schema migration (store/src/metadata.rs) and changes to the BeaconBlob/BeaconDataColumn get/put paths.
impact: Small at steady state: about 32 block loads per prune run, each with column key_exists checks. It matters more when catching up after pruning was off. The query side already gets ordered seeks for the freezer.
refute_note: I searched for to_be_bytes and iter_column_from across the store. The mechanism (big-endian slot keys, seek to the cutoff, stream in order) exists for the freezer and LC-update tables, and blob pruning uses it to find its start point. Only the root-keyed prunable tables lack it, so I upgraded the verdict to partial.
