title: State delta against snapshot, not parent
idea: Store each non-snapshot state as a delta against the nearest snapshot on its branch rather than against its parent, so a cold read applies one delta instead of folding a chain of deltas.
measured_best: None stated (up to 31 sequential deltas replaced by one) (pr:ethlambda#684)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:660 storage_strategy: DiffFrom(previous layer slot/n_big*n_big), not snapshot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2423 load_hdiff_buffer_for_slot folds layer chain
gap: Change HierarchyModuli::storage_strategy and load_hdiff_buffer_for_slot to diff against the layer-top snapshot. Diffs get larger, trading disk for fewer applies; needs schema change.
impact: Cold state reads apply at most a few diffs now (layers) so gain is small and disk grows; marginal.

title: Drop in-memory index for archived block range
idea: Do not keep an in-memory root-to-block index for the archived (backfilled) range; look up slot to root in a DB table on demand.
measured_best: 100-200MB memory savings for checkpoint-synced nodes (pr:nimbus#3429)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3099 get_cold_block_root reads slot->root from freezer DB column
beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:234 forwards iterator over frozen columns
impact: No in-memory index of archived range exists; lookups go to DB.

title: No delta encoding before general compression
idea: Do not delta-encode balances in stored state snapshots when a general compressor (Snappy) is applied anyway; the delta pass costs much more CPU on load than it saves.
measured_best: Database load 129ms -> 12.5ms (10x faster), no compression gain (pr:nimbus#2397)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:385 balances delta is state-to-state diff then zstd
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2143 snapshots stored as plain SSZ + zstd, no delta
note: Snapshots are stored without any delta pass (zstd only); the per-state balance delta is inherent to diffs, so the Nimbus anti-pattern does not occur.
impact: None: snapshots already use only a general compressor; the balance delta in HDiff is between states (needed for diffs), not an intra-state delta before compression.

title: Store base columns plus proofs, reconstruct extensions
idea: For finalized data column sidecars, keep only the base half of the columns plus the KZG proofs of the extension columns, and reconstruct the extension half on demand via erasure coding. This roughly halves column storage.
measured_best: 508 GB to ~259.67 GB for 14 target blobs supernode (pr:teku#10137)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8411 supernodes skip the custody retain and persist every column
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985 put_data_columns writes each full DataColumnSidecar as SSZ
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2679 get_data_column reads stored bytes only, no reconstruction on read
gap: Supernodes store all 128 columns. Store the base half plus extension-column KZG proofs after finalization and rebuild the extension half on read (reuse the data availability checker reconstruction) in the get_data_column / by-range / by-root serving paths.
impact: About half of supernode column storage (Teku: 508 GB to 260 GB at 14 blobs); CPU cost on serving extension columns; supernodes only.
refute_note: Checked the import path that chooses which columns to store (beacon_chain.rs block_data_to_store) and searched store and beacon_chain for any reconstruct-on-read or half-column storage; none found.

title: Per-index diff for validator and builder registries
idea: When diffing states, diff list registries (validators, builders, balances) per index and store only (index, change) for changed entries, leaving a small remainder to a generic binary delta. Much faster and smaller than a generic byte diff of the whole list.
measured_best: hdiff n=1M, 1000 mutated: ~354ms -> ~27ms; n=2M: ~814ms -> ~54ms; diff size slightly smaller (pr:lighthouse#6556)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:439 ValidatorsDiff::compute emits (index, changed fields) only for changed validators, then zstd
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:385 CompressedU64Diff for balances/inactivity_scores
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:329 xdelta3 only for the remaining state bytes
impact: Already done (PR 6556 present).

title: Persist archive/checkpoint states periodically during sync
idea: During initial or range sync, write archive/checkpoint states to the DB at a fixed epoch interval instead of only at migration, so cold storage fills incrementally and a restart does not lose sync progress.
measured_best: Avoids losing 2+ hours of sync progress (pr:lodestar#2151)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2103 store_cold_state called from migration at finalization
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1741 store_hot_state_diffs stores hot state diffs/snapshots on import

note: Lighthouse imports synced blocks through the normal pipeline and persists hot state snapshots/diffs at hierarchy points, so there is no in-memory-only sync progress to lose; the problem is specific to the other clients' design.
impact: Little: blocks and hot state snapshots/diffs are written on import so a restart resumes from the DB; cold states are produced by finalization migration.

title: Split hot and finalized databases, prune non-canonical
idea: Keep unfinalized blocks/states in a hot DB or tables and finalized data in a separate archive DB with its own schema and tuning, deleting non-canonical hot data at finalization. Disk holds only the finalized chain plus live forks, and sparse finalized state storage becomes possible.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:66 separate cold_db, hot_db and blobs_db
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db deletes non-canonical states/blocks at finalization
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:645 abandoned-fork block pruning
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3532 migrate_database moves finalized states to cold with hierarchical diffs
impact: Already done.

title: Do not store historic finalized states by default
idea: Offer (and default to) a storage mode that drops finalized historic states instead of archiving them, with no or optional restore points, cutting disk usage and write load for non-archive nodes.
evidence: beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1301 --archive flag opt-in for all states
beacon_node/src/config.rs:603 archive only when flag set
impact: Default non-archive nodes do not keep all historic states.

title: Offline tool to prune historic states/blocks in place
idea: Provide a command that deletes unneeded historic states and blocks from an existing database in place, reclaiming disk without a resync.
measured_best: 50G to 1.0G on disk (pr:nimbus#1593)
evidence: database_manager/src/lib.rs:406 prune_states in-place subcommand
impact: Already available as lighthouse db prune-states.

title: Resume pruning from a persisted cursor in bounded steps
idea: Track the last pruned slot or earliest stored slot (persisted watermark or in-memory) and start each prune run right after it, scanning only newly eligible ranges and deleting a bounded amount per step, instead of rescanning from slot zero or over tombstones. This lowers prune CPU, memory and startup delay.
measured_best: Prune run avg 0.66s vs 3.99s; beacon RSS 9.60 GB vs 13.58 GB (pr:lodestar#10216)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3296 persisted DataInfo.oldest_data_slot is the blob/column prune cursor
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3313 start_epoch..end_epoch window, run only each epochs_per_blob_prune
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3359 iteration walks back from end block and stops at first already-pruned block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3144 payload pruning stops early if already pruned (finalized_payloads_are_pruned)
impact: Prune runs scan only the newly eligible range; deletion per run is not capped but the range is small.

title: Forwards freezer iterator for historic root lookups
idea: Resolve historic block and state roots by slot with a forwards iterator over freezer restore-point data instead of reverse-iterating from the head, which materialises many states and spikes memory.
measured_best: memory spike 400mb to 800mb+ avoided; response from ~1-2s to near instant (informal) (pr:lighthouse#2376)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3099 per-slot BeaconBlockRoots column in freezer
beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:234 HybridForwardsIterator reads frozen range forwards
impact: Historic root lookups hit the DB directly, no state materialisation for frozen range.

title: Store data column sidecars as flat files
idea: Store data column sidecars as flat files outside the KV DB (for example all columns of a block in one file with an offset table, in epoch directories), and prune by deleting whole files or directories. This avoids DB compaction and inode exhaustion and allows partial column reads.
measured_best: "over 16 million files" with old design (pr:prysm#15061)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:144 get_data_column_key = block_root ++ column index KV key
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:261 DBColumn::BeaconDataColumn
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:275 blobs_db is a separate BeaconNodeBackend (leveldb/redb) instance
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1353 per-key DeleteKey on prune
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3398 pruning iterates per-column keys
gap: No flat-file sidecar store. Add a per-epoch directory file store (one file per block with offset table) behind put_data_columns/get_data_column/prune paths in hot_cold_store, replacing the BeaconDataColumn KV column in blobs_db; prune by unlinking epoch dirs.
impact: Removes per-key deletes and leveldb/redb compaction on the blob DB; enables partial column reads. Lighthouse already isolates columns in a separate blobs_db, so compaction does not touch hot/cold state DBs; real gain is uncertain.
refute_note: Checked store/src/database (only leveldb_impl, redb_impl), all fs::create_dir_all/File writes in beacon_node (only debug SSZ dumps and network dirs), and the blob pruning path. Only related mechanism is the separate blobs_db KV instance, which is not a flat-file store.

title: Do not preload all block summaries at startup
idea: Read block summaries from the database on demand instead of loading all of them into memory at startup.
measured_best: RSS 1.56 GiB -> 1.11 GiB; DAG load 6m45s -> 7m00s (pr:nimbus#3164)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:539 load_hot_state_summaries only used at finalization
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3003 per-root summary read on demand
impact: No startup preload of all block summaries; fork choice restored from persisted proto-array.

title: Lazy branch nodes for reloaded tree states
idea: When loading a finalized state stored as tree nodes, create lazy branch nodes that fetch children from the DB only on access instead of loading the full tree.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state/as_state work on SSZ bytes
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2235 load_cold_state_as_snapshot deserializes whole SSZ state
note: States are persisted as SSZ snapshots plus diffs, not as tree nodes keyed by hash, so lazy branch loading has no counterpart.
impact: None: Lighthouse does not store states as DB-resident tree nodes; milhouse trees are built from SSZ bytes.

title: Persist decompressed BLS pubkeys
idea: Persist decompressed BLS pubkeys alongside the finalized checkpoint (and write finalized state in batches) so restarts skip expensive pubkey decompression.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:60 load_from_store reads DatabasePubkey per index
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:209 DatabasePubkey holds PUBLIC_KEY_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES_LEN bytes
impact: Already done: restart loads uncompressed pubkeys from the store instead of decompressing.

title: Persist derived light-client data in the DB
idea: Store light-client bootstrap and update data (sync committees, epoch-boundary headers) in a small DB table at finalization so they are served without historic states or block replay after restart or pruning.
measured_best: "A full database with default settings (129 periods) uses <15 MB disk" (pr:nimbus#3823)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:212 store_current_sync_committee persists sync committee+branch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:396 bootstrap built from persisted parts
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:831 LightClientUpdate column
impact: Light client data persisted so bootstrap/updates are served without historic states.

title: Presize state-diff serialization buffer
idea: Compute the serialized size of a state diff first and allocate the output buffer at that capacity, avoiding repeated growth and copies for large registries.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:198 compress_bytes presizes output via estimate_compressed_size (len/2)
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:390 CompressedU64Diff::compute builds uncompressed_bytes with flat_map().collect(), no exact capacity
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state uses as_ssz_bytes (presized by ssz)
gap: Presize uncompressed_bytes in CompressedU64Diff::compute (ys.len()*8) and the ValidatorsDiff buffer, and size the compressed output from a better estimate; currently only the compressed Vec is presized with a fixed factor 2.
impact: Small cut in allocation/copy churn when computing hdiffs at snapshot/diff boundaries during migration; background-thread work, not on the block-import path.

title: Pool compression decoders, share one low-memory encoder
idea: Reuse zstd/compression decoders from a pool instead of creating one per call, and use a single shared, reset encoder with a small window instead of pooling large encoders. This bounds memory while keeping read throughput.
measured_best: Decoder pool gave 2x throughput; encoder pool caused high memory (pr:caplin#16023)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:198-213 compress_bytes/decompress_bytes create a fresh zstd Encoder/Decoder per call
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2152 Encoder::new per snapshot write
no pool anywhere in beacon_node (grep Decoder::/Encoder::)
gap: Keep a reusable zstd Decompressor (or bulk::Decompressor) per thread or in a pool and use it in StoreConfig::decompress_bytes; optionally share one reset encoder for compress_bytes.
impact: Cuts per-call zstd context allocation on historic state loads (HTTP state queries, reconstruction); modest, probably single-digit percent of diff apply time.

title: Leaner state diffs: whole small fields, parallel shuffle
idea: In the historical state diff store, store tiny fields (inactivity scores, slashings) whole instead of as diffs, reconstruct the previous epoch without DB reads, and compute shuffled sets in parallel.
measured_best: removed 15GB; dumps 2048 to 1024 added 5GB; 2x faster participation reads (pr:caplin#8963)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state: whole state SSZ goes through xdelta BytesDiff; only balances, inactivity_scores, validators, historical lists are split out
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:385 inactivity_scores use CompressedU64Diff (diffed, not whole)
gap: Lighthouse does not keep a per-field store with participation/slashings diff tables; the idea is specific to Caplin's per-field layout. The only transferable bit (store inactivity scores whole) is a tuning of CompressedU64Diff with unclear gain.
impact: Not applicable to the single-blob hdiff design; no clear mainnet saving.

title: Memoize deserialized diff anchor states
idea: Cache the deserialized anchor/snapshot state per diff level (invalidated on replacement) instead of deserializing it on every reconstruction, and snapshot resume states periodically.
measured_best: avoids ~410k full state deserializations on mainnet walk (pr:prysm#17292)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/historic_state_cache.rs:12 HistoricStateCache LRU of hdiff_buffers and states by slot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2424 load_hdiff_buffer_for_slot checks cache before recursing to the snapshot
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:27 cold hdiff buffer cache size 16
impact: Already done; anchors are cached as hdiff buffers (near-SSZ form), and put_both caches the snapshot state. Cache is keyed by slot, entries are immutable so invalidation is unneeded.

title: Point lookups for strided block range requests
idea: For blocks-by-range with step > 1, fetch archived blocks by slot point lookups instead of streaming the whole range.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/methods.rs:448 step field kept only for v1 compat
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:1319 get_block_roots_from_store uses forwards root iterator, then blocks fetched by root
impact: None on mainnet; strided requests are essentially not issued.

title: Prune contiguous key ranges with one range delete
idea: When pruning finalized data (blocks, signatures, states, data columns), lay keys out so the doomed rows form one contiguous range and delete it with a single range-delete instead of iterating and deleting key by key. One tombstone replaces thousands, so pruning cost stops scaling with chain height and later seeks do not crawl over tombstones.
measured_best: States grew ~150 MiB per snapshot, ~33 GiB/day, previously never pruned (pr:ethlambda#683)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:99 KeyValueStore only has delete_batch(HashSet keys) and delete_if, no range delete
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:262 delete_batch writes one tombstone per key
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:272 delete_if scans the whole column and deletes matching keys one by one
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:284 redb delete_batch uses table.retain over all keys
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs per-key deletes
gap: No DeleteRange op in KeyValueStoreOp or in either backend (C LevelDB has no native DeleteRange; redb has range-based retain_in/extract_from_if). Blob/column keys are by block root, so a range delete also needs slot-prefixed keys.
impact: Fewer tombstones and less compaction during blob/column and state pruning; small steady-state saving.
refute_note: Also checked delete_if in leveldb/redb/memory backends and its callers: it is a full-column scan with per-key deletes, not a range delete.

title: Delete secondary index entries together with pruned blocks
idea: When pruning archived blocks, also delete every secondary index entry (slot, root, parent-root indexes) in the same range delete, so no orphaned index keys accumulate on disk.
measured_best: ~80 bytes per block of leftover index keys (pr:lodestar#10110)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3249-3470 only blobs/columns are pruned; blocks are kept forever
consensus/types/src/core/chain_spec.rs:297 min_epochs_for_block_requests exists but is not used by any pruning
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs DBColumn: blocks are keyed by root only, no slot or parent-root secondary index
gap: Lighthouse never prunes finalized blocks and has no slot/parent-root secondary index columns for blocks, so there are no orphaned index keys. Blob pruning deletes by block root key, the only key.
impact: Nothing to gain today; becomes relevant only if block pruning is added.

title: Shorten block retention window after new forks
idea: Recompute the block retention/serving window from the new fork's churn parameters (e.g. ~8192 or ~14299 epochs instead of 33024) so the pruning cutoff keeps far fewer historical blocks, and cap blocks pruned per run so the larger catch-up prune does not stall.
measured_best: window 33024 -> 8192 epochs (~36 days) (pr:lodestar#10518)
evidence: consensus/types/src/core/chain_spec.rs:297 min_epochs_for_block_requests field present, grep shows no use outside spec parsing

beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs only handles blobs and data columns, window from min_epochs_for_blob/data_column_sidecars_requests (canonical_head.rs:1651, hot_cold_store.rs:3250)
no block pruning mode in database_manager/src/cli.rs
gap: Lighthouse would need a block-pruning pass (e.g. alongside try_prune_blobs) that deletes finalized blocks older than a window computed from the current fork's churn limits, with a per-run cap. Blob/column cutoff already follows spec constants, but blocks are never pruned.
impact: Pruning blocks beyond ~36 days would cut hundreds of GB on a full-history node (blocks are ~tens of GB per year on disk plus freezer growth); no effect on CPU.

title: Reuse stored block roots instead of re-hashing
idea: When archiving or pruning finalized blocks, read roots from the DB keys or the root-to-slot index rather than recomputing hash_tree_root for each block.
measured_best: Switching a synced mainnet node from prune to minimal took about 80 minutes with no visible impact on block import (pr:teku#6606)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3366 try_prune_blobs walks with ParentRootBlockIterator: block roots come from parent_root links starting at a known root, not hash_tree_root
beacon_node/store/src/iter.rs:243 ParentRootBlockIterator
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs: migration uses roots from fork choice/state roots, no canonical_root of blocks (grep found none)
impact: Already avoids per-block re-hashing in pruning and migration paths.

title: Delete data violating current retention on mode change
idea: At startup or after switching storage mode (archive to prune/minimal), scan for stored finalized states that the current retention policy would not keep, delete them in batches, and compact the affected range so the disk space is actually reclaimed.
measured_best: Extra states accounted for 50GB of 120GB DB on Prater nodes (pr:lodestar#4526)
evidence: database_manager/src/lib.rs:406 prune_states and hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states delete all freezer states then compact_freezer
no startup scan that detects states violating the current retention/hierarchy config
hot_cold_store.rs:382 TODO(tree-states) about pruning advanced states
gap: Only a manual `lighthouse db prune-states --confirm` that deletes everything exists; there is no automatic cleanup on a mode or hierarchy-exponents change at startup, and no partial (batched) deletion of just the non-conforming states. Add a startup check in HotColdDB::open that compares stored layers with hierarchy_config and deletes in batches plus compact_column.
impact: Reclaims disk after config changes (could be tens of GB on archive nodes); no runtime CPU effect.

title: Stream-copy DB files instead of reading into memory
idea: When copying or restoring large DB files, stream through the filesystem rather than reading the whole file into memory, avoiding OOM.
measured_best: prevents OOMs during database restoration (pr:prysm#8708)
evidence: database_manager/src/lib.rs: no backup/restore or file-copy command (grep copy/backup/restore found none)
gap: Lighthouse has no DB restore/copy path that reads whole DB files into memory.
impact: None.

title: Independent retention mode for data columns
idea: Give data column sidecars their own retention/archive setting separate from blocks, since columns take an order of magnitude more disk and are not needed for consensus.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:61 one prune_blobs bool
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:63 one epochs_per_blob_prune and blob_prune_margin_epochs shared by blobs and columns
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1046 single --prune-blobs flag
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:52 supernode/semi-supernode only change custody count, not retention
gap: Add a separate column retention setting (prune flag or retention epochs) and use it in the Fulu branch of try_prune_blobs.
impact: Operators can keep or drop columns independently of blobs; disk saving only.
refute_note: Checked all store config fields and CLI flags for column-specific retention; only custody-count flags (supernode/semi-supernode) affect column disk usage, which is not a retention mode.

title: Separate storage queue for column sidecar queries
idea: Route heavy data column sidecar reads through their own async channel/queue so they do not stall block and state storage operations.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:68 blobs_db is a separate database instance from hot/cold
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:600 DataColumnsByRangeRequest has its own work type and queue
impact: Column sidecar reads already go to their own DB handle and their own beacon processor queue, so they cannot block block/state storage through a shared queue.

title: Throttle peer-driven chain data DB queries
idea: Wrap the chain-data DB client with a concurrency limiter so heavy RPC/peer requests cannot starve the node's own storage access.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/mod.rs:51 MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 2 per peer and protocol
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/inbound_limiter.rs:126 rejects inbound requests over the per-peer concurrency limit
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1715 by-range/by-root handlers run as beacon processor work
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1776 spawn_async/spawn_blocking hold the worker slot (SendOnDrop) until the DB read finishes, so total peer-serving concurrency is bounded by max_workers
gap: Peer-driven DB reads are bounded indirectly (per-peer concurrency 2, rate quotas, global max_workers shared with own work, low-priority queues), but there is no dedicated limiter that reserves storage capacity for the node's own access; add a semaphore around store reads in the by-range/by-root handlers.
impact: Marginal: less DB contention during heavy peer serving.
refute_note: Found the per-peer inbound concurrency limiter and confirmed beacon processor worker slots are held for the whole request, which is an indirect global cap; still no DB-level limiter.

title: Serve historical blocks from ERA files
idea: Read historical/finalized blocks (and the checkpoint state) directly from ERA files with an index instead of importing them into the DB or downloading a checkpoint, saving DB storage.
evidence: no e2store/era/era1 crate in Cargo.lock and no ERA reader in any .rs file (grep)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/historical_blocks.rs:84 import_historical_block_batch only imports network batches
gap: Needs an ERA (e2store) reader with index and a fallback block/state source in HotColdDB and backfill/checkpoint loading.
impact: Could avoid storing/backfilling historical blocks (hundreds of GB) and speed up initial backfill.
refute_note: Searched the whole tree and Cargo.lock for era/e2store/era1 names and dependency crates; none present.

title: Skip redundant CRC and buffer zeroing on loads
idea: When loading blocks/states from DB or ERA files, skip CRC32 checks already done by the storage layer and avoid zero-initialising read buffers.
measured_best: CRC32 check cost ~50ms per 110MB state load (pr:nimbus#5207)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:198-216 zstd encoder/decoder, no frame checksum enabled (zstd default off), output Vec::with_capacity not zero-filled
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2176-2179 read_to_end into with_capacity buffer, no zeroing
impact: Nothing left to gain; at most the storage-engine checksum remains, ~50ms per 110MB state at best.

title: Reuse existing states when archiving finalized states
idea: When storing finalized state snapshots (e.g. after long non-finality), first check whether the state already exists in memory or the DB and use it, instead of regenerating it by block replay.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1812 get_hot_state checks state_cache by state root first
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3606 migrate_database loads hot state (cache hit if present) and only for diff-boundary slots
impact: Finalized snapshots reuse cached states and skip non-boundary slots; no regeneration by replay unless the cache misses.

title: Skip archiving blobs/columns outside retention window
idea: When archiving finalized blocks during sync, do not write blobs or data columns that are already outside the data-availability retention window.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1311 data_columns_required_for_epoch gates column download by epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1314 blobs_required_for_epoch gates blobs
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:268 complete_blob_backfill opt-in beyond window
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/historical_blocks.rs:230 get_blobs_or_columns_store_op writes only delivered data
impact: Backfill does not request or write blobs/columns outside the DA window unless --complete-blob-backfill is set.

title: Coarser default spacing of full state snapshots
idea: Raise the default interval between stored full states (restore points), trading slower historical state reconstruction for several times less freezer disk and writes.
measured_best: reduces disk usage by 32x, historical queries under 10s (pr:lighthouse#790)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:622 default hierarchy exponents [5,9,11,13,16,18,21]: full snapshot every 2^21 slots
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:746 --slots-per-restore-point deprecated, no effect
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:20 legacy DEFAULT_SLOTS_PER_RESTORE_POINT const unused
impact: Hierarchical state diffs replaced restore points; full snapshots are far sparser than the old 8192-slot default.

title: Migrate hot-to-cold state diffs in one pass

title: Split large prunes into many small transactions
idea: Delete large ranges of old data in bounded chunks, each in its own write transaction, instead of one huge transaction. The writer lock is not held for the whole prune, and the store does not rebalance or crash after a massive commit.

Chunk the ops Vec in these functions (e.g. 1 epoch or N thousand ops per do_atomically).

title: Spread pruning over slots instead of epoch bursts

After a finality gap, one run deletes the whole range in one atomic batch. Only the reconstruction step is chunked (BLOCKS_PER_RECONSTRUCTION).

title: Apply store updates in memory before disk write
idea: Apply block-import and finalization updates to the in-memory store immediately and write them to disk asynchronously, keeping references to pending data to avoid read-before-write races. Block import does not wait on storage I/O.
evidence: beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:~4750 import_block calls store.do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache(ops) synchronously, fork choice write lock held until it returns

gap: Block import writes block, state diff and blobs to disk synchronously before releasing the fork choice write lock and declaring the block imported; only the state cache is updated in memory first. To copy Teku, import would hand the KV batch to a background writer, serve reads from a pending-writes overlay, and release fork choice before the write finishes. This conflicts with the explicit crash-consistency design (fork choice must not be ahead of disk, issue 2028).
impact: Removes the DB write (BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE, tens of ms, more on diff slots) from the import critical path and fork choice write lock, at the cost of crash-consistency risk; modest gain.

refute_note: Verified the eth1 deposit cache is gone from the tree, so the deposit half is moot; milhouse structural sharing reduces per-state validator memory but is not disk-backed.

title: Persist pending unknown-parent blocks on disk
idea: Store blocks waiting for an unknown parent in the DB with only an in-memory index of roots, instead of holding full blocks in memory during long non-finality.
measured_best: not sustainable in memory during non-finality (pr:lodestar#1670)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:77 MAX_LOOKUPS=200
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:408 lookup rejected when at cap
impact: Negligible; memory is already bounded.

title: Periodic hot state snapshots to bound replay
idea: Persist full hot (unfinalized) states only at regular intervals (every N slots or epochs, for example every epoch or every other epoch, also during sync and long non-finality) and rebuild other states by replaying blocks from the nearest snapshot. This bounds hot DB size and write volume as well as the replay cost on restart or state regeneration.
measured_best: cuts hot DB state storage by a factor of SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (32) (pr:lighthouse#746)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1727 store_hot_state_summary writes a summary for every state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1752 store_hot_state_diffs: Snapshot/DiffFrom only on hierarchy layer slots, ReplayFrom stores nothing more
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1949 load_hot_state replays from nearest stored base (ReplayFrom)
impact: Already bounds hot state storage and restart replay; nothing to gain.

title: Store only hot blocks, regenerate hot states
idea: Do not persist each new unfinalized state on import; store only hot blocks and regenerate hot states by replaying from the finalized (or migrated) state, leaving state persistence to the finalization migration. This trades CPU for disk and write volume.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1741 store_hot_state_diffs: ReplayFrom slots persist only the summary, layer slots get a diff or snapshot
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:660 storage_strategy returns ReplayFrom for slots that are not on a diff layer, so those states are rebuilt by block replay
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:407 hot_storage_strategy uses the anchor (finalized) slot as the hot hdiff start snapshot
gap: Most hot states already cost only a summary and are rebuilt by replay, but Lighthouse still writes hdiffs at every lowest-layer slot (each epoch with default exponents) and snapshots at higher layers during import. Making hot persistence summary-only, with replay from the finalized state, would need a hot-only hierarchy with no diff layers below the anchor.
impact: Small: the remaining writes are per-epoch diffs; dropping them adds replay cost during long non-finality.
refute_note: Confirmed that the hot hdiff design already gives the replay path for non-layer slots (StorageStrategy::ReplayFrom). The hierarchy exponents are shared by hot and cold (cli hierarchy-exponents), and I found no hot-only config that turns off hot diffs.

title: Skip no-op DB deletes and empty transactions
idea: Do not issue DB deletes for keys known to be absent, and do not open or commit a transaction or storage update when the write batch is empty.
measured_best: removed 20k key encodings and level db searches per block (pr:lodestar#1409)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1376-1420 DeleteState picks snapshot/diff/none by slot via hot_storage_strategy (avoids some absent-key deletes)
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3405 prune_blobs checks key_exists before queuing delete

store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:155-189 do_atomically opens write tx and commits even for empty batch; leveldb_impl.rs:143-168 writes empty Writebatch
gap: Add early return `if ops_batch.is_empty()` in leveldb/redb do_atomically (and skip blobs_db write in do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache when kv_blob_ops empty); in migrate prune only queue Delete ops for columns known present (fork/slot based). DeleteBlobs also does a get_blobs read first.
impact: Small per-block saving: avoids an empty redb write tx (with fsync cost under redb) on every block import, and a few hundred tombstone writes per finalization; leveldb deletes are cheap so likely sub-ms to ms.

title: Get state root from next block in replay
idea: During block replay, load one extra block to read the state root it commits to instead of tree-hashing the replayed state.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:183 get_state_root takes root from prev block
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:222 extra leading block used only for its state root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2530 load_blocks_to_replay includes block at start slot for its state root
impact: Replay avoids tree-hashing the state at block slots; already done.

title: Blob sidecars as files with atomic rename
idea: Store blob sidecars as individual files written to a temporary file and atomically renamed, instead of in the key-value DB, keeping writes crash-safe without DB overhead.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:275 blobs_db opened as BeaconNodeBackend (LevelDB/redb)
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:36 and redb_impl.rs:28 are the only backends
gap: There is no file-per-sidecar storage. Blobs and data columns go to a separate KV instance. A filesystem backend with temp-file plus rename would have to sit behind put_blobs/get_blobs/delete and pruning.
impact: Low: blobs are already in their own DB, so this would mostly remove compaction write amplification on that DB.
refute_note: Searched beacon_node and common for fs::rename and tempfile persist use: the only hits are test mocks and account_utils, none in the store. The store has only the leveldb and redb backends.

title: Epoch-keyed blob directory layout with summary
idea: Lay out blob files as period/epoch/root/index and keep an in-memory summary per block root (epoch plus index mask), so startup warmup and pruning list epoch directories instead of reading every sidecar.
measured_best: order of magnitude faster cache warm up time and sub-ms pruning times (pr:prysm#14023)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3340-3430 prune_blobs walks back from end block until an already-pruned block, only touching newly expired blocks
store/src/lib.rs:259 BeaconBlob column in KV DB keyed by block root
impact: Blobs/columns live in a KV database (no file tree), there is no startup cache warm-up and pruning only visits the newly expired range, so a directory layout does not apply.

title: One KV instance for hot and finalized data
idea: Keep hot and finalized data as column families or tables in one key-value store instance instead of two, so each instance's native caches and buffers are not duplicated and a write that touches both is one atomic transaction.
measured_best: "should reduce native memory consumption by ~500Mb" (pr:teku#2934)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:270 hot_db = BeaconNodeBackend::open(hot_path)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:284 cold_db opened separately at cold_path
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:30 each redb backend is its own database file
gap: Hot, cold and blobs are three separate KV instances, and the redb backend does not share one either. Merging them would need one instance with column prefixes or tables, a datadir migration, and an atomic migrate_database.
impact: A few hundred MB of native cache, and an atomic finalization migration; no CPU gain.
refute_note: Checked HotColdDB::open and both backend constructors: every instance is opened on its own path. Neither backend shares a cache or an environment between instances.

title: Resolve block slot without loading block or state
idea: Answer root-to-slot queries (for example in state pruning) from fork choice, a slot index, a state summary or the block instead of decoding the full state, so callers that need only the slot do not load large objects.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3867 HotStateSummary stores slot, latest_block_slot, previous_state_root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3003 load_hot_state_summary gives slot without loading state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:537 prune_hot_db builds DAG from summaries, never loads states
impact: State/block pruning and slot lookups already use summaries, not full states.

title: Defer pruning until block-processing cascade ends
idea: Run heavy state and block pruning only after a cascade of pending child blocks finishes processing, so states just computed for those children are not deleted and recomputed.
measured_best: Fixes devnet loop at 100% CPU (pr:ethlambda#240)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:310 run_migration on finalization in background thread, prune_hot_db at :509 only deletes states not descendant of finalized checkpoint
gap: Lighthouse prunes on finalization in a separate migrator thread and removes only non-viable forks and pre-finalization states, never states of pending child blocks; there is no block-processing cascade that would invalidate freshly computed states.

title: Clean up temporary hot states and their flags
idea: Clear the temporary flag on stored advanced pre-states correctly, delete a state's temporary flag whenever the state is deleted, and prune hot states older than the split slot by scanning hot state summaries. Advanced states and stale flags then do not accumulate on disk or need garbage collection at startup.
measured_best: "Garbage collecting 223069 temporary states" at startup (problem) (pr:lighthouse#6422)
evidence: store/src/lib.rs:304-307 BeaconStateTemporary column deprecated, temporary-state flag no longer used
beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:455 advanced state written with put_state (gets a hot summary)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:690-795 prune_hot_db builds states_to_prune from hot summaries DAG and queues DeleteState for all not on finalized/descendant chain
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1376 DeleteState removes summary + snapshot/diff
impact: Temporary flags no longer exist and advanced states are pruned via summary DAG at finalization, so no startup GC of ~200k states.

title: Avoid a global or redundant store lock
idea: Do not serialize unrelated DB operations on one global store mutex or an outer lock around an already thread-safe DB handle: remove it where atomicity is guaranteed elsewhere, or give small disk I/O paths their own lock so they do not wait behind large state writes.
measured_best: state dump 420 ms p50 vs envelope 0.2-3.6 ms (contention avoided) (pr:caplin#25436)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:52-90 HotColdDB has no global store mutex; hot_db/cold_db/blobs_db are plain handles
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1057-1064 put_payload_envelope writes straight to hot_db without a lock
store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:14 only RwLock around redb handle (read for writes)
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:74-87 only cache mutexes, not held across state writes
impact: Global/redundant store lock already removed (lighthouse#7311) and small writes go directly to the DB.

title: Retention pruning during finality stalls
idea: When finalization does not advance, still prune states, blocks and attestation tables older than max(finalized, head - window) on head updates, protecting head/justified/finalized and evicting orphans whose parents never arrive, so storage does not grow without bound.
measured_best: Estimated 10,800 states x 100+ MB after 12h without finalization; closed unmerged (pr:ethlambda#175)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2860 POST lighthouse/finalize manual finalization endpoint
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1837 manually_finalize_state sends ManualFinalizationNotification
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:292 run_manual_migration runs full run_migration/prune_hot_db at an unfinalized checkpoint
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3307 blob pruning also capped by split slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:310 automatic migration only on finalization
gap: Lighthouse has an operator-triggered equivalent (POST /lighthouse/finalize) that migrates and prunes the hot DB at a chosen unfinalized checkpoint during a stall, but nothing automatic: no head-driven retention window that prunes old hot states/blocks while finality is stuck. Blob pruning is also capped by the split, so it stalls too. Missing: an automatic head-window prune in migrate.rs that keeps head/justified/finalized and fork-choice nodes.
impact: Bounds hot DB growth in long non-finality without operator help; hdiff storage and the manual endpoint already reduce the need.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review I found the manual finalization HTTP endpoint and its migrator path, which prune the hot DB during non-finality when an operator calls them. I also checked that blob pruning is bounded by the split slot.

title: Prune hot states older than finalization
idea: When a new checkpoint finalizes, delete hot-DB states older than the finalized slot (including boundary states), optionally keeping only sparse periodic states, and enable this by default so state storage stays bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:640 states_to_prune: everything not descendant of finalized checkpoint, except sparse hdiff layer points (required_finalized_diff_state_slots)
impact: Hot state storage is already bounded by finalization, keeping only sparse hierarchy states.

title: Optional pruning of historical states
idea: Make deletion of historical (cold) states not needed for the node's mode available, as a configurable option or an offline command, trading availability of old states for much less disk usage.
measured_best: takes a few seconds max on mainnet (pr:lighthouse#4835)

impact: Already lets a node drop historical states offline; disk saving only for nodes that wanted them.

title: Run metric column scans off the pruning path
idea: Run full O(N) column count scans used only for metrics on a separate low-priority task, not at the end of the pruning cycle, so pruning is not delayed by minutes.
measured_best: scans "can take minutes on large databases" (pr:teku#11171)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:456-506 store metrics set only in-memory gauges (caches, anchor info)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs: no column count scans at end of pruning
impact: Lighthouse does not run O(N) column-count scans for metrics, so there is nothing to move off the pruning path.

title: Partial state getters and cached state hash
idea: Give callers getters for single state fields (validators, balances) and a cached state hash, so they do not clone or rehash the whole state.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3070 update_tree_hash_cache, :1087 canonical_root: hash cache lives inside the state (milhouse)
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs: states cached and cloned cheaply (persistent trees)
impact: Equivalent effect via milhouse structural sharing: state clone is O(1) and root is incremental, so no whole-state clone/rehash.

title: Write-back buffer for state summaries
idea: Buffer state summaries in memory in the DB layer and flush them in one batch (on a count threshold, or with blocks during initial sync) instead of writing each summary on its own.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4751-4756 block, columns and PutState (summary+diff) go in one do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache batch per block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1307 PutState -> store_hot_state; :1722 store_hot_state_summary pushes one op immediately, no cross-block buffer
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1630-1633 each skipped-slot state written in its own hot_db.do_atomically
gap: No write-back buffer: each block import (and each skipped-slot state) is its own DB batch. A buffer would batch summaries across blocks during range sync and serve reads from it; LH already avoids Prysm's original problem (separate summary transaction) by writing the summary in the block's own batch.
impact: Small: summaries are ~100 bytes and already share the block's atomic write; saving is fewer write batches during initial sync only.
refute_note: Checked the block-import op list and StoreOp::PutState handling: the summary rides in the same batch as the block, which covers the 'with blocks' half of the Prysm idea, but there is no in-memory summary buffer or count-threshold flush anywhere in store/.

title: Persist states only when a block follows
idea: Do not write states produced by empty-slot advancement or attestation-driven processing to the hot DB; store a state only when a block is applied to it. Such states are cheap to recompute, rarely read and bloat the DB.
measured_best: storing states is (very) slow; avoids state database size explosion (pr:nimbus#1860)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:455 put_state of the empty-slot-advanced head state every slot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1068-1076 put_state -> store_hot_state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1750-1760 ReplayFrom slots store only a summary; Snapshot/DiffFrom slots store a full snapshot or hdiff
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1698-1706 skips diff computation if summary already on disk
gap: The state-advance timer still persists the advanced (empty-slot) state each slot; it is a summary on most slots but a diff/snapshot when the advanced slot is a hierarchy boundary. That state is not in chain history when a block does follow at that slot. Drop the put_state in advance_head (or defer it until the slot is known to be empty).
impact: Avoids one summary write per slot and an hdiff/snapshot computation+write at boundary slots on the state-advance thread; DB-size impact is small because of hierarchical storage.
refute_note: Confirmed no attestation-driven path persists states (attestation verification uses shuffling/state caches), and that the hierarchical diff scheme makes most empty-slot writes summary-only, which is the partial mitigation; the advance-timer write remains.

title: Persist committee caches with stored states
idea: Store committee/shuffling caches together with the state in the hot DB so a state loaded from disk does not need a shuffling recompute.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3865-3871 HotStateSummary: slot, block roots, diff base, previous state root only
beacon_node/store/src/: no reference to committee_cache or ShufflingCache in the store crate
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs: in-memory only
gap: Committee caches are neither stored with hot snapshots/diffs nor is ShufflingCache persisted; a state loaded from disk rebuilds committees on demand. Would need an extra column keyed by shuffling id or decision root.
impact: Saves one shuffling compute (~100s of ms) after restart or on a state_cache miss; rare on a running node.
refute_note: Grepped the whole store crate for committee/shuffling persistence and checked the state cache put path; the only committee data persisted is sync committees for light client, not attester shufflings.

title: Persist head, fork choice and eth1 data less often
idea: Write chain metadata (head pointer, fork choice, op pool, eth1 cache, wall-clock time) only when it changes or at coarse points (epoch crossing, every N blocks, shutdown) instead of on every block, attestation or tick. Split large persisted objects so only the changed part is written.
measured_best: "committing less frequently to the database, which should help with contention" (pr:teku#1232)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1564-1566 persist_fork_choice only on epoch transition or reorg
canonical_head.rs:1720 persist at finalization
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8464-8466 op pool, custody context and fork choice persisted on Drop
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:687 head persisted only as genesis root; no eth1 cache or wall-clock persistence
impact: Already coarse: fork choice per epoch/reorg/finality, op pool only at shutdown, head pointer not rewritten per block.

title: Persist data columns on arrival, prune cache after
idea: Write each accepted data column sidecar to disk as soon as it is accepted, and remove it from the in-memory column cache only once persistence is confirmed (with a short retention window). No column is lost to cache pruning and the cache stays bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:351 pending columns held only in an in-memory LruCache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8421 StoreOp::PutDataColumns built only at block import
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985 put_data_columns only called from checkpoint-sync builder (builder.rs:583) and historical backfill (historical_data_columns.rs:121)
gap: Gossip/RPC columns are not written to disk on acceptance; they live in the DA LRU until the block imports, so eviction under load forces refetch. Persisting on arrival needs a hot-DB write in the DA put path plus orphan-column pruning.
impact: Avoids re-download of evicted pending columns; adds disk writes for columns of blocks that may never import; benefit unclear.
refute_note: Enumerated every caller of put_data_columns / data_column_as_kv_store_ops / PutDataColumns: none is on the gossip or RPC acceptance path (the old disk-overflow store of the DA cache is gone).

title: Store previous state root in hot summaries
idea: Store the previous state root in each hot state summary so loading a state from disk needs no tree hashing; reading a few summaries is cheaper than building a tree hash cache.
measured_best: tree hash cache costs 1s+ CPU and 300MB+ RAM; summaries read <250ms for 32 (pr:lighthouse#2954)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3872 HotStateSummary.previous_state_root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3981-3993 filled in HotStateSummary::new
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3859 get_ancestor_state_root walks previous_state_root links without hashing
impact: Already done: state roots found by summary links, no tree hash cache build when loading from disk.

title: Prune orphaned execution payload envelopes
idea: On each finalization, delete hot-DB execution payload envelopes whose block is no longer in fork choice, since the finalized-chain walk never reaches them.
measured_best: Observed 17 stale hot envelopes on a devnet node (pr:lodestar#10206)
evidence: beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:777 blocks_to_prune built from summaries DAG minus finalized/descendant blocks (includes forks no longer in fork choice)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:777-779 pushes DeletePayloadWithSummary per pruned block

impact: Envelopes of abandoned blocks are deleted at each finalization together with their block.

title: Prune blocks older than retention window
idea: Delete blocks and associated data older than a retention tail (e.g. min_epochs_for_block_requests or a weak-subjectivity based tail) from DB and in-memory indexes, so storage does not grow without bound.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3119 try_prune_execution_payloads (finalized payloads deleted, the bulk of post-merge block bytes)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs (blobs past DA boundary)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states (freezer states only, no blocks)
database_manager/src/cli.rs:75 subcommands: PrunePayloads/PruneBlobs/PruneStates, no PruneBlocks
beacon_node/store/src/metadata.rs:99 oldest_block_slot only ever moves down via backfill
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:919 delete_block used only for abandoned forks (migrate.rs pruning)
gap: No retention prune for finalized blocks: once stored, beacon blocks (blinded) below a retention slot are never deleted and oldest_block_slot never moves up. Add a retention prune in the migrator that deletes blinded blocks below e.g. current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS via the cold BeaconBlockRoots index and raises anchor oldest_block_slot (status/blocks_by_range already honour it).

refute_note: Searched store, beacon_chain and database_manager for any block retention/prune (prune_blocks, DeleteBlock callers, anchor oldest_block_slot updates, db subcommands); only payload, blob, freezer-state and abandoned-fork pruning exist.

title: Write intermediate states to DB as temporary
idea: Write intermediate states created during block processing directly to the hot DB marked temporary, clear the mark on success, and garbage-collect leftovers at startup, so they need not be held in memory.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1632 intermediate skip-slot states written via store_hot_state immediately
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:304 BeaconStateTemporary column deprecated
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1741 store_hot_state_diffs writes only summary on replay slots

title: Prune dangling states at startup
idea: At startup, delete states between genesis and the last finalized slot that are not on archive/restore-point boundaries, to shrink the state store.
measured_best: 4000 state keys down to 86 (pr:prysm#4697)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states only for archive-to-hdiff migration, run on user command
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1661 store_hot_state: hot states stored as summaries+diffs, finalization migrates and deletes them
gap: Add a startup pass that scans hot state summaries below the split and deletes those not on a snapshot/diff boundary. Lighthouse already deletes non-boundary hot states at finalization migration, so only legacy leftovers would benefit.
impact: Smaller DB on nodes with leftover states; no runtime speed change. Lighthouse's finalization migration already prunes, so little to gain.

title: Raise DB and open-file resource limits
idea: Raise KV store limits (mmap/initial size) and the process open-file soft limit to the hard limit at startup, so the DB does not stall or crash on default resource limits.
measured_best: crash after days on 1024 limit (pr:ethlambda#422)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:128 fdlimit::raise_fd_limit used only in validator client
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs and redb_impl.rs: no open-files or mmap options set
grep fdlimit/rlimit finds nothing in beacon_node or lighthouse/src

title: Slot-ordered range scans instead of per-key lookups
idea: Iterate slot-ordered DB keys with range filters (gt/lt/reverse/limit, streaming) instead of issuing one lookup per slot or scanning a hash-keyed index, for custody scans, pruning and queries.

idea: When migrating finalized blocks from the hot to the cold/finalized DB, copy the raw stored bytes keyed by the known root (use the DB key as root) instead of deserializing, re-hashing and re-serializing each block.

title: Reuse computed block root when saving blocks
idea: Carry the already computed block root (a wrapper caching hash_tree_root) into the block save path instead of re-hashing the block there.

title: Skip checkpoint state writes during sync
idea: Do not persist checkpoint states while syncing, avoiding large state writes not needed during sync.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:33 MAX_ADVANCE_DISTANCE: 'avoids doing unnecessary work whilst the node is syncing'

gap: Lighthouse's analogue of the Grandine checkpoint state (the head state advanced to the next epoch boundary by the state advance timer, written via put_state) is already not computed or written while syncing. What remains is the block-import path: hot summaries plus hdiff snapshots/diffs at hierarchy boundaries are written during range sync too; deferring the diff part while far behind is possible but migration needs those states.
impact: Remaining gain small: diffs only at hierarchy-boundary slots, and the clock-driven checkpoint state write is already skipped during sync.
refute_note: Checked the state advance timer, which the earlier review missed: it refuses to advance (and thus to persist the advanced epoch-boundary state) when head is >256 slots behind, matching the Grandine commit's is_forward_synced gate on its checkpoint-state append; import-path hot state writes remain unconditional.

title: Reuse fresh DB state instead of checkpoint download
idea: When started with a checkpoint sync URL, reuse the persisted finalized state if it is recent enough relative to the wall clock and skip the download.

impact: Restart with a persisted DB never re-downloads the state; stricter than a recency bound (no staleness check, node just syncs forward from DB).

title: Skip fork pruning with a single head
idea: Skip fork pruning at finalization when there is only one head, since it replays blocks and rebuilds tree hash caches for nothing.
measured_best: 5.5GB allocations in ~1 min (12.8% of total) during Witti sync; pruning vanished from the flamegraph (pr:lighthouse#1268)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db works on state summaries DAG (load_hot_state_summaries, descendants_of, ancestors_of)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:372 call site
gap: The 2020 pruning replayed blocks via head tracker; current pruning is a pure summary-DAG walk with no block replay or tree-hash cache rebuild, so the pathology no longer exists.
impact: None; pruning cost is a DAG over hot summaries, small.

title: Trust local blocks, skip signature work on load
idea: Mark blocks read from the local DB as trusted and skip BLS signature deserialization and checks when loading them; load blocks lazily during state rewinds.
measured_best: 50x startup time improvement, 200x block load time improvement (Initialize DB 187709 ms -> 3815 ms; load block 0.558 -> 0.043 ms) (pr:nimbus#1227)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:663-686 get_blinded_block/get_block_with decode every read with SignedBeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:195-197 Signature deserialize = blst from_bytes (point decompression)
crypto/bls/src/generic_signature.rs:68-74 GenericSignature holds a decoded point, no lazy bytes mode
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:96,571-597 LRU block_cache only avoids re-decoding recently used full blocks
gap: No trusted/lazy decode for DB blocks: every uncached block load decompresses all G2 signatures. A decoder using SignatureBytes on the DB path would be needed. The LRU block cache mitigates repeated loads but is not the mechanism; startup does not replay blocks, so Nimbus's startup gain does not apply.
impact: Tens of microseconds per signature on uncached block loads (RPC serving, replay, migration); minor on a mainnet node.
refute_note: Checked the BLS GenericSignature wrapper for lazy decoding and the store block cache; neither skips signature decompression on a DB read.

title: Smaller in-memory block cache

title: Snappy-compress blocks and states in DB
idea: Compress stored block and state values with snappy by default, shrinking disk size and I/O and speeding sync.
measured_best: 3GB vs 12GB for 4000 epochs; 3-4x sync blocks/sec (pr:nimbus#1169)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:557-560 blinded block stored as raw as_ssz_bytes()

~/.cargo/registry/src/*/leveldb-0.8.6/src/database/options.rs:72 default compression: Compression::No (and store/Cargo.toml:22 uses default-features = false, dropping the leveldb-sys snappy feature)
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:402 state diffs zstd-compressed
gap: States (hdiffs) are zstd-compressed, but blocks, blobs and columns are stored uncompressed and LevelDB's built-in block compression is off (snappy not even compiled in). Enabling LevelDB snappy or zstd-compressing the BeaconBlock column would close it.
impact: Maybe 20-30% smaller block column and less read I/O at small CPU cost; modest since hdiff already dominates savings.
refute_note: Checked the dependency layer the earlier review skipped: the leveldb crate defaults to Compression::No and Lighthouse disables its snappy feature, so there is no hidden storage-engine compression. Enabling LevelDB snappy is an S-effort route needing no schema migration.

title: Compress cached anchor states in memory

title: Separate block header and body tables
idea: Store block headers and bodies separately so header-only code paths (parent lookup, slot scans, pruning) do not read or decode bodies.

title: Avoid redundant Status re-requests
idea: Re-request peer Status only on a slow period (every few slots or epochs), refresh a peer's last-status timestamp on every update, and stop periodic re-requests once synced, instead of re-asking every peer each slot or epoch.

gap: Only difference: Status keeps being re-requested every 5 min once synced instead of stopping; cost is negligible.
impact: About 1 Status per peer per 5 min already; stopping when synced saves a few tiny RPCs per minute.

title: Evict stale peer-tracking sets
idea: Bound or periodically prune side caches and sets of peer ids (every peer ever seen, per-peer side caches) so they do not grow without limit.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:1187-1230 shrink_to_fit bounds banned peers (MAX_BANNED_PEERS) and disconnected peers (MAX_DC_PEERS), called from inject_disconnect at :1172

gap: banned_peers_per_ip keeps one key per IP (IPv6 /56) ever banned; counts go to 0 but the entry stays. Remove the key when the count reaches 0 in BannedPeersCount::remove_banned_peer. sigp PR 10259 (peerdb cache eviction fixes) is still open.

refute_note: Re-read the whole BannedPeersCount impl and shrink_to_fit: no retain/remove on banned_peers_per_ip anywhere, so the leak is real; the main peer map is bounded.

title: Retry peer search quickly after startup
idea: Right after startup, retry peer search with short (about 1s) delays and drop duplicate immediate attempts, so first peers connect in seconds instead of half a minute.

title: Filter ENRs inside the discovery service

title: Discover subnet peers before publishing
idea: Before broadcasting an attestation on a subnet with no known peers, run discovery for that subnet and wait for at least one peer, so the message reaches someone.

title: Reject banned peers before handshake

title: Stop discovery when peer target is reached
idea: Start discovery queries only when there is a free peer slot and the connected (and outbound) peer count is below target, and ease lookup frequency as the target is approached, instead of querying at a fixed fast rate.

title: Cooldown before reconnecting disconnected peers
idea: After a disconnect (longer for serious goodbye reasons), keep the peer in a time-limited ban/cooldown list checked at the swarm layer and by discovery before dialing, so peers are not redialed or accepted in loops while at the limit.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:55 PEER_RECONNECTION_TIMEOUT=600s; line 198 temporary_banned_peers LRUTimeCache

title: Preallocate subnet bitfield decode buffers
idea: When decoding ENR subnet bitfields or set-bit indices, allocate the output once at the right size instead of growing or concatenating intermediate arrays.

title: Prefix-targeted subnet peer search
idea: Search for subnet peers by targeting node ids whose prefix maps to the subnet (deterministic subnet-to-node-id mapping) instead of random targets, so each query finds more subnet peers per request.

title: Protect useful peers from random pruning
idea: Tag in-use or useful peers as protected in the connection manager so that over-limit pruning does not drop them at random and cause churn and redials.

title: Prune non-sync peers while syncing
idea: While not synced, disconnect peers that do not support sync protocols and a share of the lowest-scored sync peers each heartbeat, so slots free up for useful sync peers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1307 prune_excess_peers has no sync-state input

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1237 is_synced_or_advanced only a sort key in custody-subnet pruning
gap: No step disconnects Behind or low-score peers while the local node is syncing. Add a sync-state-aware branch in the PeerManager heartbeat (sync state is already in network_globals) that drops Behind/Unknown peers and a share of the lowest scored peers when SyncingFinalized/SyncingHead. The 'no sync protocol' part has no analogue in eth2.
impact: Could speed initial/catch-up sync when slots are full of unhelpful peers; no steady-state saving; target peer count is high so benefit is uncertain.
refute_note: Also checked network_behaviour.rs, sync/network_context goodbye_peer callers and status relevance checks: only fork/finality relevance disconnects exist, nothing tied to local sync state.

title: Ping peers less often
idea: Ping connected peers at about the rate peers ping us (minutes, not seconds), to cut network work competing for the main thread.

title: Churn peers when head is starved
idea: During long non-finality, detect a starved head and churn extra useless peers while keeping peers far ahead of us, so the node finds peers that can serve it.

gap: No detection of a starved head (head unchanged and behind wall clock) and no extra churn in that state. Add a check in the PeerManager heartbeat that, when starved, prunes extra useless peers below target and exempts peers whose head is far ahead.

idea: Decode ENR attnets/syncnets bitfields with a precomputed byte-to-bits table and no exceptions, instead of the generic SSZ bitvector path.

title: Fetch blobs from EL to build sidecars locally
idea: When a block or first data column sidecar arrives, call engine_getBlobs (V1/V2) to pull its blobs and proofs from the local EL blob pool and build blob or data column sidecars locally. This skips waiting for gossip or downloading from peers, and lets the node publish the sidecars itself.

title: Use getBlobsV4 to build partial columns from sparse blobpools
idea: Call engine_getBlobsV4 to get cells for the blobs the EL has, even when it holds only part of them, and build partial data columns locally. This reduces column downloads from peers when the EL blob pool is sparse.

title: Fetch blobs from EL during range sync too
idea: Also during sync, on the first received column sidecar call getBlobsV2 to build the remaining columns locally, and retry block import once half of the sampled columns are present. The node does not wait for peers to serve every column.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:209-231 getBlobs only after single-block lookup returns MissingComponents
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:960-995 spawn_fetch_block_columns (gossip/RPC/HTTP sources only)

title: SSZ over REST transport for the engine API
idea: Talk to the execution client over REST endpoints with SSZ bodies (optionally HTTP/2, negotiated through capabilities, with JSON-RPC fallback) for newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated, getPayload and getBlobs. Binary SSZ avoids hex-JSON encoding/decoding and roughly halves or better the wire size of large blob payloads; blob responses can be decoded as views without copies.
measured_best: Payload body 4.7x smaller; getBlobsV2 roundtrip 17x faster on average (pr:prysm#16901)
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api/http.rs:661-694 rpc_request sends application/json and decodes JSON only
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api/ contains only auth.rs, http.rs, json_structures.rs, new_payload_request.rs
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api/http.rs:65 capability exchange is JSON-RPC method names only
gap: Add an SSZ REST transport (optionally HTTP/2) next to HttpJsonRpc with capability negotiation and JSON-RPC fallback for newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated, getPayload and getBlobs, plus SSZ request/response types. The listed Lighthouse PRs are not merged in this checkout.
impact: Removes hex-JSON encode/decode and shrinks large blob/payload bodies; reported getBlobsV2 roundtrip up to 17x faster.
refute_note: Checked the request builder for any non-JSON content type and the engine_api module for alternative transports; the only SSZ use in http.rs is decoding deposit/withdrawal request fields inside JSON.

title: SSZ encoding for builder API calls
idea: Use SSZ instead of JSON for builder API getHeader, submitBlindedBlock and validator registration requests and responses, with JSON fallback (for example on 415 or missing headers), and forward the original received SSZ block bytes to the builder without re-serialization. SSZ is smaller and cheaper to encode/decode than JSON.
evidence: beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:380 getHeader Accept prefers SSZ unless disable_ssz
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:263 post_builder_blinded_blocks_v2_ssz sends SSZ body
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:269 blinded_block.as_ssz_bytes() re-encodes
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:257 post_builder_validators uses post_generic (JSON)
beacon_node/builder_client/src/builder_http_client.rs:305 Gloas builder client also SSZ for block submit, no SSZ registration path
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1851 propose_blinded_beacon_block calls the SSZ submit when available
gap: SSZ is used for getHeader responses and blinded block submission with JSON fallback. Missing: SSZ for validator registrations, and forwarding the original SSZ bytes received from the VC instead of re-encoding.
impact: Small: registration bursts get cheaper encoding; skipping a re-encode of a blinded block saves microseconds.
refute_note: Also checked the new Gloas builder_http_client.rs: it adds SSZ bid responses and SSZ block submit, but registrations stay JSON there too and no raw-bytes passthrough exists.

title: Drive EL sync from light-client head
idea: While the beacon chain DAG is behind, pass the light-client head execution block hash to the EL through forkchoiceUpdated (light-client sync on by default). The EL syncs to the wall slot in parallel with the CL forward sync.
evidence: beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:272 light client is server-only (enable_light_client_server)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7180 update_execution_engine_forkchoice sends only the fork-choice head
gap: No light-client consumer or sync-committee follower exists in Lighthouse; while syncing, the EL only gets the CL's own lagging head. Needs a light-client follow component and a fcU path that sends the LC head hash while the CL is behind.
impact: Helps only initial or long-range sync: the EL could sync to the tip in parallel with the CL.
refute_note: Searched network/src/sync and canonical_head/beacon_chain for any light-client bootstrap/update consumer or alternative head hash sent to the EL; found none.

title: Send early forkchoiceUpdated with payload attributes
idea: When a local validator proposes in the next slot, send forkchoiceUpdated with payload attributes ahead of time (one slot early, or immediately when a timely block does not become head) and cache the payload id. Block production then gets an already-built payload instead of waiting for the EL.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1931 prepare_beacon_proposer after every head change
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:217 prepare_beacon_proposer from the late-slot timer

title: Prepare payloads only for imminent local proposals
idea: Send the proposer-preparation forkchoiceUpdated with payload attributes (and the state advance to find the proposer) only when a registered local validator proposes in the next slot, and skip it while the head is far behind the wall slot or optimistic. This avoids wasted EL payload builds and state rewinds for blocks that would not be used.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6757-6764 skips when head older than sync_tolerance_epochs

gap: Missing: no skip while head is optimistic, and the head-too-far-behind threshold is sync_tolerance_epochs (8 epochs) rather than about one slot. Add an optimistic check and a tighter lag bound in prepare_beacon_proposer.
impact: Saves some wasted EL payload builds during sync/optimistic periods; negligible on a healthy mainnet node.

title: Exempt critical builder calls from request throttling
idea: Do not route getHeader and getPayload builder calls through the throttler used for validator registrations, and cap non-critical concurrency, so registration batches cannot delay critical-path calls.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:813 registrations forwarded in own spawned task
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:81 plain reqwest client, no throttler
gap: Lighthouse has no shared throttler between registrations and getHeader/getPayload: registrations are forwarded as a separate task per VC request, so the Teku problem of registrations queueing ahead of critical calls does not exist (concurrency is just uncapped).

title: Send timeout header on builder getHeader
idea: Include a timeout header in the builder getHeader/bid request so the relay knows the deadline and responds in time.

idea: At the start of the epoch transition, make one pass over validators and participation (or pending attestations) to build per-validator status flags (unslashed participating per flag, inclusion distance) and aggregate per-flag balances. Justification, rewards/penalties, inactivity and slashings then read that summary instead of each rescanning attestations or the registry.

title: Flat array copy of validator fields for epoch loops
idea: Copy the validator fields epoch processing reads (effective balance, slashed, activation/exit epochs) into a flat struct array once per transition, and iterate that instead of the tree-backed validator list. Fetch the full validator only when it must be modified.

title: Flat balances array shared across epoch steps
idea: Extract balances once into a flat array in the epoch-processing context, apply rewards, penalties, deposits, consolidations and effective-balance reads on it with plain arithmetic, and write it back to the tree once at the end. Later steps read the array instead of re-reading or writing balances through the state tree per element.

title: Flat or transient inactivity scores with batched write back
idea: Hold inactivity scores in a plain array or fast mutable/transient form for the inactivity update, update them there, and write back changed scores in one batched operation (skip when unchanged). This avoids reading and rebuilding tree paths per validator.

title: Write validators, balances and scores only when values change
idea: In epoch processing (effective-balance updates, balances, registry, inactivity), read validators read-only and take a mutable reference, copy, or dirty mark only when the value actually changes, skipping validators that cannot cross the hysteresis threshold. Unchanged entries stay shared with the parent state and are not rehashed.

title: Hoist per-epoch constants out of validator loops
idea: Compute values that are constant within an epoch (previous epoch, finalized epoch, finality delay, inactivity-leak flag, base_reward/total division, config-derived constants, activation checkpoint) once before the per-validator loop. This avoids repeated getter, lock, division, and copy cost per validator.

title: Compute sqrt of total balance once per epoch

title: Memoize integer sqrt / base reward per increment
idea: Cache the integer square root of total active balance (and the derived base reward per increment) in state/transition caches keyed by its input, so block and epoch processing reuse it across calls; on a miss, Newton iteration can start from the cached value.
measured_best: Above-52-bit sqrt about 2.3x faster; ~55ns old vs ~28-46ns new per op (pr:prysm#12191)

title: Fast exact integer square root

title: Pass total active balance into base reward computation

idea: Compute the epoch shuffling once as a flat array of active indices, cache it by seed/decision root (check the cache before shuffling), and derive committees and attesting indices from it instead of recomputing committees per lookup or per slot.

title: Reuse one hash output for multiple random draws
idea: In compute_shuffled_index-based sampling (sync committee, PTC, proposer selection) compute hash(seed || i/16) once per 16 iterations and reuse its 32 bytes, also caching pivot/source hashes, instead of hashing per candidate.
