title: Preallocated reusable buffers, no per-validator allocations
idea: Hoist allocations out of per-validator epoch loops and keep validator-count-sized arrays (statuses, active indices, balances, inactivity scores, reward buffers) preallocated and reused across epoch transitions and replays, using iterators instead of copying participation arrays or validators. title: Diff-synced flat validator cache across epochs
idea: Keep a persistent flat index-addressed copy of the validator fields and bring it forward by diffing the last synced tree root against the current one, so the epoch-start validator pass is a linear scan that does not degrade as tree nodes scatter.
measured_best: Hoodi 1.59M validators: epoch-start init 29.2 ms to 15.7 ms at epoch 0 and 48.9 ms to 14.1 ms at epoch 900; flat stays about 14-15 ms (commit:lodestar@d7282c7a751d)

But the main pass still walks the validator tree with iter_cow, and the cold rebuild (restart, reorg, loaded state) is a full tree scan. A diff-based sync (milhouse diff between last synced and current root) could feed initialize_epoch_cache.
impact: Only helps cold epoch-cache rebuilds and the tree walk; roughly tens of ms per epoch at 1.5M validators at best.

title: In-order copy-on-write cursor for list writes
idea: Write epoch balance changes through an in-order lazy copy-on-write cursor over the persistent tree list, copying a leaf only on first write and keeping cached hashes for unchanged leaves, instead of buffering updates in a map, sorting and rehashing.

title: Advance committee caches per slot, not in epoch processing
idea: Do not build the next-epoch committee/shuffling caches inside the epoch transition; rotate or build current/next caches during per-slot processing so the epoch transition does not pay for them and cache building is not repeated.

title: Lazily iterate pending deposits/consolidations with early stop
idea: In process_pending_deposits and process_pending_consolidations, walk the state list lazily (batched or via an iterator) and stop as soon as the per-epoch churn limit or first unprocessable entry is reached, instead of materializing the whole list. Cost scales with the processed prefix, not the queue length.

title: Lightweight justification-only balance totals

What is left: BeaconChain::block_root_at_slot (HTTP API block_id by slot and other callers) still falls back to forwards_iter_block_roots_until when the slot is older than the head state's 8192-slot block_roots window. title: Dense per-validator array of compact vote records
idea: Store each validator's latest vote as a compact plain record (or dense parallel arrays with sentinels) in a flat array indexed by validator index, instead of a hash map, interned dedup index, or boxed/SSZ-backed objects. This gives O(1) set/get, fewer allocations and faster delta computation under the fork choice lock.
measured_best: set with pinned messages 61,418 ns/op -> 8.5 ns/op; ~1.66s lock hold per slot removed (pr:caplin#22352)

impact: Already O(1) get/set in a flat array of plain records; no hash map or boxed objects.

title: Single non-throwing lookup for proto-array root-to-index
idea: Do proto-array root-to-index lookups with one map get returning a sentinel or default (e.g. -1/None), instead of contains followed by get, two sequential lookups, or an exception-raising lookup, so hits and misses are cheap.

consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:621 contains_key only in on_block insert path
impact: Hot loop uses one HashMap get per lookup, returning Option; no contains+get or exceptions.

title: No cache rebuild on cloned head state per update
idea: When the head state is cloned for a head change, do not rebuild pubkey/exit caches on each head update; keep or share caches so the ~70ms rebuild is not paid every time.

title: Slot-ordered queued attestations with bulk drain
idea: Keep fork choice's queued (future-slot) attestations ordered or bucketed by slot (e.g. BTreeMap by slot, sorted deque split with partition_point), so dequeuing due votes splits off a prefix in bulk instead of iterating, copying or reallocating the whole queue on every attestation or tick. Removes quadratic CPU when many attestations are gossiped.

title: Cache head in fork choice; serve duties from it
idea: Cache the computed head node (with its payload status) inside fork choice and recompute deltas/scores only at explicit points or when votes or balances changed since the last get_head. Validator duties (attesters, proposers) and block production read the cached head instead of re-running head selection.

gap: Minor: proto_array find_head (proto_array_fork_choice.rs:788) still runs compute_deltas over all validators on every get_head, with no skip when votes and balances are unchanged. Adding a dirty flag in ProtoArrayForkChoice::find_head would skip it.
impact: Duties and block production already use the cached head. A dirty-flag skip would save one O(validators) vote scan per recompute_head (low value, order of ms).

title: Batch attestations into fork choice, recompute head periodically
idea: Collect verified attestations and apply them to fork choice in one batch call (grouped by target, tracking dirty validators), and recompute the head on a timer such as once per slot, instead of one call per attestation that each propagates deltas or recomputes head.

title: Reweight votes at justification from epoch-processing data
idea: When the justified checkpoint changes, reweight all fork-choice votes in one pass using balances and attester data already computed during epoch processing, instead of attaching weights per attestation; also stream blocks during archival.
measured_best: States attestation reweighting "is fast, lots of the work was already done as part of epoch processing"; no numbers (pr:lodestar#1540)

impact: Lighthouse does not attach weights per attestation; weights come from the per-validator vote array and justified balances in one delta pass per get_head, so there is nothing to batch at justification.

title: Stop ancestor walks early, at finalized slot
idea: Iterate fork choice ancestors lazily newest-first and stop at the finalized root/slot, the window start, or the minimum needed (reorg distance, payload counts), instead of collecting or walking the whole chain back to genesis/anchor. Makes queries O(window) rather than O(chain).

idea: Keep the in-memory by-root block index/graph only for the non-finalized portion and serve finalized blocks from an on-disk slot index, so memory does not grow with chain length and startup need not load the finalized index.

title: Cache per-node head viability in proto-array
idea: Cache each proto-array node's viability-for-head result and invalidate on checkpoint change, since during long non-finality the viability check repeatedly walks the unfinalized chain.
measured_best: significant time during non-finality; no numbers (pr:nimbus#6076)
evidence: consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:2251 is_finalized_checkpoint_or_descendant: O(1) fast path compares the node's own finalized/justified (:2279) and unrealized (:2285) checkpoints before walking ancestors
consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:2135 node_is_viable_for_head: called only for leaves (:1413-1416), uses that fast path

consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:1336 filter_node_tree: reverse single pass over all nodes from justified index, allocates invalid_payloads HashSet, excluded vec and per-node child vecs each call
gap: The costly part of the Nimbus problem (each leaf walking the unfinalized chain to prove it descends from finality) is already short-circuited in O(1) when the leaf's own checkpoint fields match the store's finalized checkpoint, which is the normal case in non-finality. Not done: viability is not cached between get_head calls. Each call rebuilds the filtered node tree in O(nodes since justified), with HashSet and Vec allocations. A cache keyed on (current_epoch, justified, finalized) and invalidated on on_block or an execution-status change would remove that rebuild.

refute_note: The earlier review said the leaf finalized-descendant check walks ancestors. But is_finalized_checkpoint_or_descendant returns at once when the node's own finalized/justified/unrealized checkpoint equals the store finalized checkpoint. That is the main cost Nimbus #6076 cached. The rebuild of the full filtered tree on each call is still uncached, so the verdict is partial, not implemented.

title: Compute justified balances once per justification change
idea: Have fork choice hold a small snapshot of justified-checkpoint effective balances (zero for inactive/slashed) plus total, fetched lazily only when the justified checkpoint changes, instead of passing or looking up balances (or caching large epoch results) on every head update or vote.

idea: Represent the non-finalized block tree as a flat array of nodes with parent, weight, best-child and best-descendant fields, apply only per-validator vote deltas in one backward pass that propagates weight to parents and updates best pointers. get_head is then a lookup of the justified node's best descendant instead of recomputing LMD-GHOST over the whole tree and all validators.

idea: For per-slot fork-choice work, fetch the pulled-up head state from the checkpoint-state cache instead of replaying the epoch transition, read a flat balances list, dedupe latest messages, scan votes in parallel chunks, and prefetch next epoch's balance-source state on the last slot.

title: Precomputed validator-to-slot table per shuffling seed
idea: Precompute, per attester-shuffling seed for recent epochs, a table mapping validator index to slot offset with size hints, so building fast-confirmation support maps avoids random balance access and repeated appends under the fork-choice lock.
measured_best: 1M validators: 106.2ms->11.95ms (8.9x), 62.6MB/2697 allocs -> 10.4KB/9 (pr:prysm#17179)

Build a Vec<u8> slot_offset per AttestationShufflingId (pre-sized to active count) in SlotAssignment::new and make get_node_support_between_slots / is_in_range index it; ideally aggregate once per slot range.

title: Cheap proto-array pruning on every finalization
idea: Make proto-array pruning cheap (no table rebuilds) and prune nodes before the finalized block whenever finality advances, including during range sync and on slot ticks, instead of waiting for a large threshold. The tree stays small, head computation traverses fewer nodes and memory does not leak.

consensus/fork_choice/src/fork_choice.rs:1957 prune -> maybe_prune

idea: Build the effective-balances snapshot for each epoch-boundary checkpoint from a state already in hand (block import or the per-epoch transition cache), cache it keyed by (boundary root, epoch), and hand the same immutable list to fork choice. A justified checkpoint switch is then a lookup instead of regenerating, rewinding or decoding a checkpoint state and copying a full balance list.

title: Store block metadata and execution status in fork choice nodes
idea: Store per-block metadata (state root, execution block hash, optimistic/execution status, justified/finalized checkpoints, dependent roots) directly on fork choice nodes. API duties, execution checks, invalidation and head events then read it from the node instead of separate hash maps or loading blocks or states from disk.

title: Build children index once per head walk, iterate filter
idea: In find_head, build the parent-to-children index once per call and run the viability filter pass iteratively in reverse node order, instead of scanning the whole block index at every visited node or recursing. This turns the walk from quadratic to linear in unfinalized blocks.
measured_best: Unchanged in 130 of 131 calls; fork choice time in block import 31.58 ms to 15.00 ms (~53%) (pr:lighthouse#10023)

idea: Make the seen-attestation filter for fork choice aware of aggregation-bit overlap so attestations whose bits are a subset of already seen ones are not reprocessed.

Reading ForkChoice::on_attestation and ProtoArray::process_attestation shows the latest-message tracker already makes reprocessing a no-op: per bit there is no weight or tree work, and compute_deltas skips unchanged votes. title: Incremental vote weight tally across get_head calls
idea: Keep per-root vote weights across get_head calls and update only for validators whose latest message or equivocation status changed (dirty set), rebuilding only when justified balances change, instead of summing all latest messages each time.
measured_best: execution done to FCU p50 107 ms -> 41 ms (pr:caplin#24985)

consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array_fork_choice.rs:1412 loop checks current vs next for each validator, no dirty set
consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:476 node weights persist across calls and only deltas are applied

gap: Weights are incremental, but the delta pass is a full O(V) scan of votes (plus a node_slots Vec rebuild) on every find_head. Keep a dirty-validator list set by process_attestation / equivocation / balance change, and iterate only it in compute_deltas, falling back to a full scan when justified balances change.

title: Skip finalized-descent walk for canonical targets
idea: In finalized-consistency checks for attestation targets, return early if the target is on the canonical chain (which implies finalized descent), skipping ancestor walks.
measured_best: CPU flame graphs before and after, no numbers (pr:prysm#7628)

title: Grow per-validator vote tables without doubling
idea: When the per-validator vote/latest-message tables grow for new validator indices, reslice within existing capacity or reserve the exact size plus fixed headroom, instead of reallocating and doubling. Avoids allocating twice the needed size at a capacity edge (~120 MB on mainnet).

evidence: consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array_fork_choice.rs:430-445 ElasticList::ensure uses Vec::resize_with(i+1), which grows by amortized doubling
proto_array_fork_choice.rs:27 VoteTracker is ~90 bytes per validator
gap: Change ElasticList::ensure (or process_attestation) to reserve_exact(i + 1 + fixed headroom) before resize_with, so the Vec never doubles at a capacity edge.
impact: Avoids a transient ~2x allocation of the vote table (~100 MB at ~1.1M validators); mostly virtual, small RSS win.

title: Consolidate fork choice locks into one external lock
idea: Remove internal per-method fork choice locks (and separate fork choice and canonical head locks) and take one lock at the top-level import/accessor caller, so block import does not repeatedly acquire and release fine-grained locks and contend with other paths.

title: Yield to networking between gossip processing batches
idea: Run queued gossip/block processing in small batches or time slices and hand control back to the network/event loop between them (time-based, not per job), so CPU-heavy work does not starve networking; allow concurrency above one so signature work can batch.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:747-748 each worker is a tokio task started with spawn_blocking, separate from the async network tasks
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:130 max_workers = num_cpus (concurrency above one)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:890 manager only spawns while current_workers < max_workers
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1017-1054 attestation queue drained into batches for batch BLS
common/task_executor/src/lib.rs:209-229 spawn_blocking / spawn_blocking_with_rayon run CPU work on dedicated blocking/rayon pools
impact: None to gain: the source PRs fix single-threaded event loops (Nim, JS). Lighthouse gets the same result from thread isolation. CPU work never runs on the tokio core threads that drive libp2p, and the OS scheduler time-slices the threads. Batching for BLS and multi-worker concurrency are already present.
refute_note: Checked the task_executor blocking and rayon pools, and the max_workers default. The idea's goal (networking is not starved, concurrency above one, signature batching) is met by an equivalent mechanism, so a time-slice yield has no job to do here.

title: Batch BLS verification of gossip attestations and aggregates
idea: Collect signature sets from many gossip attestations/aggregates over a short window and verify them with one randomized batch BLS call, falling back to individual verification on failure; this amortizes the final exponentiation. Verify the signature early via the batch verifier, before expensive shuffling lookups.
measured_best: batch check ~0.5ms/check vs ~1ms single; throughput 2x higher; worst latency ~40ms (pr:nimbus#2439)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:110 DEFAULT_MAX_GOSSIP_ATTESTATION_BATCH_SIZE=64 and aggregate batch 64
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1017-1035 pops up to batch size attestations into a GossipAttestationBatch
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:104-110 comment: fall back to individual verification on batch failure
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:529 process_gossip_aggregate_batch

title: Route other gossip types through shared batch verifier
idea: Send signatures of sync committee messages, voluntary exits and payload-timeliness attestations to the shared async batch BLS verifier instead of verifying each inline, publishing or pooling only after the batch succeeds.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:390-409 only GossipAttestationBatch and GossipAggregateBatch Work variants exist
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:709 SyncCommitteeMessage signature verified alone with signature_set.verify()
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:604-670 contributions batch only their own 3 signatures, not across messages
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_attestation_verification/gossip_verified_payload_attestation.rs:142 payload attestation signature verified alone
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2314 sync committee messages processed one at a time
gap: Add batch Work variants and queue draining for sync committee messages and payload attestations, as is done for attestations. Call verify_signature_sets once per batch and fall back to individual checks on failure. This touches the Work enum in lib.rs, gossip_methods.rs, sync_committee_verification.rs and payload_attestation_verification. Exits are rare, so skip them.
impact: About 512 sync messages per slot, plus PTC payload attestations after Gloas, are each verified with a single pubkey. Batching could save about a third to a half of that BLS time, which is a small CPU gain.
refute_note: Also checked the Gloas payload attestation path and the contribution batch helper. Neither batches across gossip messages, so not is upheld.

title: Verify one message's multiple signatures in one batch
idea: For aggregate-and-proof (selection proof, aggregator signature, aggregate signature) and sync contributions, verify all signatures of the message in a single batched multi-pairing instead of three separate verifications.
measured_best: BenchmarkValidateAggregateAndProof 3931547 -> 2812799 ns/op (40% better, ~1.2ms per aggregate, ~300ms per slot at 260 aggregates) (pr:prysm#7744)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1457-1484 selection proof and aggregate signature sets verified via one verify_signature_sets call
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:640-670 three sets (selection proof, contribution-and-proof, contribution) in one verify_signature_sets

title: Deserialize attestation signatures once through pipeline
idea: Parse gossip attestation/aggregate signatures once and pass the parsed signature through verification queues and the pool instead of re-parsing at each stage.
measured_best: Fixed attesting regressions v1.0.10->v1.0.12 caused by repeated deserialization (pr:nimbus#2472)
evidence: crypto/bls/src/generic_signature.rs:145 deserialize decompresses once into a point held in the type
crypto/bls/src/generic_signature.rs:191 SSZ decode does this, so the parsed signature travels through queues and pool

title: Aggregate attestation pubkeys without per-validator allocations
idea: Build aggregate pubkeys for attestation verification by reading the validator registry by index without allocating a deserialized pubkey object per validator.

title: Minimal state advance for gossip validation
idea: Validate gossip attestations, aggregates, blocks, slashings and sync messages against the existing head state or a checkpoint state cache entry, advancing a copy only when the epoch actually differs and then only to the target epoch start, rather than running process_slots to the message slot per message.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:315 with_cached_shuffling reuses head state, advances only to start of epoch before shuffling_epoch via partial_state_advance (shuffling_cache.rs:~430)

title: Validate exits and BLS changes with light validator getters
idea: Validate voluntary exits and BLS-to-execution changes using only the few validator fields needed from a cheap head-validator accessor, instead of fetching or advancing a full beacon state per message.

idea: Gossip validation should take head and finalized checkpoints and the head state from in-memory chain/fork-choice info (head state root, cached state) rather than reading the head state or block roots from the DB per message.
measured_best: "major noticeable bottleneck from our profiling" (no numbers) (pr:prysm#2383)

idea: In pre-validation checks of whether a referenced block root is known, use a plain fork-choice membership lookup without the descendant-of-finalized walk, leaving that check to full validation.
measured_best: hasBlockHex took 12% of main thread CPU time (pr:lodestar#5575)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:971 contains_block

title: Proposer index from shared per-epoch cache, no state advance
idea: Get the expected proposer (and committees) for gossip blocks and blob sidecars from a shared per-epoch proposer-index cache keyed by decision root, pruning old entries, instead of advancing, rewinding or loading a state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:175 with_proposer_cache keyed by (epoch, shuffling_decision_block)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1031 block gossip uses it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1750 column gossip uses it

title: Ignore blocks whose parent is older than justified
idea: Ignore current-epoch gossip blocks and column sidecars whose parent is canonical but older than the justified checkpoint, avoiding state regeneration to check the proposer.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1019-1050 gossip block path checks only parent-known/later-than-parent, then with_proposer_cache falls to load_parent on a miss; no justified-checkpoint check
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2012-2028 load_parent only rejects pre-finalized parents
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1179-1185 and 1747-1765 column path: finalized-descendant check, then get_advanced_hot_state on proposer-cache miss
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:188-200 OnceCell dedups concurrent misses for one (epoch, decision root) but does not avoid the state load
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1730-1746 only finalized-based IGNOREs
gap: Before the proposer-cache lookup in GossipVerifiedBlock::new_without_slasher_checks and validate_data_column_sidecar_for_gossip_fulu, IGNORE current-epoch blocks/columns whose parent is canonical and older than the fork-choice justified checkpoint slot, so a lagging proposer's block does not trigger a hot-state load and advance.
impact: Avoids a cold state load and multi-epoch advance per proposer-cache miss for blocks/columns built on stale canonical parents (lagging proposers, cheap DoS); rare on healthy mainnet.
refute_note: Grepped justified across block_verification, data_column_verification, beacon_proposer_cache and gossip_methods (no hits) and read load_parent and with_proposer_cache; the only related mitigation is OnceCell dedup of concurrent cache misses, which bounds repeated work but still loads the state once.

title: Bound state advancement for old or long-skip roots
idea: Reject or ignore gossip blocks and votes whose parent or target block is too many slots behind, or cap slot processing to one epoch, before advancing state over long runs of empty slots for attacker-chosen roots.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:946-951 skip-slot limit for unaggregated attestations only, via import_max_skip_slots
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:601-602 aggregates explicitly exempt
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:151 import_max_skip_slots default None
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1091-1097 --max-skip-slots documented as disabled by default
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:315-345 shuffling looked up by (epoch, decision root) and promise-deduplicated, so one old root costs one advance
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:425-460 advance limited to the epoch before shuffling_epoch, and uses partial_state_advance (no state roots)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2173-2197 cheap_state_advance_to_obtain_committees advances only to the block epoch start
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:346 proposer shuffling also uses partial_state_advance
gap: There is no default bound on the parent or target distance. Default import_max_skip_slots to a finite value (for example a few epochs), apply it to aggregates, and add an equivalent check for gossip blocks whose parent is many slots behind. The cost is already reduced (partial advance, shuffling cache keyed by decision root, promise dedup), but it is not capped.
impact: DoS hardening only: an attacker who picks old non-finalized roots can force long empty-slot advances. No steady-state saving on mainnet.
refute_note: Checked the CLI help (the limit is disabled by default on purpose), shuffling_cache with_cached_shuffling and its partial advance and dedup, and the proposer cache advance. All of them lower the cost but none caps the distance, so partial is upheld.

title: Order gossip validation checks cheapest first
idea: Order gossip validation rules so cheap structural REJECT checks run first, then cheap in-memory IGNOREs (slot window, bit lengths, committee bits, seen cache, invalid block, parent root, target epoch), then state loads, pool lookups, shuffling and signature checks, so invalid messages are dropped before costly work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:902-980 unaggregated: target epoch, slot range, committee index, fork-choice head block, target root, then pubkey length and observed attester before signature

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:530-640 aggregate: slot range, epoch, committee index, observed subset, observed aggregator, head block known, non-empty bits, then committee/signatures
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:900-1060 gossip block: fork, future slot, blob count, finalized, duplicate, invalid roots, parent known, then proposer cache, then signature
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:462 slot range, subnet, seen, then signature
gap: Minor: the aggregate path computes the tree_hash_root of ObservedAttestationKey before the cheap committee-index check; negligible.
impact: Already drops invalid messages before state loads and BLS; no meaningful saving left.

title: Cheap sidecar checks before proposer BLS signature
idea: On blob/column sidecar gossip, run cheap checks (proposer index, seen index, parent seen) before proposer signature verification so invalid or duplicate sidecars do not cost a BLS check.
measured_best: Attack estimate: signature verification about 2ms each, hundreds of malicious sidecars per validator (pr:prysm#13347)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1150-1185 subnet, future/finalized slot, seen index (verify_is_unknown_sidecar), DA-cache PriorKnownUnpublished, inclusion proof and parent-known checks all run before verify_proposer_and_signature
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2486-2496 partial-column headers already verified for a block_root are reused from cache without a new BLS check
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1776-1801 proposer_index equality checked only after signed_block_header.verify_signature
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1052-1103 IncorrectBlockProposer checked after BLS verify
gap: In verify_proposer_and_signature (used by full and partial column headers, data_column_verification.rs:654 and 1185) compare signed_block_header.message.proposer_index to the cached expected index before verify_signature and return ProposerIndexMismatch; optionally the same for gossip blocks. Blob sidecars no longer exist in this tree.
impact: Saves one BLS verify (~1-2 ms) per sidecar carrying a wrong proposer index; only matters under attack.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, found that the DA-checker PriorKnownUnpublished early return and the partial-column header cache also skip BLS for already-known data, but the proposer-index comparison is still after the signature check, so partial stands.

title: Cheap checks before loading pre-state
idea: Run state-independent checks (time window, invalid-block reference, already imported) and use cached genesis time before loading or regenerating the head/parent state, so rejected messages never touch state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:918-975 future-slot, finalized slot, fork-choice contains_block, check_invalid_block_roots, finalized-descendant, parent-in-fork-choice all before any state load
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1298 slot range uses slot_clock (no state/genesis read)

title: Seen-check sidecars first before KZG and signature
idea: For blob and data column sidecar gossip, do the already-seen (block header/slot, proposer, index) IGNORE check first, before KZG, signature and other checks, so duplicates are neither revalidated nor re-propagated.

title: Seen-attestation cache checked first in attestation validation
idea: Check the recently-seen attestation cache at the very start of attestation validation and exit early on a hit.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:902-980 early checks (slot range, fork-choice head/target lookups) run first, all cheap

title: Compact key for seen unaggregated attestation cache
idea: Key the seen-unaggregated-attestation cache by a compact fixed-size key (e.g. attester index plus data) rather than a hashed or concatenated buffer including the full aggregation bitlist.

impact: Already one bit per validator per epoch; no bitlist in key.

title: Dedup slasher ingress before BLS and queueing
idea: Before slasher ingestion, dedup indexed attestations on (validator_index, data hash) and skip BLS verification and queue append for already staged ones, bounding the queue.
evidence: slasher/src/attestation_queue.rs:21-25 AttestationQueue is a Mutex<Vec>, no ingress dedup

gap: Dedup at slasher ingress on (validator_index, attestation_data_hash) and let process_slash_info skip BLS verify and queue append for already staged records (sigp/lighthouse#10107, not merged in this base).

refute_note: Re-read the slasher queue, Slasher::accept_attestation and process_slash_info; the only dedup is batch-time in AttestationBatch, after signature verify and queueing.

title: Ignore further blocks from same proposer and slot
idea: Once a validly signed block for (proposer, slot) was seen, ignore any further gossip block for that pair so duplicates and equivocations are not re-validated or imported.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:969-972 only early pre-check is fork_choice contains_block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1076-1098 observe_slashable/observe_proposal (Slashable/Duplicate rejection) only after proposer-cache lookup and BLS verify

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1561 DuplicateCache is keyed by block root and checked only after gossip verification
gap: Do a cheap (slot, proposer) lookup via proposer_has_been_observed early in GossipVerifiedBlock::new and ignore further blocks before parent load and signature verify, while still routing the first equivocation to observed_slashable/slasher.
impact: Equivocating or duplicate-id blocks still cost a proposer lookup, possible state load and a BLS verify; small except under equivocation floods.
refute_note: Also checked the beacon processor DuplicateCache and gossip_methods block path; both act by block root and after verification, so they do not short-circuit a second block for the same (proposer, slot).

title: Atomic seen check-and-set for concurrent duplicates
idea: Mark a block or blob as seen in one locked check-and-set (or lock around validation) so concurrent duplicates from several peers are processed only once.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1087-1098 atomic check-and-set under observed_block_producers write lock, after signature verify

gap: Claim the (slot, proposer[, index]) key in-flight at the early check (released on failure) in GossipVerifiedBlock::new and validate_data_column_sidecar_for_gossip_fulu/gloas, so concurrent distinct-id duplicates do the signature/KZG work once.

title: Ignore aggregates whose bits are subset of seen ones
idea: For each attestation data (and committee index post-Electra) track the aggregation bits of seen gossip aggregates and sync contributions, and ignore a new one whose bits are a (non-strict) subset of an already seen one, before signature verification. This skips BLS work and re-propagation for redundant aggregates.

idea: Keep a per-slot seen cache of aggregate hash tree roots and aggregator messages (fed from gossip, API, blocks and local production), hashing the aggregate once, and ignore an already seen gossip aggregate at the start of validation, before signature, state work, pool insertion or propagation.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:589-600 observed_aggregators check by aggregator index and epoch

title: Cache validation work per distinct AttestationData
idea: Cache per-slot gossip attestation validation results (signing root, data root, head/target checks, committee) keyed by serialized AttestationData plus committee bits, so many attestations and aggregates with identical data hash and check once; keep lookup and insert keys consistent.
measured_best: validateGossipAttestation was ~12% of CPU (5.8% signing root, 3.9% head/target check); reduced to under 3%; cache <300kb per slot (pr:lodestar#5333)

gap: Per-slot cache keyed by (AttestationData root, committee index) holding signing root and head/target check results, reused in verify_early_checks and signature-set construction; in batch mode compute each distinct data's signing root once.

refute_note: Searched attestation_verification, its batch module and signature_sets for any data-root or signing-root memoisation; only shuffling/pubkey caches exist, which every client has.

title: Verify proposer header signature once across sidecars
idea: Cache verified (block root/header, proposer signature) results so the block and its blob/column sidecars sharing the same header skip re-verifying the proposer signature.
measured_best: Verification takes 20-40 ms on hoodi; now once per slot (pr:lodestar#8620)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2493-2500 verify_partial_data_column_header_for_gossip returns the cached verified header per block root and skips re-verification

gap: Full Fulu data column sidecars (and the gossip block) do not consult the per-block-root verified header held by PartialDataColumnAssembler; check it (or a small signed-header-root cache) before verify_proposer_and_signature, and fill it from GossipVerifiedBlock::new.
impact: For a node custodying many columns, saves ~1 ms BLS plus proposer lookup per extra full column per block; partial-column traffic already benefits.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the partial-column header cache in PartialDataColumnAssembler, which already verifies a block's header once and reuses it; the full-column and block paths do not share it.

title: Compute gossip block root once and reuse it
idea: Compute the block root once during gossip validation and carry it in the verified block/blob for proposer signature checks, error/reject paths and later stages instead of re-hashing; check slot before reading the database.
measured_best: None (pr:lighthouse#4277)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:890 block root from header root (body hash already cached), computed once
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:900 BlockErrorWithRoot carries block_root into error paths

idea: Keep a bounded cache of block roots that failed validation, and immediately reject gossip blocks, attestations and aggregates that are, reference or build on them, without repeating state work or full verification when they arrive from other peers.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:976 gossip block path consults it

beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:77,352 failed_chains LRU covers range-sync targets only
gap: No dynamic bounded cache of roots that failed consensus validation. Children of an invalid block trigger parent lookups and re-verification; attestations to it go to the unknown-block reprocess queue. Add an LRU filled on state-transition/signature failures and checked in GossipVerifiedBlock::new_without_slasher_checks, column/envelope gossip verification and attestation verification.
impact: Skips repeated parent fetch, state load and state transition for re-gossiped invalid blocks and their descendants/attestations; matters only under attack or fork spam.
refute_note: Checked sync-side caches (block_lookups ignored_chains, range_sync failed_chains): both are LRU caches of roots, but neither is filled on invalid-block results and neither is consulted on gossip. Gossipsub's duplicate cache only drops byte-identical messages.

title: Check snappy declared length before decompressing
idea: Read the uncompressed length from the snappy header and reject gossip messages outside the topic's valid size range (max gossip payload) before allocating, decompressing or SSZ decoding, including in the message-id function, so oversized messages cost no CPU or memory.
measured_best: Prevents multi-GB allocation from a ~12MB message (pr:ethlambda#199)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:108-120 SnappyTransform::inbound_transform checks compressed len, then decompress_len() against max_uncompressed_len before decompress_vec
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:510 max_transmit_size set; message-id fn runs on already-transformed data
impact: Already avoids allocating or decompressing oversized messages.

title: Bound column sidecar size by max blobs early
idea: Reject data column sidecars carrying more blobs than the fork's max blobs per block at the decompression/size check stage, before queueing, decode or KZG work.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:279-292 size cap before SSZ decode, Gloas only
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:106-121 SnappyTransform only enforces global max_payload_size/max_compressed_len

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:510 single global gossipsub max_transmit_size; per-topic max_transmit_size_for_topic in the sigp rust-libp2p gossipsub (protocols/gossipsub/src/config.rs:266, behaviour.rs:637) is unused by Lighthouse
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1516 verify_commitments_len_within_max_blobs runs in the worker after decode and queueing
gap: For Fulu, columns are decoded (bounded only by the SSZ type limit MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock) and queued before the max-blobs-per-block check. Add a Fulu size cap from the topic epoch's max_blobs_per_block in PubsubMessage::decode, or set a per-topic gossipsub max transmit size.
impact: Rejects oversized Fulu columns before decode and queueing; saves memory/CPU only against malicious peers.
refute_note: Also checked the gossipsub dependency: it supports a per-topic transmit size, but Lighthouse sets only the global max_transmit_size. The snappy transform uses only global limits.

title: Bound pending, deferred and future-slot gossip queues
idea: Cap, prune and expire queues of gossip blocks, attestations and sidecars held for an unknown parent or future slot (entry count, per-entry cell count, retained slot window, drop oldest) and run cheap structure checks at admission, so peers cannot pin unbounded memory.
measured_best: SSZ max 4096 cells with 8-root/128-column queue allows ~8 GiB heap held (pr:prysm#16831)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:78-90 MAXIMUM_QUEUED_BLOCKS 16, ENVELOPES 16, ATTESTATIONS 16384, DATA_COLUMNS 256
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:867 drops when column count full
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:384-386 per-type queues capped at 1024
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:595 attestation queue cap
gap: Caps are by entry count with delay-queue expiry; no per-entry cell/byte accounting, and unknown-parent blocks go to sync lookups rather than a held queue.
impact: Memory is already bounded by counts; byte-weighted accounting would only tighten worst case.

title: Reject future-slot messages before queueing or hashing
idea: Reject gossip blocks and sidecars whose slot is beyond wall clock plus disparity before computing hash tree roots or inserting them into pending queues, with one shared helper.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:886-890 signed_block_header() (body tree hash) and get_block_header_root run first
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:915-925 FutureSlot check comes after that, in new_without_slasher_checks
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:262-275 blocks decoded in full with no slot check before queueing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1157 column future-slot check comes early
gap: The block body hash_tree_root is computed before the future-slot check, and nothing rejects far-future slots before the block is queued. Move the now_with_future_tolerance check to before signed_block_header() in GossipVerifiedBlock::new; a check before queueing would need a slot peek in the router.
impact: Far-future blocks skip one full body hash_tree_root; negligible on honest traffic.
refute_note: Re-read GossipVerifiedBlock::new and the decode path. No earlier slot check exists in pubsub decode or in the router. There is no shared future-slot helper; each verifier does its own check.

title: Cap in-flight gossip validations per large topic
idea: Limit concurrent in-flight validations per large-message topic and drop excess before SSZ decode; ignore envelopes whose state is not cached instead of regenerating.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:384-386 count-bounded queues per work type
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:195-433 SSZ decode in the network layer before queueing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/gossip_verified_envelope.rs:237,274 load_snapshot_from_state_root on proposer cache miss and for every external builder envelope
gap: There is no per-topic cap on in-flight validations before decode; queues are bounded by count after decode. Envelope verification loads the state from the store instead of ignoring when the state is not cached; external builder envelopes always load it. Add a per-topic limit before PubsubMessage::decode and an ignore-on-miss path in envelope gossip verification.
impact: Bounds memory and state loads under envelope or large-topic floods; little effect on healthy nodes.
refute_note: Searched the sigp rust-libp2p gossipsub checkout for validation backpressure or in-flight limits and found none; its only per-topic limit is transmit size. Confirmed that the external builder path always loads the state (TODO builder pubkey cache).

title: Keep compressed payload in gossip validation queue
idea: Hold only the compressed payload plus a small decoded prefix for queued gossip messages, decompress in the worker, apply a byte-weighted per-topic limit, and read slot from fixed SSZ offset to drop far-future blocks before decoding.
measured_best: held heap per queued block 6.20 MiB -> 0.20 MiB; far-future block flood no longer OOMs (pr:teku#11503)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:106-125 snappy decompression in gossipsub inbound_transform on the network thread
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:262-275 SignedBeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes_by_fork full decode before queueing
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:384 count-only queue limits
gap: Queued gossip work holds fully decoded objects. There is no compressed-payload queue, no byte-weighted limit and no fixed-offset slot peek. Implementing this needs decompress and decode moved into the worker, plus a byte-budgeted queue in lighthouse_network/network and beacon_processor.
impact: Less heap held per queued block under flood (Teku measured 6.2 MiB to 0.2 MiB); mostly attack resilience.
refute_note: Checked the transform and decode path and the gossipsub dependency: decompression and decode are both eager. No lazy or byte-weighted queue exists under any name.

title: Reject pre-finalized gossip blocks and attestations
idea: Reject gossip blocks and attestations older than the finalized epoch before processing, so old forks cannot trigger recursive parent lookups.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:964 check_block_against_finalized_slot before parent lookup
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1843 WouldRevertFinalizedSlot

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1157 PastFinalizedSlot
impact: Already prevents old forks from triggering parent lookups.

title: Skip gossip validation while syncing or far behind
idea: While the node is syncing or more than a few slots behind head (head state too old), do not validate gossip operations such as attestations and aggregates (keep blocks and blobs), since the results cannot be used and the work is wasted.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1211 drops work with drop_during_sync when sync_state.is_syncing()
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:117,162,290 attestations/aggregates/etc set drop_during_sync: true; blocks use false (lib.rs:240-309)
gap: Gate is on SyncState (SyncingFinalized/Head), not on head being N slots old, so a node merely a few slots behind but reported Synced still validates.
impact: Wasted attestation/aggregate validation during sync is already skipped.

title: Batch KZG verification of gossip column sidecars
idea: Verify KZG proofs of multiple gossip data column sidecars together in a batch rather than one sidecar at a time.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:417 GossipDataColumnSidecar(AsyncFn) is one work item per sidecar
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1035 verify_kzg_for_data_column verifies one column via iter::once (also :1060 with_commitments variant)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:342 awaiting_data_columns_per_root only delays columns, releases them individually
gap: Gossip columns are KZG-verified one at a time. Add a batch work type in BeaconProcessor that drains several GossipDataColumnSidecar items, runs cheap gossip checks per item, then one validate_data_columns call with per-column fault attribution on failure.
impact: One multi-pairing replaces N when many columns of one block arrive together; mainly helps supernodes; not measured.
refute_note: Also checked the reprocess queue (groups columns per root but releases them singly), the partial-column verify path, and all validate_data_columns callers: none batch gossip columns.

title: Remove seen caches made redundant by other dedup
idea: Drop a duplicate-filter or seen-attestation skip cache in gossip validation when another layer (gossip message-id dedup, op pool dedup, other checks) already filters the same duplicates, saving its memory and lookups.
measured_best: Frees 300MB of memory (pr:caplin#12937)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:431 observed_attestations (ObservedAggregateAttestations) still exists
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:572 is_known_subset skip before BLS; :589 observed_aggregators
beacon_node/PR lighthouse#2750 (removal) was closed unmerged
gap: Remove observed_attestations/observed_sync_contributions and the AttestationSupersetKnown path in attestation_verification.rs, relying on gossipsub message-id dedup plus op pool dedup. Lighthouse relies on the subset check to skip BLS, so removal may cost CPU.
impact: Frees some memory (Caplin saw 300MB for its own cache; LH cache is smaller and pruned by slot) but may add BLS work for redundant aggregates; marginal net.

title: Bypass queue gating for gossip blocks
idea: Process gossip blocks immediately, bypassing the BLS-pool and regen availability gates other gossip objects wait on.
measured_best: delay could exceed 2s in worst case (pr:lodestar#5263)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:929 gossip_block_queue popped before attestation queues, after chain segments/rpc blocks/delayed blocks
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1239 GossipBlock dispatched immediately when can_spawn
impact: Lighthouse has no BLS-pool/regen availability gate on other gossip, so blocks are simply highest-priority gossip; nothing to bypass.

title: Hold slightly-early gossip objects until their slot
idea: Put gossip blocks, attestations and other items that arrive slightly early (within clock disparity or one slot) into a bounded future queue and replay them at slot or interval start, instead of dropping or repeatedly retrying them.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:659 EarlyBlock held until slot start + 5ms (MAXIMUM_QUEUED_BLOCKS cap)
beacon_node/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:~725 EarlyEnvelope likewise

impact: Avoids dropping and re-requesting legit slightly early attestations; small CPU/bandwidth effect, mostly correctness at slot boundaries.

title: Verify block signature before pending-queue insertion
idea: Check the proposer index and signature of a gossip block before saving it to the unknown-parent or future-slot pool, keeping at most one per proposer and slot, so invalid or unsigned blocks cannot fill pools or trigger parent lookups and sync fetches.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:921 blocks past slot+clock-disparity are rejected (FutureSlot) before any pool

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1877 ReprocessQueueMessage::EarlyBlock is queued only with a fully gossip-verified block (proposer + signature checked, observed_block_producers updated)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:990 verify_parent_block_and_envelope_are_known returns ParentUnknown before the signature check at :1055
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1693 ParentUnknown sends SyncMessage::UnknownParentBlock unsigned
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:77 MAX_LOOKUPS=200 cap and :276 PARENT_DEPTH_TOLERANCE bound lookups (dedup by root, not by proposer/slot)
gap: Future-slot (early block) pool already holds only signature-verified blocks. Unknown-parent blocks still reach sync lookups without proposer/signature checks and with no one-per-(proposer,slot) limit; only the global MAX_LOOKUPS cap and root dedup bound them. Verify the signature via the proposer cache (when the shuffling is known from the head/finalized chain) before sending UnknownParentBlock.
impact: DoS hardening of parent lookups; little steady-state CPU saving.
refute_note: Earlier review missed that Lighthouse's future-slot queue (EarlyBlock) stores only GossipVerifiedBlocks and far-future blocks are dropped, which covers the future-slot half of the idea; the unknown-parent half is still missing.

title: Expire held unknown-root gossip messages
idea: Expire buffered unknown-root gossip messages for blocks seen but never imported, so the global cap does not fill permanently.
measured_best: counter stuck at 16385 for 3+ hours on mainnet node (pr:lodestar#10389)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:53 QUEUED_ATTESTATION_DELAY 12s expiry via attestations_delay_queue
beacon_node/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:595 MAXIMUM_QUEUED_ATTESTATIONS cap; :1268 awaiting_attestations_per_root pruned on expiry (regression test :1847)
beacon_node/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:864 unknown-block data columns have their own cap and delay
impact: Held unknown-root messages already expire; global cap cannot fill permanently.

title: Per-(validator, epoch) seen caches checked before validation
idea: Dedupe gossip attestations and aggregates with in-memory seen caches keyed by (attester or aggregator index, target epoch) and check them before state loads and BLS verification, so duplicates from the same validator in an epoch cost a map lookup, not a DB lookup or signature check.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_attesters.rs:308 AutoPruningEpochContainer
impact: Duplicates cost a bitfield lookup rather than state load or BLS.

title: Size seen caches for the validator set
idea: Size the seen-attester and seen-aggregator gossip caches from the validator count and committee/aggregator counts over several slots, so entries are not evicted before duplicates arrive and duplicates are not revalidated.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#13756)

title: Replace DB reads in gossip checks with in-memory state
idea: Answer bad-block and seen-proposer checks in gossip validation from in-memory caches or fork choice instead of a database read per message, or drop the DB check where fork choice membership already covers it.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:971 fork choice contains_block for duplicates
beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3880 invalid roots is in-memory config set

title: Group queued attestations by data for batch verify
idea: Index the gossip attestation queue by attestation data key and pop chunks of same-data messages together, so attestations sharing data can be batch-verified with shared work.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#5803)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1010 attestation queue popped in plain batches, no key by data
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification/batch.rs:133 batch_verify_unaggregated_attestations builds one set per attestation

gap: Queue is not keyed by AttestationData; equal-data attestations are not grouped and their messages are hashed to curve separately. Key the queue by data root and pop same-data chunks, sharing signing-root computation and hash-to-curve (or aggregate same-message sets before multi-verify).
impact: Saves hash-to-curve and repeated per-data checks; small share of attestation CPU.
refute_note: Checked beacon_processor for any data-root keyed queue and the blst batch-verify wrapper for same-message dedup; none found.

title: Bounded prioritized gossip work queue, blocks first
idea: Put all gossip messages (attestations, slashings, exits) into bounded per-type queues pulled by a scheduler with bounded concurrency that prioritizes blocks over attestations, so attestation floods cannot starve or delay block processing.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:759-765 WorkQueues with bounded per-type queues
lib.rs:890 max_workers bound; lib.rs:955 blocks checked before attestations
beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:335-363 queue lengths from validator count
impact: Already in place; attestation floods cannot starve block processing.

title: Attestation admission budget scaled to traffic
idea: Rate-limit gossip attestation processing with a node-wide budget per window sized from expected traffic (subscribed subnets times active validators per slot and subnet, with headroom), so CPU is bounded without dropping legitimate attestations.
measured_best: None (pr:caplin#24970)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:357 attestation_queue sized from active validators / slots_per_epoch
beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:110 batch size 64, batching verification
no time-window rate limiter found in network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs
gap: Lighthouse bounds attestation work by queue length (sized from validator count) and drops on overflow rather than a per-window admission budget; CPU is bounded by workers and batching. A budget would need a counter in the router before sending attestation events to BeaconProcessor::send_gossip_attestation.
impact: Little: Lighthouse already sheds load via bounded queue and batch BLS; a budget could cut dedup/decode CPU under floods but risks dropping legitimate attestations (Caplin dropped 39-99%).

title: Cheap raw-byte field reads without views
idea: Read fixed-offset fields like slot from raw SSZ gossip bytes with direct byte arithmetic rather than constructing a view or decoder object, to make pre-validation field extraction cheaper.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#6941)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:254 SingleAttestation::from_ssz_bytes full decode
pubsub.rs:266 SignedBeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes_by_fork
impact: Rust SSZ decode of fixed-size containers is already direct byte reads with no view/lazy object; saving would be nanoseconds per message.

title: Peek raw SSZ bytes to skip deserialization
idea: Extract keys (attestation data bytes, block root) from serialized gossip bytes at fixed offsets and use them as seen-cache keys, fully deserializing only on a cache miss or not at all for already-imported objects; most attestations per slot share few data values.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#5363)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:492 gossip_message_id = sha256(prefix+topic+decompressed bytes)
accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:1950 message id computed on raw bytes; :1985 duplicate_cache.insert drops repeats before the message reaches Lighthouse
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:1390 PubsubMessage::decode runs only for non-duplicate messages
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:254 non-duplicate attestations always fully decoded, no data-bytes keyed cache
gap: Byte-identical duplicates (same block/column/attestation from many mesh peers) are already dropped by the gossipsub duplicate cache, keyed on a hash of the raw bytes, before SSZ decode; IDONTWANT also suppresses them. Missing: peeking semantic keys from bytes, e.g. AttestationData bytes shared by thousands of distinct attestations, or a block root for an already-imported block re-sent with other bytes, to skip decode and per-data validation.
impact: Remaining saving is per-attestation decode and shared-data work; smaller than the earlier review stated since duplicate blocks/columns never reach decode.
refute_note: Earlier review missed that the gossipsub dependency dedups on a raw-bytes message id before PubsubMessage::decode, which covers the 'skip deserialization for already-seen objects' part for identical bytes.

title: Singleflight state replays for sidecar verification
idea: Deduplicate concurrent state replays/regenerations for the same target when many data column sidecars arrive at once and each needs the same verifying state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:~190 cache_entry.get_or_try_init OnceCell: concurrent misses share one state load and computation
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1746 verify_proposer_and_signature uses chain.with_proposer_cache
impact: Equivalent singleflight already exists via the OnceCell in the proposer cache; sidecar verification needs only the proposer shuffling.

title: Plain map for bounded seen key space
idea: Track already-seen slashed validator indices in a plain map instead of an LRU cache, since the key space is bounded and needs no eviction bookkeeping.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#8332)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_operations.rs:27 observed_validator_indices: HashSet<u64>, reset at fork boundary
impact: Nothing; plain set already used.

title: Precompute per-shuffling committee aggregate pubkeys
idea: Precompute aggregate public keys per committee for the shuffling and derive aggregate keys by subtracting non-participants, and pass parsed views to avoid re-parsing and re-hashing in attestation validation.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/signature_sets.rs:295 indexed_attestation_signature_set collects participant pubkeys per attestation
crypto/bls/src/generic_signature_set.rs:119 verify aggregates the pubkey list each time (fast_aggregate_verify)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:39 CachedShuffling holds committees only, no aggregate pubkeys
gap: No per-committee precomputed aggregate pubkey; each aggregate sums participant pubkeys from scratch. Cache per-shuffling committee aggregate pubkeys and derive by subtracting non-participants when participation is high.
impact: Cuts G1 additions per aggregate; small next to pairing cost; adds memory.
refute_note: Searched beacon_node/consensus/crypto for AggregatePublicKey use: only the sync committee spec field and op-pool, nothing cached for attestation committees.

title: Use proposer lookahead to skip epoch transitions
idea: Post-Fulu, read the expected proposer for gossip blocks and data column sidecars from the parent state's proposer lookahead instead of advancing a state across an epoch boundary or regenerating a block-slot state.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1746 and block_verification.rs:1031 use the proposer cache keyed by decision root
impact: Post-Fulu the parent state already holds the lookahead, so no epoch transition is run and results are cached per decision root.

title: Read-only head or parent state, no copy
idea: Validate gossip objects (exits, BLS changes, blocks) against a read-only reference to the head or parent state instead of cloning the state per message.
measured_best: None (pr:caplin#24523)

idea: Validate gossip aggregates, blocks and sync messages against already cached states (checkpoint/target state, pre-advanced slot state, parent post-state, tip state) instead of copying the head state or regenerating.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#5737)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1031 block proposer checked via proposer cache before loading parent

title: Direct state lookup by block root
idea: When the block is known to be at the message slot, fetch its post state directly by block root rather than via a slot-plus-root checkpoint-state path, avoiding queue locks and key scans per message.
measured_best: None (pr:teku#11215)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:315 with_cached_shuffling keyed by head block root via fork choice get_block
shuffling_cache.rs:340-350 read-lock cache hit path; no checkpoint-state cache scan

title: Parse fork digest from topic without allocation

title: Keep the KZG library at its latest release
idea: Bump the KZG libraries (c-kzg-4844, rust-eth-kzg, jc-kzg, blst) to the newest release to pick up upstream speedups, including faster trusted-setup context load. Check the KZG crate versions in the Lighthouse Cargo.toml against the latest upstream release.

title: Enable fixed-base precomputation tables in the KZG setup
idea: Load the trusted setup with a nonzero fixed-base precompute window (7 to 9 bits, higher on supernodes) so the fixed-base MSMs in cell/proof computation and cell recovery run up to about 2x faster, at tens of MiB of memory. Check the precompute argument where Lighthouse initializes its KZG context, and whether it is larger on supernodes.
measured_best: pr:lighthouse#5795: table off doubles the time to compute cells and proofs (pr:nimbus#8405: about 1.6x faster at 48 MiB)
evidence: crypto/kzg/src/lib.rs:76 new_from_trusted_setup uses UsePrecomp::Yes{width: RECOMMENDED_PRECOMP_WIDTH}

impact: Already on: width 8 (about 48 MiB). Not raised on supernodes (9 would be a small extra gain), but main saving is taken.

title: AVX-512 IFMA FFT for blob cell extension
idea: Compute the 128 extended cells of a blob with an 8-lane AVX-512 IFMA field FFT instead of scalar blst arithmetic, falling back to scalar when IFMA is absent. Check whether the KZG backend Lighthouse uses for compute_cells has a SIMD FFT path.
measured_best: pr:silver#412: 1717.6 us -> 79.7 us per blob (21.55x)
evidence: Cargo.lock: rust_eth_kzg 0.9.1, ekzg-* 0.9.1, blstrs 0.7.1, blst 0.3.17
grep avx512|ifma|avx2|_mm512|simd|vpmadd52 over ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/{blst-0.3.17,blstrs-0.7.1,ekzg-*-0.9.1,rust_eth_kzg-0.9.1}: no hits
blst-0.3.17/build.rs:160-180 only ISA switch is ADX (scalar mulx/adcx), or portable
gap: No SIMD field FFT anywhere in the KZG stack; cell extension uses ekzg-erasure-codes/ekzg-polynomial scalar FFT over blstrs Scalar (blst ADX asm). Would need an IFMA field/FFT backend behind runtime CPU detection inside rust_eth_kzg or a replacement of Kzg::compute_cells.
impact: Up to ~20x on per-blob cell extension on IFMA CPUs, but absolute cost is small on most nodes since EL getBlobsV2 supplies proofs; matters for block production and reconstruction.
refute_note: Searched blst assembly/build flags and all ekzg crates, not only rust_eth_kzg; the only ISA-specific path is blst's ADX scalar Montgomery multiply, which is not lane-parallel.

title: AVX-512 IFMA MSM and pairing for cell batch verify
idea: Batch-verify cell KZG proofs with an 8-lane AVX-512 IFMA Pippenger MSM (signed-digit buckets, batched affine adds, lazy reduction) and run the final pairing on IFMA lanes with SHA-NI for the challenge hash. Check whether Lighthouse's cell verification backend has a vectorized MSM and pairing.
measured_best: pr:silver#413: verify 128 columns 116.12 ms -> 24.78 ms (4.69x vs c-kzg)
evidence: ekzg-multi-open-0.9.1/src/fk20/verifier.rs:186,200,224 g1_lincomb, :251 multi_pairings
ekzg-bls12-381-0.9.1/src/lincomb.rs:29 G1Projective::multi_exp (blstrs -> blst Pippenger, scalar ADX)
ekzg-bls12-381-0.9.1/src/booth_encoding.rs, batch_addition.rs: signed-digit and batched affine adds exist but only in the fixed-base MSM (fixed_base_msm_window.rs:4), scalar code
No avx512/ifma/simd hits in blst-0.3.17, blstrs-0.7.1, ekzg-*-0.9.1
gap: Some algorithmic tricks from the idea (Booth signed digits, batched affine addition with batch inversion) already exist in ekzg, but only for fixed-base MSM, and nothing is vectorized; verify-path MSM and pairing go to blst scalar code. Would need an IFMA multi-lane MSM and Miller loop backend, feature-gated with fallback.
impact: Up to ~4.7x cheaper cell batch verification on AVX-512 IFMA CPUs; meaningful on supernodes and range sync, small on regular nodes.
refute_note: Traced verify_multi_opening down to blstrs multi_exp/multi_pairings and checked ekzg's own MSM helpers; found non-SIMD signed-digit and batched-affine code, which does not count as the vectorized idea.

title: Vectorized G1 point decompression and subgroup check
idea: Decompress and subgroup-check compressed G1 points (KZG proofs, commitments, pubkeys) eight at a time with AVX-512 IFMA instead of one at a time in blst. Check how Lighthouse deserializes KZG proofs and commitments before verification.
measured_best: pr:silver#397: 3.67x over blst, 8.6 us vs 31.6 us per point
evidence: crypto/kzg/src/lib.rs:63 Kzg wraps rust_eth_kzg DASContext only

gap: Would need a vectorized decompress/subgroup-check in or under rust_eth_kzg (or a fork) with runtime CPU detection; Lighthouse itself passes compressed bytes straight to the library.
impact: Saves tens of microseconds per point on IFMA CPUs only; commitments and proofs per column are few, so negligible per block.

title: Use the fastest available native KZG backend
idea: Switch blob and cell KZG operations to a faster native library (C or optimized Rust, or a runtime-selectable alternative such as Constantine) instead of a slower implementation. Check which KZG backend Lighthouse uses for column construction and cell verification and compare it in benchmarks with the alternatives.

title: Run KZG work off the async runtime or event loop
idea: Run KZG proof verification and cell computation on worker or blocking threads, not on the async runtime or main event loop, so networking, attestation production and other tasks are not stalled. Check whether every Lighthouse KZG call on the gossip and import paths runs via spawn_blocking or the beacon processor, not inline in an async task.

title: Dedicated prioritized executor for cell computation and recovery
idea: Run cell computation and cell recovery on a dedicated executor apart from the shared thread pool, and give computation for the head block priority over background recovery, to cut tail latency under load. Check whether Lighthouse's KZG compute and reconstruction share the global rayon pool and whether recovery can delay head-block work.
measured_best: pr:grandine#596: reduces p99 latency during high load (no number)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3811,3845 cell recovery runs on RayonPoolType::HighPriority pool, the only BN user of that pool (others: builder.rs:1199, beacon_chain.rs:4827, beacon_processor lib.rs:1728 use LowPriority)

refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, checked that the HighPriority pool is effectively dedicated to reconstruction in the BN, and found the beacon processor queue order plus the reprocess delay queue that defer recovery behind gossip block/column work, which is equivalent to Grandine #596 (dedicated executor, computation over recovery).

title: Batch KZG verify all columns of a block or segment
idea: When a code path holds more than one data column or blob (block import, RPC response, range sync segment, getBlobs result), verify all their KZG proofs in one batch call instead of per item, and fall back to per-item checks only to attribute a failure. Check Lighthouse's RPC, sync, getBlobs and import paths for per-column verification loops.
measured_best: pr:lighthouse#4903: batch ~32x faster than a loop (pr:prysm#14559: 32 blocks 12-13 s -> 700 ms)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:495-525 batch_verify_kzg_for_range_sync_blocks: blobs batched across segment, but columns call verify_columns_against_block per block (comment at :507)

gap: Custody backfill (historical_data_columns) already batches across blocks, and blobs batch across a segment, but forward range sync (signature_verify_chain_segment) and block backfill (batch_verify_kzg_for_range_sync_blocks) still verify columns once per block. Collect (column, commitments) pairs of all blocks in the segment into one validate_data_columns_with_commitments call, as historical_data_columns.rs already does, with per-block fallback only to attribute a failure.
impact: Range sync and backfill column KZG: fewer, larger multi-pairing batches and better rayon utilisation; likely 1.5-3x less KZG time while syncing, no effect at head.
refute_note: Found an existing cross-block column batch in custody backfill (historical_data_columns.rs) the earlier review missed, and confirmed the sync network layer does no separate KZG pre-check; the per-block loop remains in forward range sync and block backfill, so partial stands with a template to copy.

title: Drain queued gossip columns into one KZG batch
idea: Feed gossip data column KZG verification through a worker that drains all pending requests into one batch call (immediately when idle, accumulating while busy), with per-item fallback on failure. Check whether Lighthouse verifies each gossip column's KZG proofs individually or batches concurrent arrivals.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:944 gossip_data_column_queue.pop() takes one item per worker; only attestations/aggregates have batch work variants (lib.rs:382-411, 962)

refute_note: Checked beacon_processor queue scheduling (single pop, batch variants only for attestations/aggregates) and the cells-to-verify view that avoids re-verifying already-known cells; neither batches concurrent gossip columns, so not stands.

title: Filter log events early and format without intermediate allocations
idea: In the logging layer, check whether an event is enabled for its target and output before any formatting, and write formatted output directly into one buffer (no color-then-strip, no intermediate Strings), so disabled or verbose subsystems cost little CPU.

title: Read head state by reference when computing scrape metrics
idea: Compute scrape-time metrics from the head state by borrowing it under the read lock or through read-only validator views, instead of cloning the beacon state or copying every validator, and fold validator counters into one pass.

title: Settable gauges updated on writes, not computed at scrape
idea: Update store-derived metrics (checkpoints, map sizes) into settable gauges when the store changes or at slot boundaries, so a metrics scrape never takes the store/fork-choice lock.

title: Demote or remove per-message logs on hot paths
idea: Log per-message, per-peer, per-attestation and per-validator-loop events at debug/trace or not at all, instead of info/warn, because they scale with peers and validators and their formatting and writing cost CPU and disk; metrics already cover the outcome.

title: Check log level before building expensive log arguments
idea: Before building expensive log arguments (serializing messages, collecting events, building field contexts, running DB queries for log data), check once whether the debug/trace level is enabled and skip the work if not, so hot paths do nothing for disabled logs.
measured_best: pr:caplin#24940: 64-step walk 7.55 us, 352 allocs -> 1.55 us, 0 allocs

title: Log only sparse progress during sync
idea: During range/backfill sync, do not log every block or request; log only epoch-start blocks or periodic progress, with an opt-in verbose flag.

idea: Do not attach tracing spans to long-running tasks or keep spans alive for long periods; keep only a few short root spans on key import paths, since long-lived spans accumulate memory.

Because MetricsLayer (and the debug file layer) has no level filter, those debug spans are live in the registry by default, not only at debug. Drop or shorten them, and give MetricsLayer an events-only filter.

title: Remove tracing spans from hot, cheap functions
idea: Do not create tracing spans around very frequent or trivial functions (DB has-checks, getters, per-signature or per-slot helpers, slasher loops), because span creation costs more than the work it measures.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:643 #[instrument(skip_all)] on cached_head_write_lock

title: Gzip-compress metrics endpoint responses

title: Prune pending lookup queue at finalization
idea: When finality advances, drop queued unknown-parent blocks and pending by-root roots (blocks or payloads) whose slot is at or below the finalized slot. This stops the node holding and re-requesting orphaned ancestors no peer will serve.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:718 prune_lookups = drop_lookups_without_peers + drop_stuck_lookups only, no finality check
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:107 SyncMessage has no finalization/new-finalized-checkpoint event
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1151 should_search_for_block filters by head-slot distance only while not synced, not by finalized slot
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:1095 WouldRevertFinalizedSlot/NotFinalizedDescendant only caught when a downloaded block is processed
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1089 prune_pending_unknown_roots is TTL only
gap: No finalization hook into sync: lookups and pending unknown roots at or below the new finalized slot are only removed after their block is downloaded and fails processing, by the no-peers/stuck timers, or by TTL. Add a finalization notification that calls drop_lookup_and_children for lookups whose known slot <= finalized slot (and drops pending roots not descending from finalized).
impact: Frees a few held lookups and avoids some by-root requests for orphaned ancestors after finality; small on a healthy node.
refute_note: Checked every SyncMessage variant, the prune interval path, should_search_for_block and the processing error mapping for any finality-driven pruning; none exists. Gossip blocks below finality are rejected before raising unknown-parent, which limits new entries but does not prune existing ones.

title: Expire pending blocks and lookups by age
idea: Give each pending unknown-parent block or lookup a maximum lifetime (TTL or max duration) and drop it, with its children, when it expires. This bounds the queue and frees state and peers held by stuck lookups.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:67 LOOKUP_MAX_DURATION_STUCK_SECS
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:71 LOOKUP_MAX_DURATION_NO_PEERS_SECS=10

title: Exponential backoff for failing by-root roots
idea: Track retry count and next-retry time per missing root in a bounded map, back off exponentially after failures and stop after a max count, servicing newest roots first. Stale unservable roots then stop consuming peer request slots every loop.
measured_best: Retry rate ~170 req/s from 82 stale roots; verified by unit tests only (pr:lodestar#9791)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:917 failed_downloading capped at SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=4
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:721 peers that already failed the request are de-prioritized
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:922 notified_unknown_roots dedups (peer, root) for 30s (NOTIFIED_UNKNOWN_ROOT_EXPIRY_SECONDS, manager.rs:93)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1059 record_unknown_root requires unknown_root_min_peers distinct peers before a new lookup
gap: Retries are count-capped, peer-deprioritized and event-driven (no polling loop), and re-triggers from attestations are throttled to once per (peer, root) per 30s plus corroboration. But there is no per-root memory of failure after a lookup is dropped and no exponential backoff, so an unservable root can be re-looked-up every ~30s per corroborating peer set. Add a bounded LRU of failed roots with attempt count and next-retry time checked in new_current_lookup.
impact: Small: Lighthouse does not have the poll-every-loop pattern that produced ~170 req/s in Lodestar; saves occasional repeat by-root requests for dead roots.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, found the 30s per-(peer,root) notification cache, the multi-peer corroboration gate and failed-peer deprioritization, which together act as a fixed-interval throttle but not a per-root exponential backoff.

title: Attestations for unknown root trigger block lookup

idea: Keep a set or state machine of in-flight lookups keyed by block root and skip creating another request for a root already being fetched or already queued (including delayed lookups and parent/child lookups). This removes duplicate concurrent downloads and processing of the same block.
