idea: Before issuing a by-root request, check gossip-seen caches, the pre-import and data-availability caches, fork choice and recently completed lookups, and skip or suppress the lookup if the block is already there. Gossip-delivered blocks are then not downloaded again via RPC once per attestation.

title: Request deepest missing ancestor directly
idea: When a block's parent is unknown, walk the locally held pending/queued blocks to the oldest missing ancestor and request only that root (processing queued parents first). This ends a parent-chain search in far fewer round trips than re-walking one block at a time.

title: Remember invalid and unviable blocks and forks
idea: Keep a cache of block roots and chains found invalid or unviable (failed lookups, bad parent) and refuse to look them up, request them or reprocess them again; remove them from missing tables and penalise peers that keep sending them.
measured_best: 86 low-score disconnects in ~30 min before, 0 after; 580 penalized empty responses -> 0 (pr:nimbus#9288)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:96 ignored_chains LRUTimeCache (from pr:lighthouse#1534), 60s expiry at mod.rs:61

gap: Only too-long lookup chains (60s), failed range chains (30s) and EL-invalid payloads (fork choice) are remembered. Blocks that fail consensus validation in a lookup (bad signature, state transition error, etc.) are retried up to 4 times, dropped with children, and not cached, so a later attestation/gossip can trigger the same download and verification. Insert penalty-bearing failed roots into a longer-lived lookup-side LRU and check it in new_current_lookup and search_parent_of_child.
impact: Stops repeated download and verification of invalid forks from misbehaving peers; modest CPU/bandwidth saving.
refute_note: Checked range sync failed_chains, fork choice invalid-payload tracking, the operator invalid_block_roots set and drop-with-children; none caches consensus-invalid roots for lookup sync.

title: Do not start RPC lookups from partial gossip
idea: When gossip has delivered only a block or one blob, do not start a delayed RPC lookup for the rest; let gossip deliver it, avoiding double downloads.

title: Bound pool size with hard cap and oldest-first eviction
idea: Put a hard cap on the number of attestations or gossip signatures held in the pool and evict the oldest slot or data root first (FIFO) when it is exceeded, with an O(1) size counter. This keeps memory bounded when finalization stalls or gossip floods.
measured_best: Devnet memory climbed to ~11.5 GB and crashed every ~27 min before; caps 4096/512 entries (pr:ethlambda#182)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:143 SLOTS_RETAINED=3

beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:638 stats() walks every map (no O(1) counter)
gap: The gossip-signature analogue (naive aggregation pool) has a hard per-slot cap but rejects new items rather than evicting oldest. The op pool has no entry cap, only a 2-epoch target window that does not depend on finalization, so it cannot grow without bound under a finality stall. Add a cap with oldest-slot eviction and an O(1) counter to AttestationMap.
impact: Low on Lighthouse: the time-based prune (not finality-based) plus observed_aggregators/observed_attesters dedup already bound pool size; a cap only guards pathological floods.
refute_note: Checked observed_aggregates/observed_attesters capacities and the naive pool cap; the ethlambda crash case (pool tied to finalization) does not apply because LH prunes by epoch, but no hard op-pool cap or FIFO eviction exists.

title: Skip attestations whose attesters are already on chain
idea: Track, per attestation data, the union of validators already included on chain (bitlists or index sets updated incrementally from imported blocks, with epoch-scale expiry) plus those already covered in the block being built, and reject, prune or skip pool attestations whose bits are all covered. The pool stays smaller and block packing does less work and carries no redundant attestations.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#6993)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:96 has_attested_in_epoch drops on-chain-covered validators at packing
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:62 zero-score items excluded

refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, found observed_block_attesters (on-chain attester set) and the gossip subset check; neither is used to drop pool entries covered on chain.

title: Remove block-included attestations from the pool on import
idea: When a block is imported (or becomes canonical on head change), delete its attestations from the op pool right away instead of waiting for expiry, decomposing post-Electra multi-committee attestations into per-committee aggregates so they match pool entries. The pool stays small and block production does not rescan or re-pack them.

refute_note: Listed every op pool pub fn and every op_pool.prune/remove call in beacon_chain; the only attestation removal is the epoch prune.

title: Aggregate attestations into pool entries on arrival
idea: When an unaggregated gossip attestation arrives, OR its bits and add its signature into an existing pool aggregate with the same data (keyed by attestation data), so the pool holds few large aggregates. Fewer objects are stored, hashed and compared, and an aggregator request becomes a lookup of a precomputed aggregate.

title: Aggregate lazily at block production or aggregator duty
idea: Store single-vote attestations separately, with no periodic background aggregation routine, and aggregate them only when an aggregate is requested or a block is produced, using hash tables keyed by attestation data and a temporary cache. No aggregation or signature deserialization is paid for aggregates that are never used.
measured_best: Speeds up iterating all attestations for a slot; improves aggregate quality and block packing (commit:nimbus@4ed2e34a9eb7)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2596,2699 single votes are aggregated eagerly on arrival, in both the naive pool and the op pool
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:380 Electra cross-committee aggregation is lazy, done only in get_attestations

title: Avoid duplicate aggregation passes per slot
idea: Do not aggregate the same unaggregated attestations twice in a slot (for example for fork choice and again for an aggregator request), do not re-aggregate an aggregate with itself, and do not reset aggregate expiry on update. Reuse the earlier result to cut CPU and keep the pool small.

impact: Saves a few hundred to a few thousand insert calls (index lookups plus clones) per produced block; only matters on proposer duty.

title: Aggregate only committees a local aggregator will request
idea: Pre-aggregate gossip attestations and sync messages only for (slot, committee/subnet) pairs with a subscribed local aggregator or an imminent local proposer, and skip messages from old slots or arriving after 2/3 of the slot. Aggregation work for other committees is skipped.

title: Index pool entries in hash maps by data root
idea: Index attestations (and other pool items) by attestation data root or id in a hash map, so existence checks and lookups are O(1) and do not rehash data or scan the list.

idea: Store pool entries in per-slot maps and, every slot, drop whole slots that fall outside the inclusion window by the current wall-clock slot (for every attestation variant), instead of per-entry TTL caches or finality-based pruning. The pool stays bounded even during non-finality.

title: Fast custom hash for attestation pool keys
idea: Key pool attestations with a fast non-SSZ hash of their fields instead of the generic SSZ hash_tree_root. Key computation becomes over 10x cheaper.

title: Fine-grained or concurrent locking in the op pool
idea: Put the locks inside the operation pool, per pool field or per attestation-data key, or use concurrent maps and lock-free groups, instead of one big lock around the whole pool on the chain. Gossip inserts and block production reads then do not contend on a single lock.

title: Greedy max-cover attestation selection by marginal reward
idea: When producing a block, select attestations from the op pool with a greedy maximum-coverage algorithm whose score is the marginal proposer reward (validators newly covered given those already chosen), instead of naive ordering. Blocks carry more rewarded attesters within the attestation limit.

title: Greedy packing instead of unbounded ILP solver
idea: Pack attestations with a greedy best-per-committee pass, and either drop the integer-programming/knapsack solver or cap its input (aggregates per data) so it fits a time budget. Packing CPU stays bounded with almost no loss of coverage.
measured_best: a plain best-per-committee greedy already covers 99.89% of observed attesters (pr:grandine#823)

beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:392 two greedy runs (prev/curr epoch) in rayon::join
gap: Input is not capped, so cost is O(limit*items*set size); a cap on aggregates per data would bound it.
impact: Packing is already greedy; a cap would only trim the worst case on a busy pool (block production, ms-level).

title: In-place bitfield operations in max-cover
idea: In the max-cover aggregation loop, mutate bitfields and candidate slices in place instead of allocating new bitlists and slices each step, and drop per-call length checks. This cuts allocations during aggregation and packing.
measured_best: Benchmarks show fewer allocations; ops/sec only relatively useful (pr:prysm#7938)

impact: Fewer allocations and hash-map work in block production packing; small absolute gain (tens of ms at most).

title: Compare and merge aggregates with bitfields, not indices
idea: Merge, compare and score aggregate participation (OR, subset, superset, intersection, unseen count) directly on committee-ordered aggregation bitfields, instead of expanding them to validator index arrays or Sets through committee lookups. Aggregates of one committee share bit positions so this is much cheaper.

title: Fast Electra committee-bits aggregation
idea: In post-Electra aggregation, skip committee-bit remapping when committee bits are equal, avoid recomputing committee start offsets and SSZ-hashing committee bits in superset checks, and OR aggregation bits directly on a bitset. Aggregation of many attestations gets faster with less memory.

beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:264 aggregate_same_committee unions bits with no committee remapping

974f78f/ssz/src/bitfield.rs:525 is_subset byte-wise, no tree hashing
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:279 cross-committee merge appends in increasing committee order, no offset recompute
gap: Residual micro-opt only: bitlist_extend (attestation_storage.rs:416, TODO) copies bits one at a time when merging disjoint committees, once per block production.

title: Electra cross-committee merge of aggregates at packing
idea: Post-Electra, group pooled aggregates by AttestationData and merge those with disjoint committee bits into one on-chain multi-committee attestation when packing, keeping all aggregates for that data rather than only the best one. Fewer, larger attestations fit more votes into the block.

beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs compute_on_chain_aggregate / aggregate_with_disjoint_committees

title: Key packing candidates by data and committee index
idea: Post-Electra, key attestation packing candidates by (AttestationData, committee index), not data alone, because all committees of a slot share the same data. Deduplicating by data alone drops most votes from the block.

title: Group by committee, cache validity, prune by score bound
idea: When selecting block attestations, group by (slot, committee index) so the committee is fetched once, track not-yet-seen attesters, cache validity per (head root, target epoch), and skip data whose maximum possible score is below the lowest included score. Worst-case selection drops from about 1s to about 100ms.

title: Check attestation targets without slot processing
idea: When validating or converting pooled attestations for packing or aggregation, get the target dependent root from block-root history or the nearest cached state and reuse cached target checkpoint states, instead of running slot processing to build a checkpoint state. This removes state-cache lock contention and CPU in block production.

title: Validate exits without cloning or advancing state
idea: Validate gossip and pool voluntary exits against the head state directly, without cloning it, skipping slots, or building a shuffling/epoch cache, since exit validity does not depend on slot processing.

idea: When packing operations from the pool into a block, check validity without signatures first, then verify all signatures as one batch, falling back to individual checks only if the batch fails.

title: Cache deserialized signatures of pooled attestations

title: Time-boxed lock-free block attestation packing
idea: Build block attestation aggregates without a global pool lock and under a time budget, sort by reward and take the top entries, then fill up with single attestations under a total budget, so block production latency is bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:381-387 attestations.write() held for aggregate_across_committees, then downgraded to a read lock that is held through packing (blocks insert_attestation writers at lib.rs:301)

beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:424 only prev/curr epoch packed in parallel (rayon::join)

Add a deadline to maximum_cover (return the best result so far) and/or take a snapshot of the per-checkpoint map so that packing does not hold the pool RwLock. refute_note: I also checked the block production call site for a timeout or a spawn_blocking deadline (none), and the max_cover internals for an early exit (none). Reward-sorted selection and insert-time aggregation exist, but the idea's core (time-boxed and lock-free) is absent.

title: Slasher bloom filter of data root for double votes

evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:443 slasher fed only after verify_attestation_signature (line ~495) when signature not already checked
slasher/src/attestation_queue.rs:14 MAX_VALIDATOR_INDEX cap and :84 drop out-of-range index
impact: Already done; no further gain.

title: Stack buffer for deterministic randomness seed
idea: Encode the deterministic-randomness seed into a fixed 8-byte stack buffer instead of a growable heap buffer, removing heap allocations in a hot helper.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#16695)
evidence: No deterministic-randomness helper; searched beacon_chain for seeded RNG, only rand in builder/test_utils
impact: Prysm's DeterministicRandomness helper has no Lighthouse counterpart; shuffling uses a fixed stack buffer in swap_or_not_shuffle/src/shuffle_list.rs:20-43.

title: Word-wide is-zero check for hashes
idea: Check whether a 32-byte hash is zero by comparing it as wide words (u64 chunks) instead of a byte-wise loop; this was 25% of time during sync.
measured_best: None (pr:nimbus#6682)
evidence: alloy-primitives-1.7.1/src/bits/fixed.rs:696 is_zero is `*self == Self::ZERO` (inlined, compiled to wide compares)
beacon_node/store/src/iter.rs:264 Hash256::is_zero use
impact: Hash256 is alloy FixedBytes; is_zero is a single array equality that LLVM vectorises, no byte loop.

title: Debug state dumps only for failed blocks
idea: When a debug flag dumps SSZ state and block per transition, persist only the failed transitions, since valid ones can be retrieved later and each full state is about 175MB.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#13720)
evidence: lighthouse/src/main.rs:337-346 dump-config flags only dump config; no per-transition SSZ state/block dump flag found in beacon_chain/src
impact: Lighthouse has no flag that dumps state and block per transition, so there is nothing to restrict to failed blocks.

title: FIFO eviction for recent block and blob caches
idea: Evict the recent-block and recent-blob caches in insertion order (FIFO) instead of LRU, so RPC reads of old entries cannot promote them and push out the newest blocks that gossip and import need.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:95
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:121
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:571
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:597
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:22
gap: BlockCache (block/blob/data_column) is hashlink LruCache and try_get_full_block both promotes on hit and inserts on miss, so any read (including RPC range serving) refreshes or adds entries. A FIFO (or peek-on-read) policy is absent; it only matters if block_cache_size is non-zero, which it is not by default.
impact: Negligible on default nodes (cache size 0); with the cache enabled, keeps the newest blocks resident under RPC read load.
refute_note: Checked every BlockCache use in hot_cold_store.rs: reads go through LruCache::get and misses insert, no peek path. The import path uses DA checker and fork choice rather than this cache, so there is no other recent-block cache with FIFO semantics.

title: LRU eviction for epoch and shuffling caches
idea: Evict the least-recently-used entry from the per-epoch shuffling/committee caches instead of the oldest epoch, so work alternating between two forks or epochs does not keep evicting each other and force repeated shuffling recomputation.
measured_best: pr:nimbus#4196: "blocking of over 5 minutes in extreme cases" with the old oldest-first policy
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:128
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:143
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:254
gap: ShufflingCache::get does not record use; prune_cache sorts by shuffling_epoch and evicts oldest non-head entries. Add recency tracking and evict least-recently-used non-head entries.
impact: Marginal: 16 entries keyed by (epoch, decision block), head ids protected, and states carry their own committee caches, so thrashing needs many concurrent forks.
refute_note: Re-read get/insert/prune in shuffling_cache.rs and the http_api historical committees LruCache (caches.rs:23, separate API-only cache). Head-id protection mitigates but the eviction policy is still oldest-epoch, not LRU.

title: Bounded LRU unviable-block set with reason
idea: Keep invalid/orphaned (unviable) block roots in a fixed-capacity LRU map and record why each is unviable, so gossip can reject descendants of known-bad blocks immediately without re-validating, at bounded memory.
measured_best: pr:nimbus#7685: use minilru instead of OrderedTable for simplified capacity management and performance (no numbers)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pre_finalization_cache.rs:9
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pre_finalization_cache.rs:24
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1842
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1277
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:96
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:77
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1512
gap: A bounded (512) LRU of orphaned pre-finalization roots exists (PreFinalizationBlockCache), but it has no reason field and is consulted only by attestation verification, not gossip block verification. Consensus-invalid roots are remembered only by sync's time-expiring ignored_chains/failed_chains. Missing: one capacity-bounded root->reason map checked in gossip block verification for parents, fed by failed imports.
impact: Saves repeated lookups and re-validation of descendants of known-bad blocks; only matters under attack or after invalid-block forks.
refute_note: Found PreFinalizationBlockCache (bounded hashlink LRU of unviable pre-finalization roots, fed from check_block_against_finalized_slot) that the earlier review missed; it strengthens partial but does not cover gossip descendants or record reasons.

title: Cache total active balance per epoch
idea: Compute total active balance once per epoch and cache it (in the epoch/committee cache or keyed by epoch and decision root) instead of summing effective balances of all active validators on every call.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:819 total_active_balance: Option<(Epoch,u64)> cache field
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2682 get_total_active_balance_at_epoch reads cache
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2703 set_total_active_balance set by single-pass epoch processing
impact: Already computed once per epoch and cached in state.

title: Cache attestation data responses per slot
idea: Cache the attestation data API response per (slot, head/committee) so the many validators asking for the same slot share one computation, and enable this cache by default.
measured_best: pr:prysm#2542: hit 29796 vs miss 894 in cluster
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:256
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:284

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2126
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2157
gap: The Lighthouse VC already fetches attestation data once per slot (index 0) and shares it across all its validators, and the BN fast path reads it from the head snapshot or early_attester_cache. Missing: a BN-side (slot, head root) response cache, so many separate VCs (other clients, DVT) still each run produce_unaggregated_attestation, and the off-epoch case repeats get_advanced_hot_state + partial_state_advance.

refute_note: Checked the VC side the earlier review skipped: attestation_service.rs produces one AttestationData per slot for all duties, which is the sharing the idea targets for Lighthouse's own VC. BN has no response cache, so partial rather than not.

title: Read-only head state for active validator count
idea: Compute the active validator count (and similar hot-path reads) from a read-only reference to the head state instead of cloning the full head state.
measured_best: pr:prysm#14592: about 500 MB less memory allocated on holesky
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:389 active_validator_count reads cached indices from the Arc head snapshot, no clone
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:748 only state_at_slot (beacon_chain.rs:1536) clones, and the clone is milhouse structural sharing
impact: None needed.

title: Compact raw-byte keys for pubkey and byte-keyed caches
idea: Key the pubkey-to-validator-index map and similar in-memory caches (e.g. blob availability index) by raw fixed-size byte arrays with a fast hash, optionally in native/off-heap memory, instead of hex strings or other heavy intermediate representations. This cuts per-key memory and hashing/allocation cost.
measured_best: ~1400 bytes/key, ~350 MB for 250k concatenated string keys avoided (pr:lodestar#3561)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:25 indices: HashMap<PublicKeyBytes, usize> keyed by raw 48-byte array
validator_pubkey_cache.rs:26 pubkey_bytes: Vec<PublicKeyBytes> flat
impact: Raw fixed-size keys already used; only the default SipHash hasher could be swapped for small gain.

title: Batch map operations under one lock
idea: Provide closure-style helpers that run several operations on a shared map under one lock acquisition, instead of taking the lock separately for each get/insert.
measured_best: pr:prysm#11953: GenericTx 25881 ns/op vs 53586 ns/op for separate locks (about 2x)
evidence: Rust lock guards (parking_lot Mutex/RwLock) already allow several map ops under one guard, e.g. beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:175 uses one lock scope

title: Well-distributed hash for committee cache keys
idea: Hash composite (slot, committee index) cache keys with a function that mixes both fields so keys do not collide into few buckets, and use a simple LRU map for the committee cache.
measured_best: pr:teku#3758: Block import 21.2 -> 18.6 ms/block (~13%); getCommitteeHit 8.47M -> 25.0M ops/s
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:128 HashMap keyed by AttestationShufflingId, 16 entries
consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:26 CommitteeCache per epoch, no (slot,index) key
impact: None; the keying problem does not exist. Lighthouse caches one CommitteeCache per epoch shuffling id, not per (slot, committee index).

title: Bound quarantine missing-parent retry tables
idea: Bound the tables of missing parents/payloads that quarantines retry fetching, with a max capacity and capped exponential backoff, so unresolved items cannot grow memory or request load without limit.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:95 MAX_PENDING_UNKNOWN_ROOTS=1024 LRU plus TTL pruning
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:77 MAX_LOOKUPS=200

beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:59 PARENT_DEPTH_TOLERANCE and :71 no-peer timeout
impact: None needed; bounded by lookup count, attempt cap and timeouts (no exponential backoff, but retries are capped).

title: Cap gossip block buffer by count
idea: Cap the number of gossip-received blocks held in memory awaiting processing and purge the oldest once over the limit.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:384 gossip_block_queue length 1024, drops when full
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:78 MAXIMUM_QUEUED_BLOCKS=16 early-block queue, drops new ones when full
impact: None needed; bounded by count (drops newest instead of purging oldest, same memory bound).

title: Byte-weighted budget for pending block pool
idea: Bound the unknown-parent pending block pool by total retained SSZ bytes as well as item count, evicting oldest first and rejecting oversized items, so memory is capped regardless of block size.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:78
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:670
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:77
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:351
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:246
gap: All pending-block holders (reprocess queue 16 blocks, lookups 200, DA pending components) are count-capped; per-item size is bounded only by the gossip/RPC max message size. No total-SSZ-bytes budget with oldest-first eviction.
impact: Only tightens worst-case memory with maximum-size blocks; count caps times max message size already bound it.
refute_note: Searched network, beacon_processor and DA checker for any byte accounting (ssz_bytes_len, byte budgets): none. Oversized items are rejected by gossipsub max_transmit_size, which covers the reject-oversized part of the idea.

title: Bound beacon processor and sync work queues
idea: Put explicit length limits on the queues and in-flight work between network, sync and the beacon processor so bursts of blocks, blobs or lookups cannot grow without bound or starve other work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:82 DEFAULT_MAX_WORK_EVENT_QUEUE_LEN 16384 and per-queue limits
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:762 bounded idle channel
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:78-90 MAXIMUM_QUEUED_* caps
commit e31b5d0ca196 is an ancestor of HEAD
impact: Already bounds memory and starvation under bursts; nothing further to gain.

title: Bounded seen-message dedup caches for gossip
idea: Back gossip seen-message dedup sets (attestations per validator/target epoch, aggregators, exits, slashings, blocks) with bounded caches instead of unbounded maps, so duplicates are dropped cheaply with capped memory; reuse epoch-boundary checkpoint states from a cache keyed by (epoch, root).
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_attesters.rs:26 MAX_CACHED_EPOCHS=4 auto-pruning epoch containers
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_attesters.rs:88 EpochBitfield per-validator bitfield
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_block_producers.rs:33 pruned on finalization
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_operations.rs:27 HashSet cleared at fork boundary
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:436-468 observed_* fields
impact: Gossip duplicates are dropped cheaply with bounded memory already. Exits/slashings sets only reset at fork boundaries (small in practice). Checkpoint-state cache part is covered by store state cache, not analysed.

title: Cache shuffling and committees once per epoch
idea: Compute the shuffled active validator list and the committees (plus per-epoch counts such as committees per slot) once per epoch, cache them in one shared cache keyed by epoch/decision root, and slice committees from it for state transition, attestation validation and duties. This avoids reshuffling per state or per lookup and avoids duplicate shuffled-index caches.
measured_best: pr:nimbus#316: ~2x state_sim speedup (12m26 -> ~8m with start_shard_cache and committee count)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:26 one CommitteeCache per epoch holds shuffling, positions, committees_per_slot
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2824 build_committee_cache builds once per epoch, Arc-shared
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5211 import_block_update_shuffling_cache_fallible primes ShufflingCache keyed by decision root
impact: Already in place; committees are sliced from the cached shuffling.

title: One shared cache of decompressed validator pubkeys
idea: Keep a single process-wide cache of decompressed BLS pubkey points per validator index, sized for the whole validator set and shared by state transition, signature verification, slasher and other components. BLS paths then never decompress the 48-byte key or re-fetch it per verification.
measured_best: pr:teku#3314: "speedup ~x50-x100" (partial fix of #3294)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:23 ValidatorPubkeyCache Vec<PublicKey> decompressed, indexed by validator index
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:144 parallel decompression at first startup
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs (pubkey cache used via validator_pubkey_cache field by gossip and block verification)
gap: Block processing in consensus/state_processing still decompresses in a few non-hot spots (per_block_processing.rs:153 closure fallback, deposits signature_sets.rs:549), which is expected for new keys.
impact: Hot BLS paths avoid decompression already; the slasher does not need pubkeys.

title: Next-epoch proposer indices warm in the proposer cache
idea: At the epoch boundary (or earlier), compute the next epoch's proposer indices and keep both current and next epoch in the proposer cache, so the first duties/block request of an epoch does not compute them cold.
measured_best: removes >500ms GetDuty delay at slot 0 (pr:prysm#12484)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:355-395 computes current and next epoch proposer shuffling in state advance
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:26 LRU of 16 keyed (epoch, decision root)
gap: Next-epoch pre-compute only happens post-Fulu (state.slot() > next_epoch_decision_slot); pre-Fulu the next epoch depends on randao at the boundary so it cannot be known earlier.
impact: First duties request of an epoch is served warm.

title: Sync committee cache keyed by period root
idea: Key the sync committee cache by the block root at the start of the sync period instead of the hash tree root of the committee, so a lookup needs no state copy and no tree hashing.
measured_best: pr:prysm#9128: Saves one copy and one hash tree root per lookup
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753 get_sync_committee_indices resolves pubkeys through pubkey_cache each call
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:472 subcommittee_positions_for_public_key scans the committee
consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_committee.rs:70 linear scan
gap: Lighthouse has no cache keyed by sync period root. The committee lives in the state (Arc) so lookups need no state copy or tree hash; the cost that remains is the per-lookup pubkey scan. A period-root keyed cache of (committee, validator->positions) in BeaconChain would fix it; see other_caches-060.
impact: Small: no copy/hash per lookup already, since the state holds the committee in an Arc. Gain is only avoiding repeated scans.

title: Committee cache invalidation only when needed
idea: Make sure the committee-per-slot cache is not cleared on every state transition, only when its key actually changes, and do not re-broadcast already-seen gossip messages.
measured_best: pr:teku#711: enabled 4 node test to finalize
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2824 build_committee_cache only builds when the cached epoch differs (Arc<CommitteeCache> kept across slots)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5220 skips insert if shuffling id already cached
impact: Already done; committee caches are rebuilt only on epoch change, and gossip dedup exists via observed_* caches.

title: Dynamic committee cache size during non-finality
idea: Size the committee/shuffling cache small by default and grow it only when the chain is not finalizing, instead of permanently using a large capacity.
measured_best: pr:prysm#13640: significantly less memory
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:25 DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 16 fixed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:169 shuffling_cache_size static; shuffling_cache.rs:247 prune to fixed cache_size
gap: ShufflingCache::new takes a fixed cache_size and prune uses it; make cache_size a function of finalization distance (update in the head-update path) and shrink back when finalizing.
impact: Memory only: each entry is a few MB at 1M validators; 16 entries is already small, so saving is tens of MB at best. Non-finality growth is a resilience gain, not speed.

title: Concurrent caches instead of synchronized LRU
idea: Replace globally synchronized LRU caches on hot paths (state transition caches, finalized state cache, db block/validator caches) with a concurrent cache (Caffeine/ristretto-style), so a slow miss on one key does not block readers of other keys.
measured_best: pr:teku#10225: Stated bottleneck only: synchronized get blocks all threads on a slow fallback; JMH benchmarks added, no numbers in text
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:571 block cache lock taken only for the map get; DB load and full-block rebuild happen outside the lock
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:82 state_cache is Mutex<StateCache> with short critical sections
impact: Not worth it: Rust Mutex sections are short and slow misses are not computed under the lock, so the Java synchronized-fallback blocking problem does not occur.

title: Evict empty reprocess queue entries
idea: In the delayed-work reprocess queue, remove the per-block-root entry when its last queued attestation times out, so entries for never-imported blocks do not leak.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1265-1281 removes empty Vec entry from awaiting_attestations_per_root on expiry
impact: Prevents the per-root map leak; negligible CPU, bounded memory.

title: Fixed growth step for pubkey cache
idea: Grow the validator pubkey cache by a fixed step instead of doubling capacity, avoiding a huge copy and over-reservation at mainnet registry size.
measured_best: commit:lodestar@133ef248a5e6: Doubling would copy ~450MB at mainnet scale
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:111 reserve(validator_keys.len()) on Vec (amortized, can still double) and HashMap
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:57 load_from_store pushes with no reserve
gap: validator_pubkey_cache load_from_store pushes without capacity and import_new_pubkeys uses Vec::reserve (amortized doubling); use reserve_exact or preallocate from the state's validator count.
impact: Only matters at startup/rare growth: avoids one transient copy of a few hundred MB and some over-reserved memory.

title: Per-period cache of validators' sync committee positions
idea: Compute once per sync committee period each validator index's positions/subcommittee indices in the current and next sync committee and keep them in the state caches. Is-in-committee checks, subnet computation, selection-proof validation, gossip validation and aggregation then are lookups instead of scanning committee pubkeys.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:472 subcommittee_positions_for_public_key per message
consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_committee.rs:70 iterates all 512 pubkeys comparing 48 byte keys
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753 get_sync_committee_indices does 512 pubkey_cache lookups per block (altair/sync_committee.rs:50)
http_api/src/sync_committees.rs:307 same scan per duty
gap: Add a per-period cache (validator_index -> subnet positions, plus the committee index vector) stored in BeaconState caches or BeaconChain; use it in verify gossip sync messages, process_sync_aggregate (get_sync_committee_indices) and the HTTP duties.
impact: Cuts a 512-key scan per gossiped sync message (thousands per slot on mainnet) and 512 hashtrie lookups per block; likely sub-ms per slot of CPU, small but cheap.

title: Feed light client server only from new head blocks
idea: Compute and import light client server data only for blocks that become the new head, not for every imported block. Blocks that never become canonical then cost no light client work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4786-4796 cache_state_data runs for every imported block (no head check)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:59-75 cache_state_data computes finality/sync-committee proofs via LightClientCachedData::from_state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:467-477 from_state computes three merkle proofs per block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5176-5190 producer event sent for any block with delay < 32 slots, not only new heads
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:141-160 updates only kept if is_latest by (attested_slot, signature_slot), a slot heuristic rather than fork-choice head
gap: Neither cache_state_data nor the update producer is gated on the block becoming the new head; only a recency filter (<32 slots) and a slot-based is_latest check exist. Gate both (or move them) to run after recompute_head when the block is the canonical head, or compute proofs lazily on demand.
impact: Only on --light-client-server nodes; avoids per-block proof computation and update recompute (DB block reads, sync committee store writes) for non-canonical blocks, a few percent of blocks.

title: Size shuffling cache for forks; compute each once
idea: Size the committee shuffling cache to hold several epochs across many forks (and long non-finality), and make a miss compute-once so concurrent requesters wait instead of recomputing. Late attestations and forks then do not evict and recompute shufflings repeatedly.
measured_best: shuffling ~6% CPU, ~20 computes/epoch reduced to 1 (pr:teku#5892)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:25 DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE=16
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:287 create_promise and oneshot waiters for compute-once
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:257 prune_cache keeps head ids, prunes oldest epochs
gap: Cache size is 16 entries, below teku long-non-finality sizing, but misses are deduplicated by promises (MAX_CONCURRENT_PROMISES=2 rejects extra instead).
impact: Duplicate shuffling computation already avoided.

title: Dependent-root keyed shuffling cache with lookahead
idea: Key the shuffling cache by the dependent (decision) root, separate from larger per-epoch data, and compute it ahead when the determining block is processed. Attestations on non-canonical forks then need no state replay, and forks sharing a dependent root share one shuffling.
measured_best: lower memory by sharing shufflings between EpochRefs of same dependent root (no numbers) (pr:nimbus#3990)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:143 keyed by AttestationShufflingId (epoch + shuffling_decision_block)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:395-420 inserts next-epoch committee cache ahead of time
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:489 insertion at block import
gap: Cache stores Arc<CommitteeCache>, so forks with same decision root share one shuffling; there is no separate smaller per-epoch structure, but sharing exists.
impact: Attestations on forks with same decision root need no state replay.

title: Persist pubkeys uncompressed to skip startup decompression
idea: Store validator pubkeys in uncompressed (or checksummed flat snapshot) form on disk and load them directly at startup, avoiding decompressing every BLS key on restart.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:94 DatabasePubkey stores serialize_uncompressed()
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:55 load_from_store loads via deserialize_uncompressed (no decompress)
validator_pubkey_cache.rs:~142 first import decompresses in parallel with rayon
impact: Restart already skips decompression of every key.

title: Parallel pubkey decompression when building pubkey cache
idea: When building the validator pubkey cache from a fresh checkpoint state, decompress the pubkeys in parallel on a thread pool, since serial decompression of every key dominates startup.
measured_best: Sepolia validator_pubkey_cache_new 109.64ms -> 21ms; Hoodi import 12.77s vs >120s timeout (pr:lighthouse#8451)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:117 is_initial_import when cache empty
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:148 into_par_iter rayon decompression
impact: Startup pubkey cache build from a checkpoint state is parallel; already captured.

title: Configurable light client data retention period
idea: Make the number of sync committee periods of light client data the beacon node keeps configurable, so operators can retain fewer and shorten LC data computation during import and sync.
measured_best: lowering below default speeds up import (no numbers) (pr:nimbus#3799)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:88 only enable_light_client_server bool
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:831-885 get_light_client_update(s) read per period, no retention setting

title: Don't block pubkey cache readers while adding new keys
idea: When block import adds new validators to the pubkey cache, hold only a read (upgradable) lock or a separate lock while decompressing and persisting new keys, upgrading to write only when needed, so attestation verification readers are not blocked.
measured_best: small improvement in attestation verification times (pr:lighthouse#6190)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4487 upgradable_read then upgrade only if state.validators().len() > cache.len()
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:91-101,128-131 import and decompress run inside &mut self; DB write deferred as StoreOp
gap: Upgradable read and DB write deferral exist, but upgrade happens before decompression, so readers are blocked during decompression of new keys. Decompress the new keys (from state.validators().iter_from(len)) while only holding the upgradable guard, then upgrade just to push into pubkeys/pubkey_bytes/indices in import_new_pubkeys.
impact: Slightly shorter write-lock hold on blocks that add validators (a few per block, decompression is tens of microseconds each); small attestation verification latency gain.

title: Precompute own committee duties per dependent root
idea: Cache the node's own validators' committee membership keyed by dependent root and do the precomputation and pruning on a dedicated executor, off the block/attestation processing path.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:323 type DependentRoot = Hash256

title: Check cache before recompute or reinsert
idea: Before computing a value for a cache (proposer indices, committees, pubkeys), check whether the key already exists and return early, skipping the duplicate computation, validation and locked write.

title: Proposer index from pre-advanced next-slot state

title: Block cache holding only most recent blocks
idea: Restrict the in-memory block cache to the most recent blocks (about 3 epochs) so lookups for the recent chain hit more often with the same memory.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:95-125 BlockCache is an LRU keyed by root, not age bounded
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:22 DEFAULT_BLOCK_CACHE_SIZE = 0 and cli.rs:794 default 0 so disabled by default

title: In-memory block and state-root maps before DB
idea: Check in-memory maps for hot block and state-root lookups before going to the database, so frequent lookups skip SSZ decode/encode.

Could add small in-memory root maps in HotColdDB for the unfinalized range.

title: Stream validator comparison in state diffs
idea: When diffing two states' validator registries, compare them by streaming through iterators instead of materializing both validator lists, lowering peak allocation.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:102 HDiffBuffer holds validators: Vec<Validator>
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:185 from_state does take_validators().to_vec()
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:439-450 ValidatorsDiff::compute single pass over slices emitting only changed entries

title: Send forkchoiceUpdated once per sync batch
idea: During range/initial sync, do not send engine forkchoiceUpdated after every imported block; send it once per batch (for its last block, in the background) or once at the end of sync. This cuts EL round trips during bulk import.

title: Pipeline batch download concurrently with import
idea: Decouple range-sync block fetching from block processing with a queue or batch state machine, so the next batches download from peers while earlier batches are imported in order. Network wait and import overlap instead of alternating.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE=5 batches queued ahead
network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:474 processing_target/to_be_downloaded advance separately

title: Self rate-limit outgoing by-range requests per peer
idea: Throttle outgoing blocks/blobs-by-range requests to each peer to the quota that peer enforces, counting cost the way the responder does (slots times max blobs, adjusted for empty slots), and schedule a retry exactly when the quota replenishes. Requests are not rejected, penalised or disconnected, and the node does not wait longer than needed.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs:34-130 SelfRateLimiter queues and retries via DelayQueue at wait_time
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/rate_limiter.rs:394-399 cost = max_responses
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/protocol.rs:858-866 BlocksByRange count, BlobsByRange max_blobs_requested
gap: Cost does not adjust for empty slots, and quotas are our configured ones, not learned from the peer.
impact: Avoids rate-limit penalties on sync peers; throttling already exists, so little extra gain.

title: Filter sync peers by earliest available slot
idea: Before assigning by-range requests (blocks, blobs, columns, envelopes, backfill), compare the requested slots with each peer's advertised earliest_available_slot and skip peers that cannot serve them. Requests are not wasted on peers that answer ResourceUnavailable.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb/sync_status.rs:35-40 has_slot vs earliest_available_slot
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:255-264 synced_peers_for_epoch used by backfill (backfill_sync/mod.rs:225,883) and custody backfill (custody_backfill_sync/mod.rs:1042)

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:297-312 good_custody_subnet_peer filters by available slot; used for range columns via custody-by-root (network_context/custody.rs:364, network_context.rs:418-421)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476-495 forward range block/blob/envelope peer pick has no has_slot filter
gap: Forward range sync picks its blocks/blobs/envelopes peer from chain.peers without has_slot; filter block_peers in block_components_by_range_request with is_synced_or_advanced_with_available_slot(batch start slot).
impact: Avoids wasted by-range requests to peers that answer ResourceUnavailable (checkpoint-synced or pruned peers); small, since forward sync starts near our own finalized slot.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review: range-sync data columns are fetched by custody-by-root whose peer set is already filtered by earliest_available_slot, and custody backfill also filters; only the forward-range block peer is unfiltered.

title: Skip range requests for already known or queued blocks
idea: When new block roots or gossip blocks arrive during sync, check whether the block or its parent is already known or queued (keyed by root) and only request the span that is new. This avoids duplicate downloads and lookups.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/peer_sync_info.rs:49-80 remote_sync_type skips peers whose head is known to fork choice

beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/sync_type.rs:28 Finalized only if finalized root unknown

title: Clip sidecar requests to DA window and fork
idea: Clip blob and data-column by-range requests (and column sync work) to slots that are inside the data availability retention window and in the fork that uses that sidecar type (no blobs pre-Deneb or post-Fulu). No requests go out for data peers do not have to serve; also re-request payload envelopes evicted from cache.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1296-1318 batch_type picks Blocks/BlocksAndBlobs/BlocksAndColumns per epoch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:574-587 DA boundary + fork gating for blobs/columns

refute_note: Also checked the coupling: columns are fetched per data-bearing block via custody-by-root, a finer clip than slot ranges, but it applies no DA-window check on Gloas; no envelope re-request on eviction exists in network/src/sync.

title: Choose range or by-root sync by distance
idea: When a peer is only a few slots or epochs ahead, use head sync or by-root fetches instead of a full finalized range sync; when it is further behind, fetch the gap with blocks-by-range at max request size instead of many by-root requests. Each gap size uses the cheaper method.

beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:432-455 FullySynced with unknown head uses by-root lookup, Advanced uses range sync

title: Batch-verify signatures across a whole sync segment
idea: Pass a complete downloaded range-sync batch to the chain as one segment, collect the signature sets of all its blocks and verify them in one batched BLS job (in worker threads) alongside the state transition. One batched verification is much cheaper than per-block verification.
measured_best: Quoted: verifyImport 3.6543 s/op vs 6.6473 s/op (ratio 0.55); roughly 8s to 4s for 32 blocks (pr:lodestar#3989)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:671-740 signature_verify_chain_segment collects all block signature sets into one verifier and verifies once
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3202 process_chain_segment

title: Couple block and sidecar downloads per batch
idea: For each range-sync batch, request blocks and blob/column sidecars concurrently, buffer them until all are complete, and submit the batch to the processor only when fully downloaded, storing sidecars before importing their blocks. Import does not refetch sidecars or fail on partial batches.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:28-38 RangeBlockComponentsRequest buffers blocks+blobs/columns/envelopes until complete

impact: Already avoids partial-batch import and refetch.

title: Request sidecars only for blocks with commitments
idea: When building blob or data-column by-range requests, skip blocks (and whole batches) without KZG commitments and missed slots, and request only the (block, column) pairs still missing per peer instead of the union over the range.

beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:493-540 blobs by range only for BlocksAndBlobs batch type

title: Request blocks in ranged batches, not singly
idea: During sync, request and serve many blocks per BlocksByRange message in bounded chunks and import them in bulk, instead of one block per request/response. This cuts round trips.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1, one BlocksByRange of up to 32 blocks per request
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:461 block_components_by_range_request

title: Use larger blocks-per-request batch size
idea: Raise the number of blocks (or blobs) asked for per by-range request to the peer rate-limit maximum (for example 64 blocks) and use arbitrary-length batches instead of epoch-sized units, halving request count.
measured_best: ~70-80 blk/s sync, occasionally 100; half as many requests (pr:prysm#5978)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1 (32 blocks) while max_request_blocks is 1024
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:236 comment assumes EPOCHS_PER_BATCH==1
gap: Raise EPOCHS_PER_BATCH (or make count arbitrary) in range_sync/chain.rs and revisit BatchInfo epoch-based ids, the custody-by-root block_epoch assumption in RangeBlockComponentsRequest::continue_requests, and batch timeout/peer scoring for larger responses.
impact: Fewer round trips during sync (up to half the requests at 64 blocks); gain depends on peer latency, likely modest since 5 batches already pipeline.

title: Cap items per outgoing by-range request
idea: Limit the number of blocks or columns per by-range request (for example 512 column items) and page through larger ranges, so responders do not reject oversized requests and responses stay bounded in memory.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1 so each by-range request is 32 slots
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:448 to_blocks_by_range_request count=end-start
Fulu columns fetched by custody-by-root after blocks arrive (network_context.rs:~540 comment), no large by-range column requests
impact: Requests are structurally bounded to one epoch; nothing further to gain.

title: Bound download lookahead ahead of processing
idea: Limit how many range-sync batches or slots are downloaded ahead of the processed head (for example 4 batches, or a bounded slot window started when the previous target is processed), and enforce that limit in the send path. This bounds memory and wasted bandwidth when a batch fails.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE=5
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1188-1215 include_next_batch counts Downloading|AwaitingProcessing against the buffer
impact: Bounds memory and wasted bandwidth already.

title: Cap concurrent in-flight sync requests per peer
idea: Track in-flight sync requests per peer (and per protocol), mark a peer at its limit as busy, and assign new batches only to free peers. Downloads spread over peers and do not queue at one peer or trip its rate limit.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:97-118 ActiveRequestsPerPeer/at_concurrency_limit
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476-490 blocks_by_range peer pick sorts at-limit peers last
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:595-606 same for data_columns_by_range
gap: Peers at MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS are only de-prioritised (tuple sort key), not excluded; if every chain peer is at the limit the request is still sent and queues at the peer. Making it strict would mean returning NoPeer/leaving the batch AwaitingDownload in block_components_by_range_request and retrying on request completion.
impact: Avoids rate-limit rejections and queueing when few peers serve a chain; small effect on mainnet sync with many peers.

title: Skip per-slot tick work while syncing
idea: Maintain a cheap is-syncing flag set as soon as sync starts, and have per-slot tick handlers read it to skip fork choice, duties and other per-slot work during sync, instead of computing a full peer-based sync status each tick. Resources go to catching up.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7491 per_slot_task returns early when best_slot + MAX_PER_SLOT_FORK_CHOICE_DISTANCE < slot (before recompute_head_at_current_slot)
impact: Already skips per-slot fork choice during sync with a cheap local slot comparison; no peer-based status computed in the tick.

title: Sync columns from minimal covering peer set
idea: Choose the smallest set of peers whose custody covers the needed data columns and sync columns from them, rather than querying many peers.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:588-627 select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request picks the min of (deprioritized, at_limit, rand::random per column per peer) independently for each column, so range requests fragment across peers

beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:237-239,381 by-root custody path uses one RandomState per request (hash_one) so the same peer ranking applies to every column and columns cluster on the top-ranked custodian ('avoiding fragmentation'); not a set cover and not used by range sync
gap: Range sync column requests still choose a random custodian per column. Minimal step: reuse the by-root per-request RandomState ordering in select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request; full step: greedy set cover over peers' custody columns.
impact: Fewer, larger DataColumnsByRange requests per batch on PeerDAS nodes; less request overhead and rate-limit pressure; modest sync throughput gain.
refute_note: Found an anti-fragmentation mechanism (consistent per-request peer ranking) in the by-root custody lookup path, which the earlier review cited but did not credit; it is absent from the range path, so the verdict for range sync stays not, with lower effort since the pattern can be ported.

title: Do not advance sync on unverified empty responses
idea: Treat a dropped connection during a range request as a failure, and require empty responses from several distinct peers before advancing past a range, so the queue does not skip real blocks and refetch them later.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:270,296,517 in-flight RPC streams end with RPCError::Disconnected on connection close
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:916-975 inject_error marks the batch download_failed and re-requests it, so a dropped connection is a failure, not an empty batch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:141-145 empty batches stay AwaitingValidation until a later batch imports a block
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:575-592 empty batch does not advance_chain
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:800-845 handle_invalid_batch re-requests all unvalidated earlier batches and scores the original peer in advance_chain:711-750
gap: The disconnect-as-failure half is implemented. Lighthouse does not ask a second peer to confirm an empty batch before moving on; a falsely empty batch is found only when the next batch fails, and then all unvalidated batches are refetched.
impact: Avoids occasional redownload of ranges after a falsely empty response; rare, small saving.
refute_note: Confirmed in the RPC handler that disconnects surface as RPCError::Disconnected and fail the batch, so the first half of the idea is done; no multi-peer empty confirmation exists.

title: Ignore gossip blocks as sync triggers while range syncing
idea: During initial/range sync, do not subscribe to or act on gossip blocks for triggering fetches; trigger new range requests only from blocks sync itself imported. This avoids duplicate processing and spurious requests.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:772-780 subscribe_core_topics only once sync state is Synced
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1156-1175 should_search_for_block ignores unknown-block triggers far from head when not synced
impact: Gossip blocks do not drive range requests during initial sync.

title: Cheap batch attempt hashing
idea: Compute the identity hash of a downloaded sync batch from block tree-hash roots (cached per block/envelope) concatenated into one preallocated buffer, instead of SSZ-serialising blocks or manual byte loops. This avoids large temporary allocations.
measured_best: byteArrayConcat 2.03 ns/op vs Buffer.concat 1.35 ns/op (pr:lodestar#4343)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:65-69 batch_attempt_hash uses DefaultHasher over the data
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification_types.rs:63-66 Hash for RangeSyncBlock hashes only the cached block_root
impact: No SSZ serialisation or large buffers; already the cheap form.

title: Check batch is parent-linked chain before import
idea: Sort a downloaded batch and verify that each block's parent root links to the previous block before any state transition; reject the batch and switch away from the peer on failure. Invalid or orphaned batches are rejected cheaply.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3079-3112 filter_chain_segment checks block_root == child parent_root and strictly increasing slots (NonLinearParentRoots/NonLinearSlots) before signature verification or state transition
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:960 NonLinearParentRoots mapped to peer-fault
impact: Already cheap-rejects non-linked batches; the check is in beacon_chain, not in the sync layer before queueing, but is before any heavy work.

title: Align sync batches to epoch boundaries
idea: Choose range-sync batch boundaries so all blocks in a processing segment are in the same epoch, so they share one shuffling/committee cache for batch signature verification.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1, batch ids are epochs
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3236-3245 segment partitioned into same-epoch runs for signature verification
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:668 signature_verify_chain_segment requires same epoch
impact: Batches are epoch-aligned and segments split by epoch, so one shuffling is used per signature-verification batch.

title: Keep latest state in memory during initial sync
idea: During initial sync, keep the latest state in an in-memory cache instead of writing the state to the database after every block.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1667 store_hot_state puts state into state_cache
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1749-1757 only summary written; full state/diff only at hierarchy boundaries
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4752 PutState per block
impact: Full states are not written per block; only a small summary, plus a diff/snapshot at hdiff layer boundaries.

title: Download ranges from several peers in parallel
idea: Track the heads of all suitable peers and send block-by-range requests to several of them concurrently (round-robin), instead of syncing serially from a single peer. Total download time is bounded by the slowest parallel request, not the sum.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE=5 batches in flight
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:478-498 block_components_by_range_request picks a peer per batch, random tie-break, de-prioritising busy/failed peers
impact: Batches from a chain's peer set are downloaded in parallel from different peers; already in place.

title: Find common ancestor instead of restarting at finalized
idea: When starting or switching sync target, probe the peer for the highest shared block behind head (with exponentially growing jumps, never falling back to finalized on an RPC error, capped to a reorg range) and sync from there. During non-finality this avoids redownloading long ranges of known blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain_collection.rs:225,329,389 start_syncing is passed local_head_epoch as the optimistic start epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:882-887 optimistic_start set to the aligned local-head batch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1130-1148 the optimistic batch is downloaded first, before any batch from the finalized start

beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:575-581,707-775 if it imports blocks, advance_chain drops every earlier batch and moves start_epoch/processing_target past it, so the known range is not downloaded

gap: Lighthouse probes one point (the batch at local head) and on failure falls back to finalized. It has no exponential back-off search for the highest shared block between finalized and local head, so a node on a minority fork during long non-finality still redownloads from finalized.

refute_note: The earlier review missed the optimistic_start mechanism: the chain first fetches the local-head batch, and if it links, advance_chain skips everything from finalized to local head. That is a one-step common-ancestor guess, not an exponential probe.

title: Rank finalized sync peers by finalized epoch
idea: Select sync peers whose finalized epoch and head reach the target (same fork, not behind us), rank them by finalized epoch then head slot, and pick the highest target, so requests go to peers that can serve the range.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:127-170 chains keyed by remote finalized root, target = finalized slot+2 epochs+1
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain_collection.rs:276-300 update_finalized_chains picks max_by_key(available_peers)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/peer_sync_info.rs:26-80 remote_sync_type filters peers behind us / not ahead
gap: Peers behind or on another fork are filtered and grouped by finalized root, but the winning chain is the one with most peers, not the highest finalized epoch/head; no per-peer ranking. Rank in chain_collection::update_finalized_chains by (finalized epoch, head slot) before peer count.
impact: Marginal: avoids syncing toward a lower finalized target first; few redundant requests on mainnet.

title: Start range requests after blocks already held
idea: Compute the range-sync start slot from what the node already has (max of last imported block, local head and local finalized slot) and clamp every by-range request start, including the first, to it. The node does not re-download and re-import blocks it already holds.
measured_best: 66 bursts / 748 redundant blocks in ~3 h on a follower, ~65 ms per redundant arrival, one 67-block burst delayed a gossip block 4.2 s (pr:ethlambda#645)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:147-160 finalized chain starts at local_info.finalized_epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:187 head chain starts at min(local head, remote finalized) epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:855-880 start_syncing advances only to local finalized epoch
gap: Start epoch is the local finalized epoch, not the max of imported block, head and finalized slot, so a new/restarted chain re-downloads the blocks between finalized and head (typically 2-3 epochs, up to ~100 blocks) and filters them afterwards. Clamp the start in range.rs add_peer / SyncingChain::new and start_syncing to local head epoch when the head is on the target chain.
impact: Saves a few epochs of redundant block downloads and filter work on chain restarts; small steady-state effect.

title: Skip already-imported blocks before batch processing
idea: Before processing a sync batch, drop duplicate blocks and blocks already in fork choice or the DB, and skip their post-processing, so overlapping, replayed or retried batches cost almost nothing.
measured_best: 4x faster forward sync (title) (pr:caplin#11663)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3068-3142 filter_chain_segment drops DuplicateFullyImported, genesis and finalized-slot blocks before import
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3220 process_chain_segment calls it first
impact: Overlapping or retried batches cost only a relevancy check; download cost remains (see range_sync-062).

title: Save synced blocks to DB concurrently
idea: During range sync, write imported blocks to the database asynchronously (off the import path) so DB writes do not serialize block processing.
measured_best: ~15 blk/s to 26 blk/s in initial sync (pr:prysm#3673)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4749-4756 import_block pushes PutBlock/PutState and calls store.do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache synchronously, under BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE timer, before fork choice is committed
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1459 do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache is a synchronous batch write
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3340-3380 chain segment blocks imported one after another
gap: Move the hot DB write out of import_block into a background writer (queue ops, flush before head or finalization needs them) and keep crash consistency with fork choice persistence (issue 2028 revert logic).
impact: Could overlap DB writes with state transition during initial sync. Prysm saw ~15 to 26 blk/s, but Lighthouse's write share is unknown (measure BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE first).
refute_note: Searched beacon_chain and store for any write queue, deferred or background write path; none exists. Only the migrator (finalization) runs in the background, not per-block import writes.

title: Verify execution payload in parallel with block
idea: In range sync, run the EL newPayload call and the payload envelope state transition concurrently with consensus block verification, and batch the envelope signatures together with the block signature set, instead of doing them serially per block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3298 signature_verify_chain_segment gets blocks only; envelopes extracted at 3291
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3372 process_range_sync_envelope awaited after each process_block, serially
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:432 verify_execution_payload_envelope (signature + state transition) runs first with its own signature check
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:452 notify_new_payload awaited only after state processing, not concurrently
gap: In process_chain_segment, overlap envelope newPayload (EL) with the envelope state transition and with consensus verification of the next block, and add envelope signatures to the segment signature set in signature_verify_chain_segment.
impact: Gloas-only; range sync envelope import is fully serial (state transition, then EL, then import, per block), so overlapping could hide EL latency per block.
refute_note: Read process_range_sync_envelope itself: it verifies the envelope signature individually with VerifySignatures::True, then does the state transition, then awaits newPayload; no join/spawn overlap anywhere in this path.

title: Do not count non-fault failures against batch retries
idea: When a batch fails because the peer rate-limited us or for another reason that is not the peer's fault, do not consume the batch retry budget or penalise the peer; back that peer off and send the batch to a different peer, so the chain is not dropped and re-downloaded.
measured_best: Observed 1,396 rate-limited responses causing peer loss (pr:lodestar#8924)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:308 download_failed counts every failure incl. None against max attempts
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:652 NonFaultyFailure handled only for processing results
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:605 RateLimited from BlocksByRange -> MidToleranceError penalty
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:916 inject_error has no rate-limit branch
gap: Processing-side non-faulty failures are already exempt, but download-side RateLimited responses still burn a download attempt and penalise the peer. Add a RateLimited case in RpcResponseError handling in Chain::inject_error that skips Batch::download_failed's counter (or backs off the peer) and retries on another peer.
impact: Avoids dropping a range-sync chain after repeated rate-limit responses from peers; only matters on busy/overloaded peer sets, small gain.

title: Score sync peers by observed throughput
idea: Track per-peer download throughput (blocks returned and processed, bandwidth) and pick range sync peers by that score, weighted-random so others still get some requests, so fast peers receive more batches and slow peers fewer.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476-495 block peer = min(deprioritized, at_concurrency_limit, rand::random); no speed term
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:116-118 at_concurrency_limit is a fixed MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS cap, not a throughput score
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:353-392 column peer pick uses attempts/lookup_peers/hash, no speed
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1028-1050 send_batch passes chain peers + failed_peers only
gap: No per-peer throughput or latency stats anywhere in sync or peer_manager. Add an EWMA of blocks (or bytes) per second per peer, updated on by-range responses, and use it as a weighted-random key in block_components_by_range_request, select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request and custody select_column_peer.
impact: Faster peers get more batches during initial sync, which cuts download stalls; gain depends on peer spread, maybe tens of percent of sync time when some peers are slow.
refute_note: Grepped network and lighthouse_network for throughput/latency/ewma/speed/response_time and every peer-selection .min()/sort; the only load-sensitive term is the 2-request concurrency cap, which lets a fast peer free its slots sooner but does not rank peers by speed.

title: Weighted round robin on peer rate-limit capacity
idea: Fetch each large contiguous batch from one peer and choose peers by weighted round robin on their remaining rate-limit capacity, so each peer's full burst rate is used without tripping its limit.
measured_best: up to 90% of burst rate (640 blk/s) (pr:prysm#5887)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs:83 SelfRateLimiter::allows mirrors the peer's rate limiter per (peer, protocol) and queues outbound requests until quota is available
beacon_node/src/config.rs:1500 self limiter enabled by default with default params
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/mod.rs:465 outbound requests go through outbound_request_limiter
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476 peer choice uses deprioritize set, concurrency limit and random tie-break, not remaining quota
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH = 1, whole batch from one peer
gap: Lighthouse already mirrors each peer's limit (self limiter) so it does not trip it, and fetches each batch from one peer; missing is using the self limiter's remaining tokens to weight peer selection in block_components_by_range_request (requests to a drained peer are delayed in the queue instead of routed to a peer with capacity).
impact: Avoids batches waiting in the self-limiter queue of a drained peer while other peers are idle; gain depends on peer count and limits, unclear.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the lighthouse_network outbound SelfRateLimiter, which is the 'mirror the peer's limiter' half of the idea and is on by default; only quota-weighted peer choice is absent.

title: Randomize sync peer selection
idea: Pick range sync peers randomly (or shuffle the peer list) instead of a fixed order or a complex scoring policy, so load spreads over all peers and the same few are not hammered.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:478-492 block_components_by_range_request picks peer by (deprioritised, at-concurrency-limit, rand::random) ordering
impact: Load already spreads randomly over peers with fewer active requests.

title: Wait for full custody subnet coverage before column batches
idea: In custody column range sync, only send a batch once there are peers for every custody column subnet, and choose a randomized custody peer per column, so batches do not fail at once and loop retrying against a failing peer.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1168 good_peers_on_sampling_subnets gates include_next_batch and send_batch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:352 select_column_peer picks randomized custody peer per column

title: Pool peers per chain and load-balance batches
idea: Group peers that report the same finalized/head chain into one syncing chain and load-balance its batch downloads over the whole peer pool through one state machine.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1028 send_batch uses chain-wide self.peers pool

title: Keep partial column responses, retry only missing columns
idea: In range sync, accept column responses that miss some columns, keep the good data, attribute the missing columns to the responsible peer, and re-request only those columns from other peers of the syncing chain instead of failing and re-downloading the whole batch.

beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:352 per-column peer selection with attempt counts; Downloaded columns kept, only missing re-requested (Status enum custody.rs:395)

idea: Re-evaluate and restart the sync engine on a fixed timer in addition to peer status changes, so a node that is still behind with a stable peer set does not idle for minutes after a batch completes.

title: Peer-unbound worker pool keeps requests pipelined
idea: Use a pool of sync workers that each take a fresh available peer for every request and issue the next request as soon as any in-flight one completes, so slow peers do not stall the pipeline and peer bandwidth stays used.

title: Narrow redownload range on batch retry
idea: When a batch fails, retry from just past the last safe/imported slot and only widen the redownload window after repeated failures, instead of re-requesting a whole epoch or finalized data again.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:619 on FaultyFailure with imported_blocks > 0, advance_chain to the failed batch so only that batch is re-downloaded

refute_note: Checked the FaultyFailure path in range_sync/chain.rs: imported_blocks > 0 triggers advance_chain, which is the core of the nimbus change at batch level; the earlier review only looked at batch.rs.

title: Remove disconnected peer from all sync chains
idea: On peer disconnect, remove that peer from every syncing chain's peer pool so no batches are assigned to it and sync does not stall.
measured_best: stalled syncs no longer seen on Schlesi (pr:lighthouse#1150)

title: Cheap slot check before DB lookup
idea: In the already-processed block check, compare the block slot with the head slot first and only query the database when that cheap test is inconclusive.
measured_best: avoids one DB lookup (pr:prysm#10620)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3068 filter_chain_segment uses check_relevancy only

title: Retry failed batch with a different peer
idea: When a sync request fails or returns an inconsistent range, return it to the queue as failed and assign it to a peer that has not been tried for it yet, instead of leaving it in flight or re-requesting from the same peer.
