title: Skip attestation processing for finalized sync blocks
idea: During initial sync, skip applying block attestations to fork choice and skip saving them (unless archival) for blocks that are already finalized.
measured_best: only 10 blocks per second before (pr:prysm#4075)

impact: Saves per-block committee lookups and indexed-attestation building for up to 128 attestations on finalized historical blocks during forward sync; likely a few percent of per-block import time, only during sync.

title: No blob wait outside DA window
idea: For blocks outside the data availability window, mark data as available at once instead of waiting for blob sidecars and their timeout.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1296 batch_type returns Blocks outside DA window

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:867 columns/blobs required only inside window
impact: Blocks outside the window are requested without sidecars and imported without waiting.

title: Serve stored SSZ bytes directly for by-range
idea: When serving blocks-by-range/root, send the stored SSZ bytes straight to the wire with only framing, instead of deserializing and reserializing each block, and take rate-limit quota per block.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:1172 get_blocks via BeaconBlockStreamer yields decoded Arc<SignedBeaconBlock> (may hit EL for payloads)

refute_note: Checked the RPC codec encode path for every response type and the beacon_block_streamer; all go through typed objects and as_ssz_bytes, no byte passthrough anywhere.

title: Skip long runs of empty slots quickly
idea: When ranges return no blocks, advance the request window, or sample ahead with stepped by-range requests, to find the next non-empty slot instead of walking empty epochs batch by batch.

title: Skip newPayload for finalized sync blocks
idea: When syncing a finalized chain, import blocks as optimistic and skip the engine newPayload call, since finality already vouches for them, removing an EL round trip per block.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:497-506 NotifyExecutionLayer::No when is_syncing_finalized

impact: Already skips newPayload for finalized sync; only block-hash verification remains.

title: Skip block verification up to trusted finality
idea: During initial sync to a trusted finalized checkpoint, skip most block signature (and other content) verification, with an option to verify everything.
evidence: beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:423 ClientGenesis::CheckpointSyncUrl starts from a trusted finalized state, so no block before the trusted checkpoint is ever state-transitioned or fully verified

Missing only for genesis sync: there is no no-verify mode up to a peer- or user-supplied finalized checkpoint, and forward sync from the anchor to head always verifies everything.
impact: For checkpoint-synced nodes (the common case) the saving already exists in a stronger form; adding Prysm's mode would only help genesis syncs/archive nodes, with a security trade-off.
refute_note: Earlier review only looked at forward-sync signature verification; checkpoint sync is an equivalent mechanism that skips all work up to a trusted finalized checkpoint, and backfill verifies only proposer signatures, so I rate it partial.

title: Bound column retry for withheld origin payloads
idea: Do not retry fetching an origin block's data columns forever when its payload may be withheld; give up or skip the prefetch so the loop does not spin the CPU and downscore peers.
measured_best: 5M+ attempts in 7 minutes at 100% CPU (pr:prysm#17458)

beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:245 - custody column download bounded by MAX_CUSTODY_COLUMN_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS=3
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:395 - constant of 3 attempts
impact: None today: no Gloas payload envelope or withheld-payload path exists in sync, and column fetches have a bounded retry count, so no 100% CPU spin.

title: Use smaller range sync batches
idea: Use smaller range sync batches (about one or two epochs or fewer) so a failed batch is cheap to retry, peers are not overwhelmed, and less data is requested redundantly.
measured_best: 2000 blobs is ~250 MB per minute per peer max (pr:teku#8982)

beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE = 5
impact: Batches are already one epoch (32 blocks), so retries are cheap.

title: Do not pre-filter peers for column sync
idea: Pass all candidate peers to the column-by-range request logic and let it filter per request, instead of pre-restricting initial sync to a small peer set, and do not block responses waiting for unavailable data.
measured_best: "initial sync takes hours" with peer filtering (pr:prysm#14482)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:578 - select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request picks per column among chain peers by is_custody_peer_of
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:598 - peers filtered per request, with deprioritization and concurrency-limit ordering, not pre-restricted to supernodes
impact: Already avoids the slow initial sync from pre-filtering; peer set is the syncing chain's peers, and a column with no custody peer fails the request (NoPeer) rather than waiting.

title: Larger download lookahead window
idea: Let the forward downloader run further ahead of the processed head (larger slots-ahead window or unbounded rolling download), so the pipeline stays full during catch-up.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH = 1
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE = 5

gap: Download runs ahead of processing, but only by a fixed 5 one-epoch batches. Raising the limit or making it adaptive (peer count, processing speed, memory for columns) is not done.
impact: Keeps the pipeline fuller when downloads are slow relative to processing; likely small since processing usually dominates.
refute_note: Confirmed constants and buffer logic; the custody backfill has the same fixed 5-batch buffer; no adaptive or unbounded lookahead elsewhere.

title: Unified peer-driven block and sidecar fetch loop
idea: Use one peer-driven loop that fetches blocks with their sidecars, by-root near head and by-range further back, with adaptive status refresh, instead of separate range and by-root managers.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs RangeSync is a separate manager
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs separately drives range sync, backfill, custody backfill and block_lookups
gap: Unifying RangeSync/BackFillSync/BlockLookups into one per-peer loop choosing by-root vs by-range by distance from finality would be a sync manager redesign.
impact: Mostly simplicity/robustness; no clear CPU or bandwidth saving.
refute_note: Lighthouse already couples blocks with sidecars in both range and lookup requests, but via separate state machines, not one peer-driven loop.

title: Verify proposer signature first in range sync
idea: For each range sync block, verify the proposer signature against the claimed proposer index using only the pubkey cache before parent load, state advance, KZG and body signatures, so invalid batches fail cheaply.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:680 load_parent before any signature check

title: Await each response write before loading next
idea: For multi-chunk responses, wait for the previous chunk write to complete (with a write timeout that closes the stream) before loading the next item from the DB, instead of firing all writes in parallel, so outbound buffers and memory stay bounded.

gap: The write side already matches Teku's fix: chunks are written one at a time per substream, and a 10s per-chunk timeout closes a stalled stream. What is missing is backpressure on loading: the beacon processor reads every block/column from the DB and queues it into the unbounded pending_items before the peer reads, so memory is not bounded by the write rate. To close it, a bounded per-request channel or a write ack from the handler must gate the DB loader.
impact: Bounds memory held for slow peers on big by-range responses (at most 2 concurrent per peer/protocol, timeout-bounded); a robustness gain with little CPU change.
refute_note: The earlier review called RESP_TIMEOUT only an overall stream timeout. The handler resets it per chunk and serialises writes per substream, so the 'await previous write plus write timeout' half exists. Only the load-gating half is missing.

title: Build state proofs from cached tree layers

title: Deserialize and clone into caller-provided output

title: Packed word storage for bitlists and bitvectors
idea: Back bitlists and bitvectors with packed machine words instead of one byte or bool per bit, so popcount, intersects and set-all work on whole words and use less memory.
measured_best: countSetBits 21M -> 249M ops/s; intersects 24M -> 332M ops/s (pr:teku#1531)

title: Start from the persisted head state

title: Keep one epoch of states for far non-canonical forks
idea: For non-canonical chains far ahead of finality, keep only about one epoch of beacon states in memory. Cache growth stays bounded during long non-finality with many forks.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:356 cull: LRU with advanced > old boundary > mid-epoch > could-finalize order, no fork awareness
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:375 only head_block_root is exempt; no canonical/fork distinction
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:420 BlockMap::prune drops only pre-finalized-slot states
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:23 count cap 128
gap: Cache growth is bounded by a count cap and cull priority, but there is no per-fork policy that keeps only about one epoch for far non-canonical forks. Needs fork-distance logic in StateCache::cull using block_map and the head root.
impact: Marginal: memory is already capped; it changes only which states survive in long non-finality with many forks.
refute_note: Re-read cull and BlockMap::prune: the only fork-related input is head_block_root (exempt from mid-epoch culling); no ancestry or distance check exists anywhere in state_cache.rs.

title: Cache finalized states keyed by slot for API
idea: Keep a cache of finalized states keyed by slot for beacon API queries. Repeated requests for the same finalized slot are served from memory instead of reloading and replaying from the freezer.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/historic_state_cache.rs:15 HistoricStateCache: LRU of freezer states keyed by Slot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2306 load_cold_state_by_slot checks the slot cache first (exact hit returns, prior slot is replayed forward)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2403 loaded cold states are put into the cache
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:799 --historic-state-cache-size makes it user-sizable
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:27 cold hdiff buffer cache default 16 makes misses cheap
gap: Default capacity is 1 state. API-heavy operators must raise --historic-state-cache-size; this is a tuning default, not a missing mechanism.
impact: Already present; only a default-size change is possible.
refute_note: The mechanism is exactly a slot-keyed cache of finalized (freezer) states on the API load path, with a CLI flag to size it and a 16-entry hdiff buffer cache behind it. A small default is a tuning choice, not a missing mechanism.

title: Preload finalized epoch states into API cache
idea: When archiving finalized blocks, preload the states of the first and last block of the previous epoch into the state-by-slot cache. Common API queries then hit the cache instead of regenerating states.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3603 migrate_database stores cold states ('There is no reason to cache this state') and never touches historic_state_cache
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2103 store_cold_state writes the DB only and does no cache population
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:127 update_finalized_state keeps only the new finalized checkpoint state hot
gap: After migrate_database, put the epoch-boundary states of the just-archived epoch into HistoricStateCache::put_state (this needs capacity above 1).
impact: Small: the first API query for a just-archived state avoids a freezer reconstruction. Matters only for state-API nodes.
refute_note: Checked migrate_database and store_cold_state for any cache warming: there is none. The only near-equivalent is that the finalized checkpoint state stays in the hot StateCache, so 'finalized' state_id queries already hit memory.

title: Persist decompressed pubkey cache across restarts
idea: Write the decompressed validator pubkey cache to a flat file on clean shutdown and load it at boot with a spot-check against the anchor state. This avoids decompressing every validator pubkey at startup.
measured_best: ~7.8s saved per restart on mainnet (9.4s to 1.6s for the cache step; 42.7s to 34.7s to metrics server); load 53-56ms for 2.37M entries (pr:lodestar#10152)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:53 load_from_store rebuilds the cache from the DB at boot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:230 DatabasePubkey::from_pubkey persists serialize_uncompressed (96-byte affine)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:236 as_pubkey: deserialize_uncompressed, no sqrt decompression
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:141 uncompressed path calls blst deserialize
blst-0.3.17/src/lib.rs:876 blst deserialize of 96-byte input: blst_p1_deserialize, no key_validate or subgroup check
gap: Storage format only: one DB row per validator (about 2M sequential get_item calls) instead of one flat blob. A bulk read might save a few seconds, but decompression, which is the cost the idea targets, is already avoided.
impact: Already present: startup does no BLS decompression; at most a small I/O gain from a flat-file layout.
refute_note: Traced the load path down to blst: the persisted keys are uncompressed affine points and deserialize does only an on-curve parse (no sqrt, no subgroup check), so this is the same mechanism Lodestar added. compress() of an affine point is plain serialization.

title: Preallocate pubkey cache capacity
idea: Reserve the pubkey cache arrays to their final size (plus registry growth headroom) when building it, reuse the loaded validators array, and skip writes of identical pubkeys. This avoids repeated reallocation and needless mutation of the shared cache.
measured_best: ~31MB virtual, ~0 resident reservation (pr:lodestar#9640)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:111 reserve(len) in import for new keys
validator_pubkey_cache.rs:55 load_from_store pushes in loop with no pre-sizing; new() starts with vec![]
gap: load_from_store could size pubkeys/indices/pubkey_bytes from a known validator count (or state validators len) and reserve small growth headroom; import already reserves exactly the delta.
impact: Slightly less realloc/rehash at startup (~1M validators HashMap rehashes); minor and one-off.

title: Never evict possibly-finalizable epoch-boundary states
idea: In state cache eviction, protect epoch-boundary states that could become finalized (checked before other conditions like is_advanced, and robust to skipped slots). Finalization migration then does not rebuild them and keeps structural sharing with recent states.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:16 EPOCH_FINALIZATION_LIMIT=4
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:376 cull checks is_boundary first, could-finalize boundary states culled last
impact: Lighthouse PRs 4762/4833 are present in current source.

title: Fork-aware state cache eviction by chain
idea: Track ancestry in the state cache, evict the least recently accessed chain first, and cap states per chain. Many forks cannot push useful head-chain states out.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:27-36 BlockMap is block_root->slot->state_root only, no parent/chain links
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:357-412 cull() is LRU with state-kind buckets (advanced, old boundary, mid-epoch, good boundary), no per-chain grouping or cap
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:228-285 put_state() has no per-chain limit
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1586 only fork pruning on finalization deletes abandoned-fork states (delete_block_states), not eviction priority
gap: Add ancestry tracking (parent links) to StateCache, evict the least recently accessed chain first and cap states per chain in cull()/put_state().
impact: Under long non-finality or many forks, fork states could push head-chain states out and cause reloads/replays; small on a healthy mainnet node.
refute_note: Checked all state_cache.lock() callers in store and beacon_chain, and the finalization fork pruning path; nothing groups or limits cached states by chain.

title: Preserve fork-choice tip states when pruning
idea: When pruning the state cache, keep the states of all unfinalized fork-choice tips so they are not evicted and later recomputed or reloaded.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:184-189 update_head_block_root stores a single head root
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:392-395 cull() exempts only the unadvanced head-block state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1515 the only caller passes only the canonical head
gap: Pass all fork-choice leaf block roots (proto-array heads) to StateCache and skip their states in cull().
impact: Avoids reloading/replaying states for competing tips during fork-heavy periods; negligible with one tip.
refute_note: Grepped store, canonical_head and migrate for any heads/tips/leaves set fed to the cache; only the single head root reaches it.

title: Head state never evicted; cap regen replay
idea: Hold the fork-choice head state through a strong reference that cache eviction cannot drop, and fail fast when regenerating a state would replay too many blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:284 CachedHead holds snapshot: Arc<BeaconSnapshot> with the head BeaconState, a strong reference outside the evictable StateCache
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:392-395 cull() never evicts the unadvanced head state
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:622 and beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:254 default hierarchy smallest exponent 5: hot ReplayFrom is at most 31 slots of blocks by layout
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1992-2014 load_hot_state ReplayFrom from the nearest diff layer
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2031-2040 load_hot_state_using_replay / 2514 load_blocks_to_replay have no explicit block-count check or fail-fast error
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:151 import_max_skip_slots defaults to None (attestation skip cap is opt-in)
gap: Head-state strong reference is done. Missing: an explicit fail-fast cap on replayed blocks/slots in load_blocks_to_replay/replay_blocks (replay is bounded only by the hierarchy layout config, and slot advancing for stale-fork attestations is uncapped unless import_max_skip_slots is set).
impact: Head-state half already present; the cap only guards pathological configs or long skip-slot advances, so the remaining gain is small.
refute_note: Confirmed that the hdiff hierarchy bounds hot replay to under 32 blocks by default (not a runtime check), and checked import_max_skip_slots and MAX_ADVANCE_DISTANCE as alternative caps; neither is a regen replay fail-fast.

title: Finalized state root fast path
idea: In state-root-at-slot lookups, return the cached finalized/split state root directly for the finalized slot instead of walking back through state loads.
measured_best: prepare_beacon_proposer took 5-10s in non-finality; no after numbers (pr:lighthouse#8353)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:977-981 fast path returns split.state_root when request_slot == split.slot
impact: Already present (lighthouse#8353).

title: Global shuffling cache keyed by epoch and decision root
idea: Cache shufflings in one shared cache keyed by (epoch, shuffling decision root) and use it for committee assignments and every attestation, so attestations on forks or across epoch boundaries hit the cache instead of memoizing per state or forcing state reads and recomputation.
measured_best: OOM kill each startup before (screenshot) (pr:lodestar#9569)
evidence: consensus/types AttestationShufflingId = (epoch, decision block root)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:~118 ShufflingCache keyed by AttestationShufflingId, 16 entries

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:~375 inserts committee cache

title: Precompute next-epoch caches in the state-advance task
idea: Before an epoch boundary (last slot, even when skipped), build the next epoch's committee, shuffling and proposer caches, ideally in the same background task that pre-advances the head state, so the epoch transition is computed once and the first block and duties of the new epoch do not miss.
measured_best: Avoids extra 500ms-1s latency on slot 0 proposal (pr:prysm#12651)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:~310-335 builds Current and Next committee caches after advancing
state_advance_timer.rs:~345-410 primes proposer cache (current/next epoch) and shuffling_cache via insert_committee_cache on epoch crossing
state_advance_timer.rs:38 runs in the background task at slot end for the head

title: Preheat n+1 shuffling at end of n-1
idea: Compute the shuffling for epoch n+1 at the last slot of epoch n-1, when its dependent root is known, so validator duty requests at the start of epoch n hit a warm cache.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:~375-395 at the last slot of epoch n-1 the head is advanced into n and the RelativeEpoch::Next (n+1) shuffling is inserted with its decision root
shuffling_cache.rs insert_committee_cache

title: Seed sync committee cache from known committee
idea: When applying blocks, seed the sync committee index cache with the known committee and cache total active balance per epoch, avoiding full validator traversals per block during sync.
measured_best: 20-30% sync speedup post-altair, plus ~10% from cached total active balances (pr:nimbus#4592)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753 get_sync_committee_indices resolves pubkeys via the state's pubkey cache, no validator traversal
beacon_state.rs:819,2682 total_active_balance cached per epoch, set in single-pass epoch processing

title: Move snapshots out of cache instead of cloning
idea: Make the block-processing snapshot/state cache move the pre-state out rather than clone it when it will not be reused (head import, sync block import), reducing clones and memory fragmentation.

title: Persistent structurally shared tree-backed beacon states
idea: Represent the beacon state in memory as persistent structurally shared trees (and diffs on disk), so clones share unchanged subtrees and cached hash roots and the state cache can hold many more states for similar memory.
measured_best: holds 32x more states for around the same memory cost (pr:lighthouse#5533)
evidence: Cargo.lock:6570 milhouse 0.9.0 persistent trees
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:229 HDiffBuffer, hierarchical diffs on disk
state_cache.rs:263 state.clone() cheap
impact: Already core design.

title: Rebase updated lists onto old tree
idea: After bulk-updating a list such as inactivity_scores, rebase the new tree onto the old one to reuse identical subtrees, instead of duplicating the whole list in memory each update.
measured_best: ~70MB+ per update to ~4-5MB; rebase time 47ms (pr:lighthouse#7062)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:245 inactivity_scores.iter_cow(), no intra_rebase/rebase after the pass
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:646-650 zero scores skip make_mut (avoids copies only in the all-zero common case, not the leak/recovery case #7062 targets)
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/milhouse-572e092edb163991/d67aabd/src/list.rs:356 List::intra_rebase exists; only caller is milhouse src/tests/proptest/operations.rs:389, with a FIXME bug note at :394

beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:197-208 rebase_on_finalized and beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7840 rebase_on are whole-state rebases against another state for disk-loaded states, not after epoch updates
gap: #7062's List::intra_rebase call after the epoch-transition inactivity_scores update is not in unstable. During a leak or recovery every non-zero score is rewritten, so each post-epoch state carries a fresh ~80MB inactivity_scores tree. Re-add intra_rebase (or rebase_on against the pre-state list) after process_epoch_single_pass once the milhouse intra_rebase dedup bug is fixed.
impact: During non-finality, about 70MB+ to about 4-5MB per inactivity_scores update per cached state (measured on Holesky in #7062); no effect when all scores are 0 (mainnet steady state), because zero scores already skip mutation.
refute_note: Searched for intra_rebase, rebase_on and .rebase( across the repo and milhouse d67aabd. The only related mechanisms are the zero-score make_mut skip and whole-state rebase_on for states loaded from disk. Neither dedups a list that was rewritten in bulk.

title: Load states onto an existing in-memory tree
idea: When deserializing a state (diff application, checkpoint-sync anchor), build it onto an already loaded related state's tree, reusing unchanged subtrees and applying only modified entries, so loaded states share memory and are not re-hashed.
measured_best: startup blocking of ~24s removed after download (pr:lodestar#7056)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:210 HDiffBuffer::as_state builds state from SSZ + balances/validators/inactivity lists
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1984-1988 and 2009-2013 rebase_on_finalized right after loading a diff/replay base state

beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:197 rebase_on_finalized; consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3416 BeaconState::rebase_on (milhouse Tree::rebase_on reuses base subtrees and their cached hashes) plus rebase_caches_on:3515
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7836-7841 chain dump also rebases on previous state
gap: Done by rebasing after deserialising rather than deserialising directly onto the base tree: a transient full tree is still built first. Checkpoint-sync anchor path not checked for rebase.
impact: Loaded hot states share memory and hashes with the finalized state; only the transient allocation and deserialisation CPU remain, which would need a diff-applied-onto-tree loader to remove.

title: Pool and reuse large state field buffers
idea: Pool released large per-state arrays (randao mixes, 2D byte slices, COW buffers) and reuse them when a state field must be copied, instead of allocating new ones.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs: fields are milhouse persistent Lists/Vectors, clone shares nodes; no large per-state arrays copied
no buffer pool found in store/src/state_cache.rs
impact: Tree-backed states copy only modified leaves, so pooling large flat arrays does not apply.

title: No state copies on head save and init sync
idea: Do not copy the state when saving it as the head, and during initial sync (linear chain) return cached states without cloning and skip the skip-slot cache.
measured_best: Memory reduction down from 3GB to 600MB (pr:prysm#5778)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs: BeaconState uses milhouse persistent trees, clone is Arc-shared
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:236 put_state clones the state (cheap structural share); no skip-slot cache module in beacon_node/beacon_chain/src
impact: Prysm's deep-copy cost does not exist in Lighthouse: cloning a milhouse-backed state is cheap and there is no skip-slot cache.

title: Read-only field accessors without state copy
idea: Provide read-only accessors on the state for validators and balance sums, so callers needing a few fields do not deep-copy the validator list or whole state.
measured_best: many times faster and doesn't require making copies (pr:prysm#13782)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2408 get_validator returns &Validator
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:~95 validators().iter_from(n) borrows without copying
impact: Borrowing accessors on milhouse lists exist; clone is cheap anyway.

title: Compact flattened checkpoint state
idea: Keep checkpoint states in a compact form: a pubkey array shared with the anchor state, balances only, active/slashed bitsets and one shuffled set.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:46-55 cache holds full BeaconState values that share tree nodes via milhouse
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3515 rebase_caches_on shares pubkey and committee caches between states
impact: Checkpoint states are structurally shared clones (validators list, pubkey cache), so a separate flattened compact form would add little.

title: In-memory LRU of recent hot states
idea: Keep recent unfinalized post-states in an in-memory cache keyed by block root, so block import and duties do not read, write or replay states from the database.
measured_best: hit ratio >99% (cited from #4834) (pr:prysm#5004)

impact: Block import and duties already hit the in-memory cache, with the disk path as fallback.

title: Tune hot state cache size
idea: Size the hot state cache large enough (e.g. 32 entries, larger at startup with many forks) to keep the miss rate low and avoid replay-based regeneration.
measured_best: hot state miss rate ~4% to 2% (pr:prysm#6033)

beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:45 LRU state cache + hdiff buffer cache

title: Store sparse states, regenerate by replay
idea: Persist only periodic archive/restore-point states plus summaries and regenerate any other state by loading the nearest saved state and replaying blocks forward, instead of storing every state.
measured_best: exp pods used 500MB less (from related flag PRs) (pr:prysm#6087)

impact: Hot states stored as periodic snapshots/diffs plus summaries and replayed; cold states use hierarchical diffs.

title: Do not pin disk-loaded states in cache
idea: Keep states loaded from storage in the cache only on demand rather than pinning them, so cold states do not hold memory.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1815-1850 get_hot_state only inserts disk-loaded states into the cache when update_cache is true

title: Periodic hot state snapshots in long non-finality
idea: During long non-finality persist a hot state every N slots so regeneration replays stay short, and delete them after finalization.
measured_best: about 2GB extra disk on Medalla; memory spikes from replay otherwise (pr:prysm#7597)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:619-624 default hot hierarchy exponents [5,9,11,13,16,18,21]: a diff or snapshot every 32 slots (one epoch)

impact: Replays are bounded to at most about one epoch of blocks even in long non-finality via on-disk epoch diffs, deleted/migrated at finalization; no regeneration spikes like Prysm's.

title: Prune before persisting checkpoint states
idea: Prune finalized checkpoint states before persisting in one serialized flow, so a racing prune cannot orphan files and soon-pruned states are not serialized.
measured_best: persisted checkpoint states grew ~197MB per orphan file (screenshot) (pr:lodestar#9463)

impact: Lighthouse has no separate on-disk checkpoint-state file store (states go in DB with summaries), so there are no orphan files to race with pruning.

title: Prune on-disk states one epoch behind finality
idea: Prune stored fork states up to one epoch behind the finalized slot (cutoff from the highest slot with a stored state), then drop fork-graph blocks older than the oldest stored state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509-720 prune_hot_db prunes states of chains conflicting with the new finalized checkpoint and states before it, keeping only hdiff grid points

impact: Hot DB state pruning at finalization exists; the one-epoch-behind cutoff and fork-graph block cutoff are Caplin-specific and not needed given Lighthouse prunes by finalized-checkpoint DAG.

title: Historical state regen on dedicated worker
idea: Serve historical state requests from a separate worker thread with its own regen queue and persisted pubkey index, so old-state API work does not block the main thread.

idea: Keep states in a cache between consecutive blocks during initial sync, avoiding DB saves and loads per block.

idea: Clear initial-sync state caches once range sync finishes, to release memory.

idea: During forward sync save or dump states only at epoch-multiple slots and prune finalized cache entries later, cutting per-block state copies.

Watch its memory cost.

title: Sparse BTreeMap for pending updates in persistent lists
idea: Store pending (uncommitted) updates to persistent validator and balance lists in a sparse ordered map (BTreeMap) keyed by index instead of a dense vector of options. Memory and work stay proportional to the number of changed entries, not the list length, so block processing and tree hashing of recent states get faster.
measured_best: block with exits: process 92.4ms to 12.5ms, post-block hash 132ms to 15.4ms (pr:lighthouse#9017)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:76-93 Validators and ValidatorsGloas use BTreeMap<usize, Validator> (PR 9017)
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:78,82 Balances = List<u64, N> and BalancesGloas = ProgressiveList<u64> keep the default MaxMap<VecMap>
participation and inactivity_scores lists also use the default (milhouse list.rs:30 default U = MaxMap<VecMap<T>>)
gap: Only validators use the sparse map. Balances, previous/current epoch participation and inactivity_scores still use the dense VecMap (Vec<Option<T>>). Change the type aliases (Balances, BalancesGloas and the participation/inactivity field types) to BTreeMap<usize,u64>/<ParticipationFlags>/<u64> and benchmark, since balances and participation are touched densely per epoch and the VecMap may win there.
impact: Lower peak memory and cheaper clone/apply for recent states when few entries change; modest, since these lists are mutated densely at epoch boundaries.

title: Cache total active balance per epoch and use it
idea: Compute the total active balance once per epoch, keep it in a state or epoch cache, and make the total-active-balance helper read that cache instead of summing over all validators for each attestation, base reward or churn computation. Block processing and replay then do no per-call validator scans for it.
measured_best: None (pr:nimbus#4434)

consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2710 build_total_active_balance_cache
impact: Already cached; no per-call validator scans.

title: Cache base reward per increment per epoch
idea: Compute base_reward_per_increment (which needs an integer sqrt of total active balance) once per epoch in the epoch cache, and in attestation processing sum effective-balance increments over attesters then multiply once. This removes per-attester and per-attestation recomputation.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#2626)

impact: Already done; isqrt once per epoch.

title: Allocation-free swap-or-not shuffle and hashing
idea: Implement the swap-or-not shuffle so its inner loop does not allocate intermediate sequences or a digest per hash: reuse one hasher and fixed stack buffers per call and read the 32-byte digest in place. Shuffles do thousands of hashes, so this removes most allocations in committee computation and replay.
measured_best: None (pr:nimbus#1547)

consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/compute_shuffled_index.rs:52 Context-based hashing, no heap alloc
impact: Already allocation-free.

title: Check-free byte conversions in shuffle inner loop
idea: In the swap-or-not shuffle inner loop, build hash inputs and read the pivot u64 with infallible fixed-size array conversions or direct little-endian loads instead of length-checked slice helpers. This removes a branch and panic path per iteration.
measured_best: Benchmarks showed no difference (pr:lighthouse#6483)
evidence: consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/shuffle_list.rs:36 copy_from_slice into [u8;8] then from_le_bytes (fixed array)
consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/compute_shuffled_index.rs:77 bytes_to_int64 similar
impact: Equivalent; the source PR measured no difference.

title: Whole-list swap-or-not shuffling
idea: Shuffle or unshuffle the entire active-index list in one list-wise pass with the swap-or-not round structure (one hash per 256 positions, flip pivots per round), instead of computing the shuffled position of each index separately. This needs far fewer hash calls per epoch shuffling.
measured_best: None (pr:teku#2539)
evidence: consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/shuffle_list.rs:92 shuffle_list whole-list swap-or-not, one hash per 256 positions, masked_swap
impact: Already done (250x vs per-index).

title: Pubkey index for builder registry lookups
idea: Keep (or build once per block) a pubkey-to-index map for the builder registry, and use the validator pubkey index for pending-deposit checks, so builder deposits, exits and fork-upgrade onboarding look up pubkeys in O(1) instead of scanning the registry or validator list.

title: Verify pending deposit signatures lazily, once per pubkey
idea: When onboarding builders or processing deposit requests, check whether a pubkey has a pending validator deposit with an O(1) per-pubkey status set, and BLS-verify a pending deposit signature only when needed and at most once, instead of eagerly verifying or rescanning the whole pending-deposit queue.

title: Read validators via read-only references, not copies
idea: In non-mutating paths (exit initiation, slashings, withdrawals sweep, pending deposits, proposer and committee selection), read validator fields through read-only references or views instead of getters that copy a validator or the registry, or get-then-commit. Validator copies showed up as 10-20% of CPU.

title: Cache and incrementally update exit queue churn
idea: Compute the exit queue epoch and churn (only the latest exit epoch, not a map of all exit epochs) at most once per block or epoch, cache it, and update it incrementally as exits are initiated, instead of scanning all validators for each exit or slashing. Blocks with many exits go from O(exits*validators) to O(exits).

title: Use known state roots in per-slot processing
idea: When importing or replaying blocks, pass the already known per-slot state root (from the parent block, the block itself, or a stored empty-slot root cache) to slot processing, or skip a root nobody observes, so it does not tree-hash the full state each slot. This saves a full state hash tree root per block and per replayed slot.

title: Avoid full beacon state copies
idea: Do not deep-copy the whole beacon state during state transition: pass views or references, take ownership of states that are not used again, and restore from the head state on failure instead of copying before each transition. This removes multi-MB copies per block and cuts allocations.

title: Copy-on-write for large state fields
idea: Share large state fields (validators, balances, roots) between state clones and copy only on mutation, or store them in chunks so a copy shares unchanged chunks. State clones become cheap in time and memory.

title: Bloom filter for new-deposit pubkey checks

title: Per-block block-root cache and batched proposer reward
idea: During block attestation processing, cache block roots for target and head lookups (most attestations share them) and accumulate the proposer reward across the block, writing the balance once. Benchmark whether the root cache beats direct state lookups.

consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1911 - get_block_root is a milhouse Vector get
gap: Proposer reward is accumulated per attestation but written to the balance once per attestation, not once per block; no block-root cache across attestations (direct milhouse get each time). To match: accumulate the reward in process_attestations (ctxt) and call increase_balance once at the end, and optionally cache target/head roots per distinct AttestationData.

title: Batch-verify deposit signatures in a block

Block path (apply_deposit) and the epoch pending-deposit loop (single_pass.rs new_validator_deposits) call is_valid_deposit_signature one by one. Collect first-time-pubkey deposits and call is_valid_deposit_signature_batch, taking care that duplicate pubkeys in the same batch only verify the first.

title: Skip validator tree reads in withdrawals

consensus/types/src/state/ (activation_queue, exit_cache, slashings_cache, progressive_balances_cache, epoch_cache, pubkey_cache) has no withdrawal-eligibility cache

title: Flat validator array beside tree state
idea: Keep a flat, structurally shared array (or persistent vector) of validator records or their hot fields beside the tree-backed state, and iterate it in epoch processing, exits, activations and effective-balance collection instead of reading validators through the SSZ tree. Per-block clones stay cheap.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#1816)
evidence: d67aabd/src/leaf.rs:14 milhouse leaves hold native Arc<T> values beside a lazily computed hash, not serialized chunks
d67aabd/src/tree.rs:85 get_recursive returns &T by pointer descent, no deserialization

consensus/types/src/state/exit_cache.rs, activation_queue.rs, progressive_balances_cache.rs, epoch_cache.rs flat caches for exits, activations and effective balances
gap: Indexed reads are O(log n) pointer descents instead of O(1) array lookups; no separate flat array exists, but it is not needed for the gain the idea targets.
impact: The Lodestar gain came from reading validators out of a serialized merkle tree. Lighthouse's milhouse tree is itself a structurally shared persistent vector of native Validator records with hashes cached alongside, so clones are cheap and reads need no deserialization. Residual gain from an extra flat array would be negligible.

idea: Keep validator pubkeys and signatures as raw bytes and parse curve points lazily, compare pubkeys by bytes, and do not mark the hash cache dirty on read-only list access.

idea: When diffing validator and inactivity-score buffers against a seed state, first compare whole buffers, then do one linear scan over fixed-size elements instead of recursive binary partitioning.

title: Per-pubkey index of pending deposits

idea: In the fork upgrade, reuse the previous state's tree nodes for unchanged fields instead of rebuilding them, so cached hashes survive and the post-fork hash tree root is cheap.

refute_note: Checked the actual git-pinned milhouse (d67aabd) and tree_hash (e5ea187) checkouts, not the registry copies the earlier review cited; both only call per-pair hash32_concat, parallelised by rayon but not SIMD-batched.

title: Compact leaf storage with cached leaf hash
idea: Store packed leaf node data as raw bytes, use a precomputed default leaf hash, and cache each leaf's hash, avoiding wrapper object and padding allocations during Merkle hashing.

validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1240-1275 small probe of INITIAL_DUTIES_QUERY_SIZE indices; full refetch only if dependent_root differs
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/beacon_head_monitor.rs:17-21 HeadEvent carries only slot and block root, no dependent roots
validator_client/src/lib.rs:439-440,565,586 head events go only to attestation and sync committee services, not to duties_service
gap: The dependent root already gates the full refetch. But two probe POSTs (current and next epoch) still go out every slot, and the proposer duties are polled every slot. A head monitor exists, but HeadEvent has no previous_duty_dependent_root/current_duty_dependent_root and duties_service does not subscribe to it. To close the gap: add the dependent roots to HeadEvent, and probe only when they change, with a once-per-epoch fallback.
impact: Saves about 2 small duties POSTs per slot per VC. That is negligible for one VC and matters only for BNs that serve many VCs.
refute_note: I found the beacon_head_monitor head-event subscription, which the earlier review did not mention. It only drives attestation and sync committee timing, and its event drops the dependent roots, so the verdict stays partial.

title: Fetch duties once per epoch, serve slots from cache
idea: Fetch attester and proposer duty assignments once per epoch (or when missing or the dependent root changes) and serve per-slot checks and attestation routines from the cache, instead of polling the beacon node every slot.
measured_best: 32 requests to 1 per epoch (pr:lighthouse#8905)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:49 INITIAL_DUTIES_QUERY_SIZE=1 probe
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1256 full fetch only if dependent_root differs or duties missing
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1031 poll_beacon_attesters
impact: Per slot cost is one 1-index probe request; full duty fetch only on epoch change or reorg. Per-slot checks served from the local map.

title: Short lookahead, per-slot batches for selection proofs
idea: Precompute aggregator/sync selection proofs only a few slots ahead, signing them in small per-slot batches, instead of 32 slots ahead or thousands of signing tasks at epoch start. Avoids wasted signing, remote signer load and contention with duty signing.
measured_best: with 5k validators replaces 5k tasks with 1 task signing ~160 proofs per slot; graphs show lower median signing time (pr:lighthouse#4033)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:121 SelectionProofConfig lookahead_slot default 0
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1581 fill_in_selection_proofs signs per slot batches
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1618 only lookahead_slot duties taken per tick
impact: Proofs are signed in per-slot batches shortly before the slot, not 32 slots ahead.

title: Decrypt keystores before waiting for beacon node
idea: Decrypt validator keystores at startup before waiting for the beacon node or genesis so the first slots are not missed.
measured_best: None (pr:lighthouse#1299)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:207 InitializedValidators::from_definitions (decrypts keystores) runs in Validator::new
validator_client/src/lib.rs:388 beacon genesis/BN wait comes later
impact: Startup already decrypts before waiting for BN/genesis; nothing to gain.

title: Batch committee subnet subscriptions
idea: Send all committee subnet subscriptions for a slot/epoch to the beacon node in one batched request instead of one call per duty.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1151-1172 collects all duties into one Vec and sends a single post_validator_beacon_committee_subscriptions
impact: Already one batched request per poll.

title: Event-driven wait for activation
idea: Wake the wait-for-activation loop on key-change notifications instead of polling every 30s, so new keys are picked up immediately.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#13448)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:686 poll_validator_indices loop runs once per slot
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:911 unknown pubkeys re-queried each slot (once per epoch backoff)
validator_client/src/lib.rs:646 pre-genesis poll
gap: Lighthouse has no 30s wait-for-activation loop; it re-polls unknown validators every slot (12s), not event-driven on key import. A new key waits up to one slot. Could notify the indices task from add_validator_keystore (tokio Notify) to poll immediately.
impact: Negligible on a mainnet node; only shaves up to 12s off picking up a freshly imported key.

title: Parallel keystore decryption for keymanager API imports
idea: Decrypt keystores imported through the keymanager API in a queued parallel worker pool rather than serially, keeping the duty path free while KDF work runs.
measured_best: ~5x faster import of many keys (pr:lodestar#5624)
evidence: validator_client/http_api/src/keystores.rs:104-131 keystores imported in a serial for loop
validator_client/http_api/src/keystores.rs:198-218 import_single_keystore decrypts once to validate then block_on(add_validator_keystore) decrypts again
initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:260 spawn_blocking decrypt, one at a time
gap: In import_keystores / import_single_keystore, run decrypt_keypair for all keystores in parallel (rayon or JoinSet of spawn_blocking), then add the validated keys; also avoid the double decryption by passing the decrypted keypair through.
impact: Bulk keymanager imports of many keys (scrypt ~1s each, done twice) would be several times faster with cores; no effect on steady-state duties.

title: Cache KDF output for shared salt and password
idea: When many keystores share the same KDF salt and password, cache the derived decryption key so the expensive KDF runs once, not per keystore.
measured_best: significantly improve decoding performance for keystores with single salt and password (pr:nimbus#4372)
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:229-300 from_definition decrypts every keystore independently via decrypt_keypair
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/key_cache.rs:36-80 KeyCache stores one master-encrypted cache so restarts run only one KDF
gap: No cache keyed on (salt,password,kdf params). Note keystore KDF output depends on the keystore's own salt and Lighthouse-generated keystores have random salts, so benefit only exists for externally generated keystores sharing salt. Would need a derived-key cache in from_definition / Keystore::decrypt_keypair; the key cache already removes KDF cost on restarts.
impact: Only first startup or first import of many same-salt keystores; restarts already hit the key cache. Seconds per key saved at most.

title: Skip key cache decrypt with no local keystores
idea: Do not decrypt or save the keystore key cache (scrypt) when no local keystore validators exist, e.g. only remote-signer keys.
measured_best: Excessive CPU / slow PATCH validators with hundreds of keys; no numbers (pr:lighthouse#4126)
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:1255-1261 has_local_definitions gate: KeyCache::new() instead of decrypt_key_cache when only Web3Signer
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:1391 save only if has_local_definitions && is_modified
impact: Remote-signer-only setups already skip key cache decrypt and save.

title: Use validator index from duties response
idea: Take validator indices from the duties response (or include them there) instead of separate per-validator index lookups and a VC-side pubkey-to-index map.
measured_best: "thousands of requests" avoided (pr:prysm#4567)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:911-1010 poll_validator_indices does one GET states/head/validators/{pubkey} per unknown pubkey, sequentially
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1058,1281 indices used to request duties
gap: Duties are requested by index, so the index must be known first; Lighthouse resolves it with one HTTP call per validator. Batch via POST /eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators with ids=[pubkeys] in poll_validator_indices (chunked), then set_validator_index for each result.
impact: Startup and key-import with thousands of keys drops from thousands of BN requests to a handful; steady state unaffected (known indices are cached).

title: Prune slashing protection database
idea: Periodically (and at startup) prune slashing-protection block/attestation records older than a horizon, relying on low-watermark guards, so tables stay small and signing checks stay fast.
measured_best: about 0.5s for 1000 validators and 54,000 epochs (pr:prysm#8221)
evidence: validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1372-1415 prune_slashing_protection_db prunes attestations and blocks via prune_all_signed_*
validator_client/src/lib.rs:476 first_run prune at startup
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:816 periodic prune

title: Lazy default slashing protection records
idea: Return defaults when a key has no slashing-protection entry instead of pre-writing a default record per key at startup, avoiding N transactions on launch.
measured_best: removes a bottleneck for starting a validator client by no longer creating N validator DB transactions (pr:prysm#5323)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:265-268 register_validators for all voting pubkeys in a single call
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:214-218 one with_transaction for all keys, prepared statement reused
impact: Rows are still pre-written at startup but in one transaction, not N, so the bottleneck the idea targets is absent.

title: Per-validator slashing protection locks
idea: Replace the global lock around slashing-protection check-and-record with per-validator locks so distinct validators sign concurrently; only shared storage writes stay serialized.
measured_best: about 2Gb memory for 1000 validating keys (pr:prysm#8086)
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:20 POOL_SIZE=1 single sqlite connection
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:646 check_and_insert_attestations: one Exclusive txn per batch
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:589 block check also Exclusive txn
gap: Slashing DB is one SQLite file with pool size 1 and EXCLUSIVE transactions, so all signers serialize on it; no per-validator locks. Would need per-key in-memory state with async flush in SlashingDatabase::check_and_insert_*.
impact: Little on a normal node: attestations are batched into one txn per slot, so the lock is held briefly. Matters only for thousands of keys on slow disks.

title: Sign a slot's attestations in parallel
idea: Issue all per-validator signatures for a slot concurrently (CPU thread pool for local BLS, concurrent requests for a remote signer) instead of one after another, so the last attestation is published sooner.
measured_best: Sequential 32 votes published from 1.61 s to ~2.3 s into the slot; 2/3-wide aggregate p50 6.49 s vs block build at 6.40 s (pr:ethlambda#655)
evidence: validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1020-1045 sign_attestations join_all over per-validator futures
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1085 spawn_blocking_handle for local BLS

title: Parallel attestation aggregation across subnets
idea: Run aggregation duties for different subnets/committees concurrently instead of sequentially.
measured_best: reduces aggregation time ~80% if you run more than 10 validators (pr:prysm#12699)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:395-425 per committee_index spawn_ignoring_error(handle_aggregates)
impact: Aggregation per committee index (per subnet) already runs as concurrent tasks.

title: Fetch duty types and epochs concurrently
idea: Fetch current and next epoch duties, and attester, proposer and sync duties within each, concurrently instead of sequentially.
measured_best: reduces the time to fetch duties from ~8-9s to ~2.5s (pr:prysm#13789)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:683-857 separate spawned tasks for proposers, attesters, sync, PTC, IL
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1066 and :1090 current then next epoch attester fetch awaited sequentially
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1863 proposer epochs fetched in sequential for loop
gap: Duty types run as independent tasks, but within attesters current and next epoch are fetched one after the other (poll_beacon_attesters), and likewise in poll_beacon_proposers. Wrap the two epoch calls in futures::join!.
impact: Halves duty polling latency at epoch boundaries for large key sets; mostly background, not critical path.

title: Share one HTTP client per remote signer
idea: Create one HTTP client per remote signer URL and reuse it for all validators and requests, so connections are pooled and memory/sockets do not scale per key.
measured_best: VC with 200 keys on Web3Signer: ~200MB to ~50MB (pr:lighthouse#3335)
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:327-356 web3_signer_client_map keyed by Web3SignerDefinition, client cloned per validator
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:440-451 build_web3_signer_client

title: Throttle concurrent remote signer requests
idea: Queue signing requests to the remote signer and cap in-flight requests, since epoch-boundary selection proofs for all keys arrive in bulk.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1596-1625 attestation selection proofs are signed in per-slot batches at mid-slot with a lookahead, not all at the epoch boundary
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1666-1679 in the default (non-DVT) mode, selection proofs are signed serially (stream::iter().then(), one request in flight)
validator_client/src/lib.rs:68-74,488-511 defaults: lookahead 8 slots, offset slot/2, parallel_sign=false for non-distributed mode
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:636-680 the FuturesUnordered unbounded path runs only when parallel_sign is set (DVT)
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:448-451 the web3signer reqwest client sets only pool_max_idle_per_host, with no in-flight cap
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1228-1341 attestation signing uses join_all with no cap
gap: The burst this idea targets (selection proofs for all keys at the epoch boundary) is already removed: default mode signs them serially and spreads them across slots. What is still missing is a general cap on in-flight remote-signer requests. Per-slot attestation and aggregate signing uses join_all with no bound, and the DVT/parallel_sign mode signs selection proofs with no bound. To close the gap, add a Semaphore around the Web3Signer requests in SigningMethod.
impact: Small. The epoch-boundary burst is already gone in default mode. A general cap would only smooth the per-slot signing of about 1/32 of the keys, or help DVT setups.
refute_note: The earlier review searched only for Semaphore/buffer_unordered. It missed that fill_in_selection_proofs signs serially and in per-slot batches (lookahead 8, mid-slot), which is a scheduling equivalent of throttling the selection-proof burst.

title: Poll next-epoch duties before boundary
idea: Fetch next-epoch proposer duties shortly before the epoch boundary, after the BN precomputes the next-epoch state, so the first-slot proposer is known without delay.
measured_best: polling at epoch start wasted up to 2 s causing missed proposals (pr:lodestar#5794)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:709-715 proposer poll runs at the start of every slot
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1863 fetches current_epoch and current_epoch+1 every slot
impact: Next-epoch proposer duties are fetched every slot of the previous epoch, so the first-slot proposer is cached at the boundary.

title: Reuse duty data instead of extra requests
idea: Use data already in the duty (committees per slot, committee length, aggregator index) for subnet subscription and aggregation rather than re-querying the BN.
measured_best: reduces the time needed to subscribe from 1-2 seconds to 1 millisecond (pr:prysm#13702)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1150-1155 BeaconCommitteeSubscription built from duty.committees_at_slot and selection_proof.is_some()
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:158 is_aggregator uses duty.committee_length
impact: Subscriptions and aggregator selection use fields already in AttesterData; no extra BN requests.

title: Memoize genesis from beacon node
idea: Fetch genesis info once and memoize it rather than requesting it on every call.
measured_best: for 1024 keys as many as 7 requests per second, becoming 1 total (pr:prysm#13796)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:388-395 genesis fetched once at startup
validator_client/src/lib.rs:832 only get_beacon_genesis call in the VC
impact: Genesis is fetched once at startup and passed by value.

title: Hoist registry scan out of per-key status
idea: When resolving status for many pubkeys, compute the last-active-validator index once per state instead of per pubkey.
measured_best: for large operators this is a strain (no numbers) (pr:prysm#12487)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:911-1000 resolves index per unknown pubkey via get_beacon_states_validator_id
beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:210 pubkey lookups via pubkey cache
impact: The VC resolves pubkey to index per key via the BN pubkey cache; there is no last-active-validator registry scan to hoist.

title: Single-pass multi-key committee assignments
idea: Compute committee assignments for all requested keys in one pass over the epoch's committees instead of per-key scans.
measured_best: 16k validators: 182708160 ns/op, 85 MB/op; previously over 4 minutes for 8k validators (pr:prysm#4294)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:295 get_attestation_duties: O(1) shuffled_position then linear scan over committees per validator
beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:15 per-index duties from cached CommitteeCache
gap: No O(validators) scan per key (shuffled_position is O(1)), but each index scans up to 2048 committees to find its range. A binary search over compute_committee_range in CommitteeCache::get_attestation_duties would remove it.
impact: Negligible: a few thousand integer comparisons per key per epoch on the BN.

title: Avoid state copies for selection proof serving
idea: Compute active indices and seed from the shared head state rather than copying the state several times per aggregate-selection request.
measured_best: reduces 3 state copies to 1 per call (pr:prysm#5813)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/aggregate_attestation.rs:12 get_aggregate_attestation looks up the naive aggregation pool by data root, no state load or copy
Lighthouse selection proofs are signed in the validator client; the BN endpoint does not compute active indices or seed
impact: None: no per-request state copies exist on this path, and BeaconState clones are cheap (milhouse persistent tree).

title: pre-sized direct JSON encoding
idea: For large JSON responses (blobs bundle), marshal directly into one pre-sized buffer with in-place hex encoding and write the already-encoded result verbatim through the RPC handler and codec, avoiding repeated reflection marshalling and compact re-scans of the payload.
measured_best: getBlobsV3 128 blobs: 309 ms -> 29 ms (~10.6x); marshal 16,516 allocs -> 1
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/task_spawner.rs:102 warp::reply::json -> serde_json::to_vec, unsized growing Vec
~/.cargo ssz_types-0.14.1/src/serde_utils/hex_fixed_vec.rs:11 hex::encode builds String per blob
ethereum_serde_utils-0.8.1/src/hex.rs:7-12 second String via '0x' prefix copy
gap: Rust serde is typed (no reflection), so the 10x reflection cost does not exist. Remaining: each blob is hex-encoded into two temporary Strings and the output Vec is not pre-sized. A hex-into-buffer serializer in ssz_types hex_fixed_vec plus a pre-sized body in blocking_json_task would remove it.
impact: Blob/data-column JSON endpoints allocate ~2 extra copies per 128KB blob; small CPU saving on a rarely hit API, likely tens of percent on that call at most.

title: publish head before state copy
idea: Publish the selected fork-choice head (root, slot) atomically at selection time, before the state copy, and serve identity-only API endpoints from it, so public handlers need not wait ~750 ms for the memoized head state or trigger fork-choice work on a cache miss.
measured_best: block/root endpoints lagged ~750 ms behind the selected head
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1106-1160 new snapshot (get_full_block, get_advanced_hot_state, build_all_caches) built before cached_head write lock; only then is the new root visible
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:48-57 BlockId::Head root reads canonical_head.head_and_execution_status() (old snapshot, no waiting)
gap: API handlers never block on head computation (they read the previous CachedHead), but the new head root/slot is only published after the state load/advance and cache build. Publish (root, slot) atomically right after new_view is chosen in recompute_head_at_slot_internal and serve identity-only endpoints from it.
impact: Removes lag of head root/header endpoints behind fork choice; small in steady state because the post-import state is normally a state-cache hit.
refute_note: Checked the BlockId::Head path and recompute_head: no early-published head identity exists; Lighthouse avoids the waiting half of the problem (handlers read the stale snapshot) but not the lag.

title: historic committee cache from randao
idea: Serve historic committee queries by building a committee cache for the requested past epoch directly from randao mixes in a recent state, instead of replaying to a state at that epoch.
measured_best: reconstruction usually upwards of 20s, sometimes minutes
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/states.rs:~640-690 committees endpoint builds CommitteeCache::initialized(state, epoch) from the given state's randao for old epochs
beacon_node/http_api/src/caches.rs:22 HistoricalCommitteeCache LRU keyed by shuffling id
impact: Committee queries for historic epochs avoid state replay.

title: pubkey cache lookup
idea: Look up validators by pubkey through the state's pubkey-to-index cache instead of scanning the whole validator registry per query.
measured_best: queries by pubkey took 10ms+ from registry loop
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:48-64 pubkey_to_validator_index uses chain.validator_index (pubkey cache) and verifies against state
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/states.rs:780 single validator lookup uses it
beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:24-47 bulk path uses hash filter
impact: No further gain; already O(1) via validator_pubkey_cache.

title: hashset id filter
idea: Filter validators by requested ids/pubkeys using a HashSet lookup per state validator instead of scanning the input list per validator, turning O(n*m) into O(n).
measured_best: 2s to 12+s with 8k IDs before (slowdown); fix removes it
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:24-27 ids_filter_set HashSet<&ValidatorId>
beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:41-45 per-validator contains() on pubkey/index
validators.rs:95-99,143-146 same for balances and POST
impact: Already O(n) over registry with O(1) set lookups.

title: persist light client bootstrap
idea: Persist light client bootstrap parts (sync committee branch by block root, sync committee by period) so bootstrap is served without expensive computation or state queries.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:396 get_light_client_bootstrap reads stored branch and sync committee
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8374 bootstrap served without state load
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:831 light client update storage
impact: Bootstrap is served from persisted sync committee branch/committee.

title: single lock acquisition
idea: Read all needed fields from the canonical head under one lock acquisition instead of locking twice, to cut lock contention in the syncing endpoint.
measured_best: "responses were taking 4-10s on occasion"
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:589-598 head_and_execution_status takes cached_head once plus one fork choice read lock
beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2452-2455 /node/syncing uses it
impact: Already a single head read; nothing to gain.

title: server-side supply computation
idea: Add a node-side endpoint that sums balances for a state, so clients do not download and parse 68MB of JSON validator balances.
measured_best: avoids 68MB JSON download
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs, validators.rs, beacon/states.rs: grep for supply/total balance finds only validator_balances (returns full list)
no supply endpoint in http_api/src
gap: Add a non-standard route (e.g. GET /lighthouse/.../supply or beacon/states/{id}/total_balance) that sums state.balances() inside map_state_and_execution_optimistic_and_finalized and returns one number; also add it to eth2 client types.
impact: Saves a ~68MB JSON download+parse per supply query for tooling/explorers; negligible for a validating node, only benefits API consumers.

title: not-while-syncing guard on duties
idea: Reject validator duty endpoints (e.g. proposer duties) while the node is far behind head, since computing duties requires advancing state over many slots and starves sync.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:475-512 not_while_syncing_filter rejects when SyncingFinalized/SyncingHead and head is beyond sync_tolerance_epochs
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:1403 proposer duties route uses not_while_syncing_filter
impact: Proposer duties are rejected while far behind.

title: skip duties when stalled
idea: Skip proposer duty computation (expensive state advance) while sync is stalled, not only while syncing, to avoid overwhelming the work queue.
measured_best: avoids 'Work queue is full' api_request_p0 at 1024
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:509 SyncState::Stalled => Ok(()) in not_while_syncing_filter
beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2703-2706 proposer duties route uses not_while_syncing_filter
beacon_node/http_api/src/proposer_duties.rs:80-90 cache miss calls compute_and_cache_proposer_duties with no head-distance check
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:673 Stalled set when no advanced/synced peers
gap: Stalled state passes the filter, and the proposer duties handler has no own head-lag guard, so a far-behind stalled node still computes duties via state advance. Apply the head-slot-vs-tolerance check to the Stalled arm.
impact: Avoids expensive state advances and api_request_p0 work-queue overflow on a stalled far-behind node; no steady-state effect.
refute_note: Also checked the proposer_duties handler itself for a head-distance or skip guard; none exists, so the earlier verdict stands.

title: index lookup instead of full scan
idea: For validator/balance state endpoints with a requested validator set, resolve the ids to indices first and read those validators directly instead of scanning the whole registry and filtering.
measured_best: validator_balances 100 vals: 260 ms to 6 ms; 10k: 260 to 23 ms; 100k: 320 to 110 ms
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:86-125 balances endpoint scans validators().iter().zip(balances()) and filters by HashSet
beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:134-170 identities endpoint does the same full scan
beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:9-75 get_beacon_state_validators also full-scans with id filter
gap: All three list endpoints scan the whole registry even for a few ids. Resolve ids to indices (index directly, pubkey via validator_pubkey_cache / state pubkey cache) and read validators().get(i)/balances().get(i); scan only when no ids (or status-only filter).
impact: Subset requests drop from a full registry scan (~260 ms) to a few ms (6 ms for 100 vals per the PR).
refute_note: Read all of validators.rs including get_beacon_state_validators (not cited earlier): it uses the same full scan, so the verdict stands and the gap covers three endpoints.

title: light client updates without state cache
idea: Generate light client updates only from the post-state at block import, kept as small proofs, without needing historical states in the state cache.
measured_best: No numbers
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4789 cache_state_data at import from the post-state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:59 stores proofs in prev_block_cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:271 fallback loads state only on cache miss

title: guard old-slot reconstruction
